children.translated_text: An <s>Aikṣvāka</s>, equal in majesty to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, of pure conduct among the unconquerable <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: priyaḥ śaraccandra iva prajānāṃ śuddhodano nāma babhūva rājā ||
children.translated_text: a king named <s>Śuddhodana</s> became dear to his subjects like the autumn moon.

children.text: tasyendrakalpasya babhūva patnī dīptyā narendrasya samaprabhāvā
children.translated_text: His wife, equal in radiance to that Indra-like lord of men,

children.text: padmeva lakṣmīḥ pṛthivīva dhīrā māyeti nāmnānupameva māyā ||
children.translated_text: was, like <s>Lakṣmī</s> in a lotus and steadfast like the earth, <s>Māyā</s> by name, incomparable and yet free of illusion.

children.text: sārdhaṃ tayāsau vijahāra rājā nācintayadvaiśravaṇasya lakṣmīm
children.translated_text: Together with her the king took his delight, and he did not even think of the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tataśca vidyeva samādhiyuktā garbhaṃ dadhe pāpavivarjitā sā ||
children.translated_text: Then she, free from evil, conceived, like sacred knowledge joined with meditation.
Before conception, the queen of the lord of men saw in a dream one white king of elephants

children.text: svapne viśantaṃ vapurātmanaḥ sā na tannimittaṃ samavāpa tāpam ||
children.translated_text: entering her own body, and she felt no distress because of that omen.

children.text: sā tasya devapratimasya devī garbheṇa vaṃśaśriyamudvahantī
children.translated_text: That goddess-like queen, carrying in her womb the splendor of his lineage,

children.text: śramaṃ na lebhe na śucaṃ na māyāṃ gantuṃ vanaṃ sā nibhṛtaṃ cakāṅkṣa ||
children.translated_text: felt no weariness, no grief, and no delusion; <s>Māyā</s> longed to go to a secluded forest.

children.text: sā lumbinī nāma vanāntabhūmiṃ citradrumāṃ caitrarathābhirāmām
children.translated_text: She sought a woodland region named <s>Lumbinī</s>, with varied trees and delightful like <s>Caitraratha</s>,

children.text: dhyānānukūlāṃ vijanāmiyeṣa tasyāṃ nivāsāya nṛpaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: suited to meditation and solitary; she spoke to the king about dwelling there.

children.text: aryāśayāṃ tāṃ pravaṇāṃ ca dharme vijñāya kautūhalaharṣapūrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing her noble disposition and her inclination toward <s>dharma</s> (righteous practice), and filled with curiosity and joy,

children.text: śivāt purād bhūmipatirjagāma tatprītaye nāpi vihārahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth went from the auspicious city for her pleasure, not for the sake of recreation.
In that lovely grove, the king's wife, watching for the time of childbirth,
approached a couch furnished with an awning, while she was greeted by thousands of women.

children.text: tataḥ prasannaśca babhūva puṣyastasyāśca devyā vratasaṃskṛtāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the asterism <s>Puṣya</s> became favorable; and from that queen, consecrated by vows,

children.text: pārśvātsuto lokahitāya jajñe nirvedanaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: a son was born from her side for the welfare of the world, without pain and without illness.
As <s>Aurva</s> was born from the thigh, <s>Pṛthu</s> from the hand, and <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, like <s>Indra</s>, from the head,
and <s>Kakṣīvat</s> from the region of the upper arm, so too was his birth of that kind.

children.text: krameṇa garbhādabhiniḥsṛtaḥ san babhau cyutaḥ khādiva yonyajātaḥ
children.translated_text: Though he came forth in due order from the womb, he shone as if fallen from the sky, not born from a womb;

children.text: kalpeṣvanekeṣu ca bhāvitātmā yaḥ samprajānan suṣuve na mūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for through many aeons he had cultivated himself, and he was born fully conscious, not bewildered.

children.text: dīptyā ca dhairyeṇa ca yo rarāja bālo ravibhūmimivāvatīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: That child shone with radiance and steadfastness like the sun descended to the earth,

children.text: tathātidīpto 'pi nirīkṣyamāṇo jahāra cakṣūṃṣi yathā śaśāṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and yet, though exceedingly bright, when looked upon he captivated the eyes like the moon.
By the blazing radiance of his own body he robbed the lamp's light, as the sun does;
lovely in color like precious <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, he illuminated all the directions.
Unconfused, uplifted, and spread out, with strides extended as though not pressing down,

children.text: tathaiva dhīrāṇi padāni sapta saptarṣitārāsadṛśo jagāma ||
children.translated_text: he likewise took seven firm steps, like the stars of the Seven Seers.
"I have been born for awakening, for the welfare of the world; this is my final arising into existence."
Looking to the four directions with a lion's gait, he spoke words that would bring auspicious meaning.

children.text: khāt prasrute candramarīciśubhre dve vāridhāre śiśiroṣṇavīrye
children.translated_text: From the sky streamed two currents of water, white as moonbeams, one cool in power and one warm,
and they fell on his gentle head, bringing pleasure through their touch upon his body.
As he lay on a bed beneath a splendid canopy, with golden-bright limbs and beryl feet,
lords of <s>yakṣas</s>, holding golden lotuses in their hands, stood around him because of his majesty.

children.text: adṛśyabhāvāśca divaukasaḥ khe yasya prabhāvātpraṇataiḥ śirobhiḥ
children.translated_text: Invisible gods in the sky, through his power, bowed their heads
and held a white parasol over him, chanting supreme blessings for awakening.
Great serpents, thirsting for the special <s>dharma</s> and having earned merit with past Buddhas,
fanned him with eyes marked by devotion and scattered <s>mandāra</s> flowers over him.
The pure beings of the <s>Śuddhādhivāsa</s> heavens, pleased by the virtue of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s arising,

children.text: devā nanandurvigate 'pi rāge magnasya duḥkhe jagato hitāya ||
children.translated_text: rejoiced, though their passion had passed away, for the welfare of the world sunk in suffering.

children.text: yasya prasūtau girirājakīlā vātāhatā nauriva bhūścacāla
children.translated_text: At his birth the earth, whose pegs are the kingly mountains, shook like a boat struck by wind,
and from a cloudless sky fell rain containing sandalwood, blue lotuses, and lotuses.

children.text: vātā vavuḥ sparśasukhā manojñā divyāni vāsāṃsyavapātayantaḥ
children.translated_text: Winds blew, pleasing to the touch, dropping divine garments;

children.text: sūryaḥ sa evābhyadhikaṃ cakāśe jajvāla saumyārcir anīrito 'gniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sun itself shone more brightly, and fire blazed with a gentle flame though unfanned.
In the northeastern part of the dwelling area, a well with white water appeared by itself;
there the amazed women of the inner palace performed rites as at a sacred bathing place.
The grove was filled with divine hosts of beings seeking <s>dharma</s>, eager to see him,
and, from sheer wonder, they made flowers fall from the trees even out of season.

children.text: bhūtairasaumyaiḥ parityaktahiṃsairnākāri pīḍā svagaṇe pare vā
children.translated_text: Fierce beings abandoned violence and caused no harm to their own groups or to others;

children.text: loke hi sarvāśca vinā prayāsaṃ rujo narāṇāṃ śamayāṃbabhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed, throughout the world all the diseases of human beings were calmed without effort.

children.text: kalaṃ praṇeduḥ mṛgapakṣiṇaśca śāntāmbuvāhāḥ sarito babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: Deer and birds uttered sweet sounds, and the rivers became calm in their waters;

children.text: diśaḥ prasedurvimale nirabhre vihāyase dundubhayo nineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: the directions grew clear, and in the spotless, cloudless sky heavenly drums resounded.

children.text: lokasya mokṣāya gurau prasūte śamaṃ prapede jagadavyavastham
children.translated_text: When the great teacher was born for the liberation of the world, the disordered world attained peace;

children.text: prāpyeva nāthaṃ khalu nītimantam eko na māro mudamāpa loke ||
children.translated_text: as if it had obtained a wise protector, only <s>Māra</s> in the world did not rejoice.

children.text: divyādbhutaṃ janma nirīkṣya tasya dhīro 'pi rājā bahukṣobhametaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his divine and wondrous birth, even the steadfast king fell into great agitation;

children.text: snehādasau bhītipramodajanye dve vāridhāre mumuce narendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: from affection, the lord of men shed two streams of tears born of fear and joy.

children.text: amānuṣīṃ tasya niśamya śaktiṃ mātā prakṛtyā karuṇārdracittā
children.translated_text: When his mother heard of his superhuman power, being by nature tender-hearted with compassion,

children.text: prītā ca bhītā ca babhūva devī śītoṣṇamiśreva jalasya dhārā ||
children.translated_text: The queen became both delighted and afraid, like a stream of water mixed with cold and heat.

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā bhayahetumeva dhyātuṃ na śekuḥ vanitāḥ pravṛddhāḥ
children.translated_text: The mature women, seeing precisely the cause of fear, were unable to reflect calmly.

children.text: pūtāśca tā maṅgalakarma cakruḥ śivaṃ yayācuḥ śiśave suraughān ||
children.translated_text: Purified, they performed auspicious rites and begged the hosts of gods for welfare for the child.

children.text: viprāśca khyātāḥ śrutaśīlavāgbhiḥ śrutvā nimittāni vicārya samyak
children.translated_text: Famous Brahmins, renowned for learning, conduct, and speech, heard the signs and considered them properly.

children.text: mukhaiḥ praphullaiścakitaiśca dīptaiḥ bhītaprasannaṃ nṛpametya procuḥ ||
children.translated_text: With faces blossoming, startled, and radiant, they came to the king, who was both frightened and pleased, and spoke.

children.text: śamepsavo ye bhuvi santi sattvāḥ putraṃ vinecchanti guṇaṃ na kaṃcit
children.translated_text: Those beings on earth who desire peace wish for no excellence apart from a son.

children.text: tvatputra eṣo 'sti kulapradīpaḥ nṛtyotsavaṃ tvadya vidhehi rājan ||
children.translated_text: This son of yours is the lamp of the family; today, O king, hold a festival of dancing.

children.text: vihāya cintāṃ bhava śāntacitto modasva vaṃśastava vṛddhibhāgī
children.translated_text: Cast off anxiety and become calm in mind; rejoice, for your lineage is destined to increase.

children.text: lokasya netā tava putrabhūtaḥ duḥkhārditānāṃ bhuvi eṣa trātā ||
children.translated_text: Born as your son, he is the guide of the world; on earth he is the rescuer of those afflicted by suffering.
He shines like a lamp, his limbs gleaming like gold, and he is endowed with all these excellent marks.

children.text: nidhirguṇānāṃ samaye sa gatāṃ buddharṣibhāvaṃ paramāṃ śriyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: A treasury of virtues, in due time he will attain the state of a <s>buddha</s>-seer, or else supreme majesty.

children.text: icchedasau vai pṛthivīśriyaṃ cet nyāyena jitvā pṛthivīṃ samagrām
children.translated_text: If he should desire the splendor of the earth, then, having conquered the whole earth by justice,

children.text: bhūpeṣu rājeta yathā prakāśaḥ graheṣu sarveṣu ravervibhāti ||
children.translated_text: he would reign among kings as the sun shines in brilliance among all the planets.

children.text: mokṣāya cedvā vanameva gacchet tattvena samyak sa vijitya sarvān
children.translated_text: Or if he should go to the forest for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), after rightly conquering all doctrines by truth,

children.text: matān pṛthivyāṃ bahumānametaḥ rājeta śaileṣu yathā sumeruḥ ||
children.translated_text: he would gain great honor on earth and reign as <s>Sumeru</s> does among mountains.

children.text: yathā hiraṇyaṃ śuci dhātumadhye merurgirīṇāṃ sarasāṃ samudraḥ
children.translated_text: As gold is pure among metals, <s>Meru</s> among mountains, and the ocean among lakes,

children.text: tārāsu candrastapatāṃ ca sūryaḥ putrastathā te dvipadeṣu varyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the moon is foremost among stars and the sun among things that heat, so your son is best among bipeds.

children.text: tasyākṣiṇī nirnimiṣe viśāle snigdhe ca dīpte vimale tathaiva
children.translated_text: His eyes are wide and unblinking, moist, radiant, and likewise spotless.
With steady black pupils, long pure lashes, they are truly able to see all realities.

children.text: kasmānnu hetoḥ kathitānbhavadbhiḥ varānguṇān dhārayate kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason does the prince bear the excellent qualities described by you,

children.text: prāpurna pūrve munayo nṛpāśca rājñeti pṛṣṭā jagadur dvijāstam ||
children.translated_text: qualities that earlier sages and kings did not attain? Asked thus by the king, the twice-born men answered him.

children.text: khyātāni karmāṇi yaśo matiśca pūrva na bhūtāni bhavanti paścāt
children.translated_text: Famous deeds, glory, and intelligence, though not present before, come into being later.

children.text: guṇā hi sarvāḥ prabhavanti hetoḥ nidarśanānyatra ca no nibodha ||
children.translated_text: For all virtues arise from a cause; hear examples of this from us.

children.text: yadrājaśāstraṃ bhṛguraṅgirā vā na cakratur vaṃśakarāvṛṣī tau
children.translated_text: That science of kingship which neither <s>Bhṛgu</s> nor <s>Aṅgiras</s>, those lineage-founding sages, composed,

children.text: tayoḥ sutau saumya sasarjatus tatkālena śukraśca bṛhaspatiśca ||
children.translated_text: their two sons, <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, in time created, O gentle one.

children.text: sārasvataścāpi jagāda naṣṭaṃ vedaṃ punaryaṃ dadṛśurna pūrve
children.translated_text: And <s>Sārasvata</s> proclaimed again the lost <s>Veda</s>, which earlier men had not seen.

children.text: vyāsastathainaṃ bahudhā cakāra na yaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ kṛtavānaśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Vyāsa</s> arranged it in many divisions, which <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, being unable, had not done.

children.text: vālmīkirādau ca sasarja padyaṃ jagrantha yanna cyavano maharṣiḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Vālmīki</s> first created poetry, which the great sage <s>Cyavana</s> had not composed.

children.text: cikitsitaṃ yacca cakāra nātriḥ paścāttadātreya ṛṣirjagāda ||
children.translated_text: The healing science that <s>Atri</s> did not formulate was afterward taught by the sage <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: yacca dvijatvaṃ kuśiko na lebhe tadgādhinaḥ sūnur avāpa rājan
children.translated_text: The brahminhood that <s>Kuśika</s> did not obtain was obtained by the son of <s>Gādhin</s>, O king.

children.text: velāṃ samudre sagaraśca dadhre nekṣvākavo yāṃ prathamaṃ babandhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Sagara</s> set a boundary in the ocean which the first <s>Ikṣvākus</s> had not established.
In the discipline of yoga, <s>Janaka</s> reached the status of teacher for Brahmins, unattained by others.

children.text: khyātāni karmāṇi ca yāni śaureḥ śūrādayasteṣvabalā babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the famous deeds of <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Śūra</s> and the others proved weak.

children.text: tasmātpramāṇaṃ na vayo na vaṃśaḥ kaścitkvacicchraiṣṭhyamupaiti loke
children.translated_text: Therefore age is not the measure, nor lineage; someone, somewhere, attains supremacy in the world.

children.text: rājñāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca hi tāni tāni kṛtāni putrairakṛtāni pūrvaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For among kings and sages, such deeds have been done by sons, though they were not done by their forefathers.

children.text: evaṃ nṛpaḥ pratyayitair dvijais tair āśvāsitaścāpyabhinanditaśca
children.translated_text: Thus reassured and congratulated by those trustworthy twice-born men, the king
cast the inauspicious doubt from his mind and rose to still greater joy.

children.text: prītaśca tebhyo dvijasattamebhyaḥ satkārapūrvaṃ pradadau dhanāni
children.translated_text: Pleased, he gave wealth to those best of Brahmins, with due honor beforehand,
saying, May he become ruler of the earth as you have said, and, having reached old age, may he go to the forests.

children.text: atho nimittaiśca tapobalācca tajjanma janmāntakarasya buddhvā
children.translated_text: Then, from the signs and from the power of his austerity, he understood that this was the birth of the one who would end rebirth.
Out of thirst for the true <s>dharma</s> (teaching), the great sage <s>Asita</s> came to the dwelling of the <s>Śākya</s> lord.

children.text: taṃ brahmavid brahmavidaṃ jvalantaṃ brāhmyā śriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca
children.translated_text: Him, a knower of <s>brahman</s> blazing with brahmanic splendor and the splendor of austerity,
the king's guru led into the royal palace with reverence and respectful rites.
He, thrilled by the joy caused by the prince's birth, approached the royal inner apartments.
Self-possessed, he entered as though they were a forest, because of the excellence of his austerity and his reliance on old age.

children.text: tato nṛpastaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pādyārghyapūrvaṃ pratipūjya samyak
children.translated_text: Then the king properly honored the seated sage, first with water for the feet and an offering of welcome.

children.text: nimantrayāmāsa yathopacāraṃ purā vasiṣṭhaṃ sa ivāntidevaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He invited him according to protocol, just as <s>Antideva</s> once invited <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
I am blessed; this family of mine is worthy of favor, since the reverend one has come wishing to see me.

children.text: ājñāpyatāṃ kiṃ karavāṇi saumya śiṣyo 'smi viśrambhitum arhasīti ||
children.translated_text: Command me: what shall I do, gentle sir? I am your pupil; you may place confidence in me.
Thus properly invited by the king with his whole being,
the sage, his wide eyes opened in wonder, spoke words deep and calm.

children.text: mahātmani tvayyupapannam etat priyātithau tyāgini dharmakāme
children.translated_text: This is fitting in you, great-souled one, to whom guests are dear, generous, and desirous of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: sattvānvayajñānavayo'nurūpā snigdhā yadevaṃ mayi te matiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For your disposition toward me should indeed be so affectionate, in keeping with your character, lineage, knowledge, and age.

children.text: etacca tadyena nṛparṣayaste dharmeṇa sūkṣmeṇa dhanānyavāpya
children.translated_text: And this is that subtle <s>dharma</s> by which your royal seers, after obtaining wealth,
constantly gave it away according to rule and became rich in austerities, though poor in possessions.

children.text: prayojanaṃ yattu mamopayāne tanme śṛṇu prītimupehi ca tvam
children.translated_text: But as for the purpose of my coming, hear that from me, and take joy.
On the path of the sun I heard a divine voice: 'Your son has been born for awakening.'

children.text: śrutvā vacastacca manaśca yuktvā jñātvā nimittaiśca tato 'smyupetaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that utterance, applying my mind, and then knowing it by signs, I have come
with the desire to see the banner of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, raised high like the banner of <s>Śakra</s>.
When the lord of men heard this speech in this way, his movement was bewildered by delight.
Taking the prince from the nurse's lap, he showed him to the ascetic rich in austerity.
Then the great seer saw the king's son, whose feet bore wheel-marks and whose fingers and toes were joined by a web,
with an ūrṇā between his brows and his organ sheathed like an elephant's; he looked upon the prince with wonder.
Seeing him resting in the nurse's lap, like <s>Agni</s>'s son resting in a goddess's lap,
he became tearful, the tears trembling at the ends of his eyelashes; sighing, he turned his face toward heaven.
But when the king saw <s>Asita</s> with eyes flooded by tears, he trembled from affection for his child.
With a faltering voice and a throat roughened by tears, he asked, hands folded and body bent low:

children.text: alpāntaraṃ yasya vapuḥ surebhyo bahvadbhutaṃ yasya ca janma dīptam
children.translated_text: 'His form is only slightly inferior to that of the gods; his radiant birth is exceedingly wondrous.

children.text: yasyottamaṃ bhāvinamāttha cārthaṃ taṃ prekṣya kasmāttava dhīra bāṣpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You have declared the highest future aim for him. Seeing him, why do you weep, steadfast one?

children.text: api sthirāyurbhagavan kumāraḥ kaccinna śokāya mama prasūtaḥ
children.translated_text: Is the prince surely of firm life, blessed sir? I hope he has not been born for my sorrow.

children.text: labdhaḥ kathaṃcitsalilāñjalirme na khalvimaṃ pātumupaiti kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This handful of water was somehow obtained by me; surely Time has not come to drink it away.

children.text: apyakṣayaṃ me yaśaso nidhānaṃ kacciddhruvo me kulahastasāraḥ
children.translated_text: I hope the store of my fame is imperishable. I hope the firm essence of my family is held in my hand.

children.text: api prayāsyāmi sukhaṃ paratra supto 'pi putre 'nimiṣaikacakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: May I go happily to the next world, even sleeping, with my one unblinking eye in my son.
I hope the tender shoot of my family, born but not yet blossomed, is not destined to wither.

children.text: kṣipraṃ vibho brūhi na me 'sti śāntiḥ snehaṃ sute vetsi hi bāndhavānām ||
children.translated_text: Speak quickly, lord; I have no peace, for you know the affection of kinsmen toward a son.'
Recognizing the king, whose thought had rushed toward fear of misfortune in this surge of feeling,

children.text: mā bhūnmatiste nṛpa kācidanyā niḥsaṃśayaṃ tadyadavocamasmi ||
children.translated_text: the sage said: 'Let no other idea arise in you, O king; it is certainly just as I have said.

children.text: nāsyānyathātvaṃ prati vikriyā me svāṃ vañcanāṃ tu prati viklavo 'smi
children.translated_text: My agitation is not because his future will be otherwise; I am distressed rather over my own deprivation.

children.text: kālo hi me yātumayaṃ ca jāto jātikṣayasyāsulabhasya boddhā ||
children.translated_text: For my time to depart has come, while he has been born as the knower of the rare destruction of birth.

children.text: vihāya rājyaṃ viṣayeṣvanāsthas tīvraiḥ prayatnairadhigamya tattvam
children.translated_text: Having abandoned kingship and become indifferent to sense-objects, having attained truth by intense efforts,

children.text: jagatyayaṃ mohatamo nihantuṃ jvaliṣyati jñānamayo hi sūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this sun made of knowledge will blaze in the world to destroy the darkness of delusion.
From the ocean of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), with foam scattered by sickness, with waves of old age and a fierce current of death,
he will carry across the afflicted world, swept along there, by the great raft of knowledge.
The world of living beings, tormented by thirst, will drink his supreme river of <s>dharma</s> (teaching),

children.text: asyottamāṃ dharmanadīṃ pravṛttāṃ tṛṣṇārditaḥ pāsyati jīvalokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: set flowing with wisdom as its water, firm conduct as its banks, cool with meditation, and vow-birds upon it.
For those afflicted by suffering, enclosed by sense-objects, and standing on the road through the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (rebirth),
he will teach the path of liberation, as one teaches the way to travelers who have lost the road.
For people in the world being burned by the fire of passion, with sense-objects as its fuel,

children.text: prahlādam ādhāsyati dharmavṛṣṭyā vṛṣṭyā mahāmegha ivātapānte ||
children.translated_text: he will bring cool relief by a rain of <s>dharma</s>, like a great cloud raining at the end of the hot season.
The door of escape for beings, barred by craving and panelled with the darkness of delusion,
he will split open with the supreme, irresistible blow of the true <s>dharma</s>.
Having awakened, this king of <s>dharma</s> will bring release from bondage

children.text: lokasya saṃbudhya ca dharmarājaḥ kariṣyate bandhanamokṣameṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the world wrapped in its own snares of delusion, overcome by suffering, and without refuge.

children.text: tanmā kṛthāḥ śokamimaṃ prati tvamasminsa śocyo 'sti manuṣyaloke
children.translated_text: Therefore do not make this sorrow concerning him. In the human world there is one who should be mourned:

children.text: mohena vā kāmasukhairmadādvā yo naiṣṭhikaṃ śroṣyati nāsya dharmam ||
children.translated_text: whoever, through delusion or through pride in the pleasures of desire, will not hear this one's definitive <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: bhraṣṭasya tasmācca guṇādato me dhyānāni labdhvāpy akṛtārthataiva
children.translated_text: Because I have fallen away from that excellence, even though I have obtained meditations, my purpose remains unfulfilled.

children.text: dharmasya tasyāśravaṇādahaṃ hi manye vipattiṃ tridive 'pi vāsam ||
children.translated_text: For, because I shall not hear that <s>dharma</s>, I consider even dwelling in heaven to be a misfortune.'

children.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sasuhṛt sadārastyaktvā viṣādaṃ mumude narendraḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this meaning, the king, together with his friends and wife, abandoned dejection and rejoiced.

children.text: evaṃvidho 'yaṃ tanayo mameti mene sa hi svāmapi sāravattām ||
children.translated_text: 'Such is this son of mine,' he thought, and he considered even himself to possess true worth.

children.text: ārṣeṇa mārgeṇa tu yāsyatīti cintāvidheyaṃ hṛdayaṃ cakāra
children.translated_text: Yet, thinking, 'He will go by the path of the seers,' he made his heart subject to anxiety.

children.text: na khalvasau na priyadharmapakṣaḥ saṃtānanāśāttu bhayaṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: It was not that he did not favor the beloved <s>dharma</s>; rather, he saw fear in the destruction of his line.

children.text: atha munirasito nivedya tattvaṃ sutaniyataṃ sutaviklavāya rājñe
children.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Asita</s>, having declared the truth about the son's fixed destiny to the king distressed over his son,
his form gazed upon with great honor, went away by the path of the wind, just as he had come.

children.text: kṛtamitir anujāsutaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā munivacanaśravaṇe ca tanmatau ca
children.translated_text: Having made his decision, and having seen his younger sister's son, whose mind was set on hearing the sage's words,
that holy man, out of compassion, instructed him in many ways as if he were a beloved son.
The king too, delighted at the birth of his son, released the prisoners throughout his realm.

children.text: kulasadṛśam acīkarad yathāvat priyatanayas tanayasya jātakarma ||
children.translated_text: Fittingly and in a manner worthy of his family, he performed the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite) for his dear son.

children.text: daśasu pariṇateṣvahaḥsu caiva prayatamanāḥ parayā mudā parītaḥ
children.translated_text: And when ten days had passed, with purified mind and filled with supreme joy,
he performed <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire offering), auspicious rites, and worship of deities for his son's highest welfare.
Moreover, cows numbering a full hundred thousand, with strong and sturdy calves and with golden horns,
not touched by old age and rich in milk, he himself gave to the twice-born for his son's increase.
Then, self-controlled, after performing rites of many kinds that delighted his own heart,

children.text: guṇavati niyate śive muhūrte matimakaronmuditaḥ purapraveśe ||
children.translated_text: at a fixed, favorable, auspicious moment he joyfully set his mind on entering the city.
Then a very costly palanquin made of elephant ivory, bearing white and dark flowers and jewel-lamps,

children.text: abhajata śibikāṃ śivāya devī tanayavatī praṇipatya devatābhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the queen, blessed with a son, entered for good fortune after bowing to the deities.
Then, after sending his wife into the city first, attended by elders and with her child as her guardian,

children.text: nṛpatirapi jagāma paurasaṃghair divam amarair maghavān ivārcyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king too went, honored by gatherings of citizens like <s>Maghavan</s> by the immortals in heaven.

children.text: bhavanamatha vigāhya śākyarājo bhava iva ṣaṇmukhajanmanā pratītaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Śākya</s> king entered the palace, delighted like <s>Bhava</s> at the birth of <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>;
his face full of joy, saying, "this, and this," he arranged many things that would bring prosperity and fame.

children.text: iti narapatiputrajanmavṛddhyā sajanapadaṃ kapilāhvayaṃ puraṃ tat
children.translated_text: Thus, through the increase brought by the king's son's birth, that city called <s>Kapila</s>, together with its countryside,
became joyful, like the city of <s>Dhanada</s> strewn with apsarases at the birth of <s>Nalakūbara</s>.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye bhagavatprasūtir nāma prathamaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the first canto, called <s>Bhagavatprasūti</s> (The Birth of the Blessed One), is completed.

children.text: ā janmano janmajarāntakasya tasyātmajasyātmajitaḥ sa rājā
children.translated_text: From the birth of that self-conquered son, who would bring birth and old age to an end, that king
grew day by day in wealth, elephants, horses, and allies, like the ocean by rushing waters.

children.text: dhanasya ratnasya ca tasya tasya kṛtākṛtasyaiva ca kāñcanasya
children.translated_text: For wealth, jewels, and every sort of gold, both worked and unworked,

children.text: tadā hi naikānsa nidhīnavāpa manorathasyāpy atibhārabhūtān ||
children.translated_text: at that time he obtained not one but many treasures, burdensome even for desire itself.

children.text: ye padmakalpairapi ca dvipendrairna maṇḍalaṃ śakyamihābhinetum
children.translated_text: Those whom even lordly elephants, lotus-like in strength, could not easily lead in formation here,
those Himalayan elephants, fierce with rut, came to him even without effort.
With horses marked by many signs, adorned with fresh golden trappings, long-maned, and others as well,

children.text: saṃcukṣubhe cāsya puraṃ turaṅgairbalena maitryā ca dhanena cāptaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: his city surged with horses acquired by strength, by alliance, and by wealth.

children.text: puṣṭāśca tuṣṭāśca tathāsya rājye sādhvyo 'rajaskā guṇavatpayaskāḥ
children.translated_text: And in his kingdom the cows were well nourished and content, gentle, free from blemish, and rich in good milk;

children.text: udagravatsaiḥ sahitā babhūvurbahvyo bahukṣīraduhaś ca gāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: many cows, with thriving calves, gave abundant milk.

children.text: madhyasthatāṃ tasya ripurjagāma madhyasthabhāvaḥ prayayau suhṛttvam
children.translated_text: His enemy became neutral; the neutral party passed into friendship;

children.text: viśeṣato dārḍhyamiyāya mitraṃ dvāvasya pakṣāvaparastu nāsa ||
children.translated_text: his friend grew especially firm, so he had supporting sides and no opposing one.
So too, with cloud-sound joined to a gentle wind and clouds adorned by lightning like earrings,

children.text: vināśmavarṣāśanipātadoṣaiḥ kāle ca deśe pravavarṣa devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rain fell at the proper time and place, without the faults of hailstorms or thunderbolt-strikes.
The grain grew fruitful in season, even with the ordinary labor of cultivation,

children.text: tā eva cāsyauṣadhayo rasena sāreṇa caivābhyadhikā babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those very herbs became richer in sap and in substance.
Even when the time that puts the body in doubt came on, like the crush of battle,

children.text: svasthāḥ sukhaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca prajajñire kālavaśena nāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: women gave birth at the proper time, healthy, easily, and without illness.

children.text: pṛthagvratibhyo vibhave 'pi garhye na prārthayanti sma narāḥ parebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when their prosperity was meager, men did not ask from others whose vows differed from theirs;

children.text: abhyarthitaḥ sūkṣmadhano 'pi cāryastadā na kaścidvimukho babhūva ||
children.translated_text: and when requested, no noble man, even if his wealth was slight, turned away.

children.text: nāgauravo bandhuṣu nāpyadātā naivāvrato nānṛtiko na hiṃsraḥ
children.translated_text: At that time in his kingdom no one was disrespectful to kinsmen, ungenerous, vowless, false, or violent,

children.text: āsīttadā kaścana tasya rājye rājño yayāteriva nāhuṣasya ||
children.translated_text: as in the realm of King <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
For gardens, temples, hermitages, wells, water-stations, lotus ponds, and groves,

children.text: cakruḥ kriyāstatra ca dharmakāmāḥ pratyakṣataḥ svargam ivopalabhya ||
children.translated_text: those who loved <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) performed works there, as if seeing heaven directly.

children.text: muktaśca durbhikṣabhayāmayebhyo hṛṣṭo janaḥ svarga ivābhireme
children.translated_text: Freed from famine, fear, and disease, the delighted people rejoiced as if in heaven;

children.text: patnīṃ patirvā mahiṣī patiṃ vā parasparaṃ na vyabhiceratuśca ||
children.translated_text: husband did not betray wife, nor wife her husband; they did not transgress against one another.

children.text: kaścitsiṣeve rataye na kāmaṃ kāmārthamarthaṃ na jugopa kaścit
children.translated_text: No one pursued <s>kāma</s> (desire) merely for pleasure; no one guarded wealth for the sake of desire;

children.text: kaściddhanārthaṃ na cacāra dharmaṃ dharmāya kaścinna cakāra hiṃsām ||
children.translated_text: no one practiced <s>dharma</s> for the sake of wealth, and no one committed injury for the sake of dharma.
With theft and other such troubles, and enemies too, destroyed, its own forces at peace and freed from hostile armies,

children.text: kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca babhūva tasya purānaraṇyasya yathaiva rāṣṭre ||
children.translated_text: his realm, in city and wild land alike, was secure and well supplied with food.

children.text: tadā hi tajjanmani tasya rājño manorivādityasutasya rājye
children.translated_text: For at that birth, in the kingdom of that king, as in the realm of <s>Manu</s>, son of <s>Āditya</s>,

children.text: cacāra harṣaḥ praṇanāśa pāpmā jajvāla dharmaḥ kaluṣaḥ śaśāma ||
children.translated_text: joy moved abroad, evil vanished, <s>dharma</s> blazed up, and impurity grew calm.
Since prosperity of this kind came to the royal house, and every purpose was fulfilled,

children.text: tato nṛpastasya sutasya nāma sarvārthasiddho 'yamiti pracakre ||
children.translated_text: the king therefore proclaimed his son's name: "This one is <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, Accomplisher of Every Aim."

children.text: devī tu māyā vibudharṣikalpaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśālaṃ tanayaprabhāvam
children.translated_text: But Queen <s>Māyā</s>, seeing the vast power of her son, who was like a divine sage,

children.text: jātaṃ praharṣaṃ na śaśāka soḍhuṃ tato nivāsāya divaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: could not bear the joy that had arisen; therefore she went to heaven to dwell.

children.text: tataḥ kumāraṃ suragarbhakalpaṃ snehena bhāvena ca nirviśeṣam
children.translated_text: Then, toward the prince, who was like a divine child, with affection and feeling no different,
his mother's sister, equal in splendor to his mother, came to raise him as though he were her own son.

children.text: tataḥ sa bālārka ivodayasthaḥ samīrito vahnir ivānilena
children.translated_text: Then, like the young sun standing at its rising and like fire fanned by the wind,
the prince grew rightly, step by step, like the moon, lord of stars, in a bright fortnight.

children.text: tato mahārhāṇi ca candanāni ratnāvalīścauṣadhibhiḥ sagarbhāḥ
children.translated_text: Then costly sandalwoods, strings of jewels containing protective herbs,
and golden little carriages drawn by deer were brought for him from the homes of friends.
Also ornaments suited to his age, golden elephants, deer, and horses,
chariots yoked with young calves, and little figures variegated with gold and silver,
thus he was attended with these various enjoyments of the senses, each suited to his age,

children.text: bālo 'pyabālapratimo babhūva dhṛtyā ca śaucena dhiyā śriyā ca ||
children.translated_text: Though a child, he became unlike a child in firmness, purity, intelligence, and splendor.

children.text: vayaśca kaumāramatītya samyak samprāpya kāle pratipattikarma
children.translated_text: And when he had properly passed beyond childhood and, in due season, reached the rite of instruction,

children.text: alpair ahobhir bahuvarṣagamyā jagrāha vidyāḥ svakulānurūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in a few days he mastered the sciences suited to his family, though they normally require many years to attain.

children.text: naiḥśreyasaṃ tasya tu bhavyamarthaṃ śrutvā purastādasitānmaharṣeḥ
children.translated_text: But after hearing beforehand from the great sage <s>Asita</s> that his highest destiny was spiritual welfare,

children.text: kāmeṣu saṅgaṃ janayāṃbabhūva vanāni yāyāditi śākyarājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Śākya</s> king fostered attachment to pleasures in him, thinking, 'He may go to the forests.'
Then, from a family endowed with firm character, he brought for him a virtuous woman, endowed with beauty, modesty, and discipline,
<s>Yaśodharā</s> by name, vast in fame, also called <s>Vāmā</s>, a very embodiment of fortune.
Shining with surpassing beauty, the prince, resembling <s>Sanatkumāra</s>,

children.text: sārdhaṃ tayā śākyanarendravadhvā śacyā sahasrākṣa ivābhireme ||
children.translated_text: delighted with that bride of the <s>Śākya</s> prince, as <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> delights with <s>Śacī</s>.

children.text: kiṃcinmanaḥkṣobhakaraṃ pratīpaṃ kathaṃ na paśyediti so 'nucintya
children.translated_text: Reflecting, 'How might he not see anything adverse, anything that could disturb his mind?',

children.text: vāsaṃ nṛpo vyādiśati sma tasmai harmyodareṣveva na bhūpracāram ||
children.translated_text: the king ordered him to dwell only within palace interiors, with no roaming on the ground outside.
Then, in palaces white as autumn clouds and adorned on the earth like celestial mansions,
in mansions that sheltered every season's comfort, he passed his time with the noble music of women.
For with drums bound in gold and struck by the tips of women's hands,
and with dances equal to those of the finest apsarases, that palace shone like <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: vāgbhiḥ kalābhir lalitaiśca hāvairmadaiḥ sakhelairmadhuraiśca hāsaiḥ
children.translated_text: There the women entertained him with artful words, graceful gestures, playful intoxications, and sweet laughter,

children.text: taṃ tatra nāryo ramayāṃbabhūvur bhūvañcitair ardhanirīkṣitaiśca ||
children.translated_text: and also with bends of the brows and half-sidelong glances.
Then, seized by women skilled in the realm of desire and bold in love-play,
he did not go down from the palace terrace to the earth, like a meritorious man from the height of a celestial mansion.
The king, however, for the sake of that son's growth and urged on by what was to come,

children.text: śame 'bhireme virarāma pāpādbheje damaṃ saṃvibabhāja sādhūn ||
children.translated_text: delighted in peace, abstained from evil, practiced restraint, and shared his wealth with the good.

children.text: nādhīravatkāmasukhe sasañje na saṃrarañje viṣamaṃ jananyām
children.translated_text: He did not cling to the pleasures of desire like an unsteady man, nor did he become unevenly attached to the mother,
and with firmness he conquered the restless horses of the senses; with his virtues he won over kinsmen and citizens.

children.text: nādhyaiṣṭa duḥkhāya parasya vidyāṃ jñānaṃ śivaṃ yattu tadadhyagīṣṭa
children.translated_text: He did not study knowledge for the suffering of another; whatever knowledge was auspicious, that he learned.

children.text: svābhyaḥ prajābhyo hi yathā tathaiva sarvaprajābhyaḥ śivamāśaśaṃse ||
children.translated_text: For he wished welfare for all subjects just as he did for his own subjects.

children.text: bhaṃ bhāsuraṃ cāṅgirasādhidevaṃ yathāvadānarca tadāyuṣe saḥ
children.translated_text: For that son's long life he duly worshipped the bright, radiant deity of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>,

children.text: juhāva havyānyakṛśe kṛśānau dadau dvijebhyaḥ kṛśanaṃ ca gāśca ||
children.translated_text: offered oblations in the abundant fire, and gave gold and cows to the twice-born.

children.text: sasnau śarīraṃ pavituṃ manaśca tīrthāmbubhiścaiva guṇāmbubhiśca
children.translated_text: He bathed his body and his mind for purity, both with waters from sacred fords and with waters of virtue,

children.text: vedopadiṣṭaṃ samamātmajaṃ ca somaṃ papau śāntisukhaṃ ca hārdam ||
children.translated_text: and he drank the <s>Soma</s> prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>, as well as the heart's peaceful joy born from his son.

children.text: sāntvaṃ babhāṣe na ca nārthavadyajjajalpa tattvaṃ na ca vipriyaṃ yat
children.translated_text: He spoke conciliatory words and did not prattle what lacked meaning; he spoke truth, and not what was unpleasant.

children.text: sāntvaṃ hyatattvaṃ paruṣaṃ ca tattvaṃ hriyāśakannātmana eva vaktum ||
children.translated_text: For, out of modesty, he could not bring himself to utter either conciliatory falsehood or harsh truth.

children.text: iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭeṣu ca kāryavatsu na rāgadoṣāśrayatāṃ prapede
children.translated_text: In matters to be done, whether desired or undesired, he did not fall into dependence on passion and hatred.

children.text: śivaṃ siṣeve vyavahāraśuddhaṃ yajñaṃ hi mene na tathā yathā tat ||
children.translated_text: He pursued auspicious conduct, pure in practice, for he did not value sacrifice as highly as that.
For a hopeful petitioner who came to him, he at once cut off thirst with streams of gifts,
and, except in battle, he sought to split the swollen pride of foes with the axe of good conduct.

children.text: ekaṃ vininye sa jugopa sapta saptaiva tatyāja rarakṣa pañca
children.translated_text: He disciplined the one, protected the seven, abandoned seven as well, and guarded the five.

children.text: prāpa trivargaṃ bubudhe trivargaṃ jajñe dvivargaṃ prajahau dvivargam ||
children.translated_text: He attained the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims), understood a threefold group, recognized a twofold group, and abandoned a twofold group.
Even after convicting offenders who were liable to death, he did not kill them, nor did he look on them in anger.

children.text: babandha sāntvena phalena caitāṃstyāgo 'pi teṣāṃ hyanayāya dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He bound them with conciliation and reward, for even abandoning them was seen as bad policy.
He practiced the ancient highest vows and cast off hostilities long accumulated.
He acquired glories fragrant with virtues and removed the dusts that bring defilement.

children.text: na cājihīrṣīd balim apravṛttaṃ na cācikīrṣīt paravastvabhidhyām
children.translated_text: He did not wish to take a tax not yet due, nor did he desire to covet another's property.

children.text: na cāvivakṣīd dviṣatāmadharmaṃ na cāvivākṣīddhṛdayena manyum ||
children.translated_text: He did not wish to speak unrighteous words even about enemies, nor to cherish anger in his heart.

children.text: tasmiṃstathā bhūmipatau pravṛtte bhṛtyāśca paurāśca tathaiva ceruḥ
children.translated_text: When the king was acting in this way, his servants and citizens behaved in the very same way,
like the senses of one engaged in yoga when the mind, calm by nature, is clear.
Then, in due time, from lovely-breasted <s>Yaśodharā</s>, bearer of her own fame,

children.text: śauddhodane rāhusapatnavaktro jajñe suto rāhula eva nāmnā ||
children.translated_text: a son of the <s>Śuddhodana</s> line was born, moon-faced as the foe of <s>Rāhu</s>, and named <s>Rāhula</s>.

children.text: atheṣṭaputraḥ paramapratītaḥ kulasya vṛddhiṃ prati bhūmipālaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, possessing the son he desired and supremely delighted at the growth of the family,

children.text: yathaiva putraprasave nananda tathaiva pautraprasave nananda ||
children.translated_text: rejoiced at the birth of a grandson just as he had rejoiced at the birth of his son.

children.text: putrasya me putragato mameva snehaḥ kathaṃ syāditi jātaharṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Joy arose in him as he thought, 'How may the love I have for my son pass to my son's son, as to myself?',

children.text: kāle sa taṃ taṃ vidhim ālalambe putrapriyaḥ svargamivārurukṣan ||
children.translated_text: and, loving his son and wishing as though to ascend to heaven, he performed each rite for the child at the proper time.
Standing on the path of the primeval, fame-endowed bulls among kings,
he practiced pure austerities without renouncing his station, and sacrificed with sacrifices free from harm.

children.text: ajājvaliṣṭātha sa puṇyakarmā nṛpaśriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca
children.translated_text: Then that doer of meritorious deeds blazed with the splendor of kingship and with the splendor of austerity,

children.text: kulena vṛttena dhiyā ca dīptastejaḥ sahasrāṃśurivotsisṛkṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: shining through lineage, conduct, and intelligence, like the thousand-rayed sun about to pour forth light.
And after honoring the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and the <s>Ārcika</s>, he, firm in prosperity, recited prayers for his son's stability.

children.text: cakāra karmāṇi ca duṣkarāṇi prajāḥ sisṛkṣuḥ ka ivādikāle ||
children.translated_text: And, like <s>Ka</s> at the beginning of time, wishing to create living beings, he performed difficult rites.

children.text: tatyāja śastraṃ vimamarśa śāstraṃ śamaṃ siṣeve niyamaṃ viṣehe
children.translated_text: He laid aside weapons, reflected on scripture, practiced calm, and endured discipline;

children.text: vaśīva kaṃcidviṣayaṃ na bheje piteva sarvānviṣayāndadarśa ||
children.translated_text: self-controlled, he did not resort to any sense-object, and like a father he looked upon all his domains.

children.text: babhāra rājyaṃ sa hi putrahetoḥ putraṃ kulārthaṃ yaśase kulaṃ tu
children.translated_text: For he bore the kingdom for the sake of his son, his son for the sake of his family, and the family for the sake of fame;
he sought renown for heaven, heaven for his own sake, and his own continuance for the sake of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sa dharmaṃ vividhaṃ cakāra sadbhir nipātaṃ śrutitaśca siddham
children.translated_text: Thus he practiced manifold <s>dharma</s>, established by the good and proved from sacred tradition,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ putramukhaṃ suto me vanaṃ na yāyāditi nāthamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while praying, 'How might my son, after seeing a son's face, not go to the forest?'

children.text: rirakṣiṣantaḥ śriyamātmasaṃsthāṃ rakṣanti putrān bhuvi bhūmipālāḥ
children.translated_text: Kings on earth protect their sons because they wish to protect the fortune fixed in themselves;

children.text: putraṃ narendraḥ sa tu dharmakāmo rarakṣa dharmādviṣayeṣu muñcan ||
children.translated_text: but that king, though desiring <s>dharma</s>, protected his son by releasing him among pleasures, away from <s>dharma</s>.
Yet all <s>bodhisattvas</s> (awakening-beings), beings of incomparable nature, after knowing the taste of sense pleasure, went to the forest once sons had been born.

children.text: ata upacitakarmā rūḍhamūle 'pi hetau sa ratim upasiṣeve bodhim āpanna yāvat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, though his accumulated karma had ripened and the cause had taken deep root, he partook of pleasure until awakening drew near.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye antaḥpuravihāro nāma dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the second <s>sarga</s>, called <s>Antaḥpuravihāra</s>, 'Life in the Inner Palace.'
Then one day he heard of groves with soft lawns and trees made to resound by male cuckoos,
adorned with lotus ponds and celebrated in songs.
Having heard then of the charming nature of the city groves beloved by women,
he made up his mind to go outside, like an elephant confined inside a house.

children.text: tato nṛpastasya niśamya bhāvaṃ putrābhidhānasya manorathasya
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning the inclination of that wish expressed by his son,
ordered an excursion suited to affection, royal splendor, and the prince's youth.
And on the royal road he had the gathering of afflicted common people turned away,

children.text: mā bhūtkumāraḥ sukumāracittaḥ saṃvignacetā iti manyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Let the tender-minded prince not become alarmed in heart.'
Then those lacking limbs, those with impaired faculties, the old, the sick, and other pitiable people in every direction

children.text: tataḥ samutsārya pareṇa sāmnā śobhāṃ parāṃ rājapathasya cakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: were removed with the utmost gentle persuasion, and they made the royal road exceedingly beautiful.

children.text: tataḥ kṛte śrīmati rājamārge śrīmānvinītānucaraḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the royal road had been made splendid, the splendid prince, attended by disciplined followers,
descended from the palace roof at the proper time and, having received permission, approached the king.

children.text: atho narendraḥ sutamāgatāśruḥ śirasyupāghrāya ciraṃ nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: Then the lord of men, his tears rising as he smelled his son's head and gazed at him for a long time,

children.text: gaccheti cājñāpayati sma vācā snehānna cainaṃ manasā mumoca ||
children.translated_text: commanded him with his voice, 'Go,' but from affection did not release him in his mind.
Then he mounted a golden chariot harnessed with four quiet horses wearing ornaments of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold,
with its reins held by a brave, skilled, and pure-handed driver.
Then, with a suitable retinue, he entered the road strewn with a bright mass of flowers, hung with garlands, and fluttering with banners,
like the moon, accompanied by the stars, entering the sky.
As if being showered with half-open blue lotuses by eyes widened through curiosity,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanai rājapathaṃ jagāhe pauraiḥ samantādabhivīkṣyamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he slowly entered the royal road, watched on every side by the townspeople.

children.text: taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ saumyaguṇena kecidvavandire dīptatayā tathānye
children.translated_text: Some praised him for his gentle qualities, while others bowed to him because of his radiance;
and some, because of his gracious face, wished abundance for his fortune and his life.
Hunchbacked women came out from great houses, and rows of <s>Kirāta</s> dwarfs appeared;
women from poor dwellings too bowed like banners in a procession of the gods.

children.text: tataḥ kumāraḥ khalu gacchatīti śrutvā striyaḥ preṣyajanātpravṛttim
children.translated_text: Then, hearing from servants the news, 'The prince is indeed going out,'
the women, permitted by respected elders, went to the palace terraces in their desire to see him.
Some were hindered by loosened girdle-strings, and some had eyes confused from waking out of sleep;
some had ornaments thrown on as the news came, and, unrestrained by curiosity, they hurried all around,
with the rumbling on the floors of palace stairways, the ringing of girdles, and the sounds of anklets,
frightening flocks of house-birds and checking one another's speed.
But for some of these lovely women, though haste had arisen and they were eager,
their broad hips and full breasts, by their heaviness, held back their gait.

children.text: śīghraṃ samarthāpi tu gantumanyā gatiṃ nijagrāha yayau na tūrṇam
children.translated_text: Another, though able to go quickly, restrained her gait and did not go in haste,
made timid by modesty and concealing ornaments put on in private.
Among those women, pressed into a mass by pushing one another, their earrings shaken by the crowding,
there was then no quiet at the windows as their ornaments rang aloud.
From the windows emerged the lotus-faces of the women, their earrings jostled by one another;
they shone like lotuses fastened upon the palace.
Then the splendid city shone on every side with mansions crowded by young women and with windows opened by curiosity,
like the sky with aerial palaces filled with <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs).
Because the windows were narrow, the earrings of the foremost women rested against one another's cheeks,

children.text: mukhāni rejuḥ pramadottamānāṃ baddhāḥ kalāpā iva paṅkajānām ||
children.translated_text: and their faces shone like bound clusters of lotuses.

children.text: taṃ tāḥ kumāraṃ pathi vīkṣamāṇāḥ striyo babhur gām iva gantukāmāḥ
children.translated_text: As they watched the prince on the road, those women seemed as if they wanted to go down to the earth;

children.text: ūrdhvonmukhāścainamudīkṣamāṇā narā babhur dyām iva gantukāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the men, looking up at him with upturned faces, seemed as if they wanted to go to heaven.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ rājasutaṃ striyastā jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā śriyā ca
children.translated_text: And seeing that prince, blazing with beauty of body and with splendor,
They softly said, 'Blessed is his wife,' with pure minds and not from any other motive.

children.text: ayaṃ kila vyāyatapīnabāhū rūpeṇa sākṣādiva puṣpaketuḥ
children.translated_text: This man, with long and full arms, is in beauty like <s>Puṣpaketu</s> himself,

children.text: tyaktvā śriyaṃ dharmamupaiṣyatīti tasmin hi tā gauravameva cakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet he will abandon splendor and resort to <s>dharma</s> (the religious path); therefore they showed only reverence toward him.

children.text: kīrṇaṃ tathā rājapathaṃ kumāraḥ paurairvinītaiḥ śucidhīraveṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: The prince saw the royal road thus filled with citizens, disciplined and pure in mind and dress,
as it had never been before; he rejoiced somewhat and thought it was like a rebirth of himself.

children.text: puraṃ tu tatsvargamiva prahṛṣṭaṃ śuddhādhivāsāḥ samavekṣya devāḥ
children.translated_text: But when the gods dwelling in the Pure Abodes saw that city rejoicing like heaven,

children.text: jīrṇaṃ naraṃ nirmamire prayātuṃ saṃcodanārthaṃ kṣitipātmajasya ||
children.translated_text: they fashioned an old man to go there, in order to stir the king's son.

children.text: tataḥ kumāro jarayābhibhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā narebhyaḥ pṛthagākṛtiṃ tam
children.translated_text: Then the prince saw that man overcome by old age, with a form different from other men,
and, his concern aroused, he spoke to the charioteer, his gaze fixed motionless on that very spot.

children.text: ka eṣa bhoḥ sūta naro 'bhyupetaḥ keśaiḥ sitairyaṣṭiviṣaktahastaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this man, charioteer, who has come here with white hair and a hand clinging to a staff,
his eyes covered by his brows and his limbs loose and bent? Is this a deformity, his nature, or chance?'
Thus addressed, the driver of the chariot explained it to the king's son,
though the matter was to be concealed; seeing no fault, his mind had been bewildered by those very gods.

children.text: rūpasya hantrī vyasanaṃ balasya śokasya yonirnidhanaṃ ratīnām
children.translated_text: 'The destroyer of beauty, the calamity of strength, the source of grief, the death of pleasures,

children.text: nāśaḥ smṛtīnāṃ ripurindriyāṇāmeṣā jarā nāma yayaiṣa bhagnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ruin of memories, the enemy of the senses: this is called old age, by which this man has been broken.

children.text: pītaṃ hyanenāpi payaḥ śiśutve kālena bhūyaḥ parisṛptamurvyām
children.translated_text: For he too drank milk in infancy; in time he crawled again upon the earth.

children.text: krameṇa bhūtvā ca yuvā vapuṣmān krameṇa tenaiva jarāmupetaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gradually he became a handsome youth, and gradually, by that same time, he has come to old age.'

children.text: ityevamukte calitaḥ sa kiṃcidrājātmajaḥ sūtamidaṃ babhāṣe
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the king's son was somewhat shaken and said this to the charioteer:

children.text: kimeṣa doṣo bhavitā mamāpītyasmai tataḥ sārathirabhyuvāca ||
children.translated_text: 'Will this defect come to be mine as well?' Then the charioteer said to him:
'Even for one long-lived, this advance of age will certainly come under the power of time.

children.text: evaṃ jarāṃ rūpavināśayitrīṃ jānāti caivecchati caiva lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And yet the world knows old age as the destroyer of beauty and still desires life.'
Then he, whose intelligence was pure through former disposition, whose meritorious deeds had been accumulated through vast ages,

children.text: śrutvā jarāṃ saṃvivije mahātmā mahāśanerghoṣamivāntike gauḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled one, hearing of old age, trembled like a cow near the crash of a great thunderbolt.

children.text: niḥśvasya dīrghaṃ svaśiraḥ prakampya tasmiṃśca jīrṇe viniveśya cakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Sighing deeply, shaking his head, and fixing his eyes on that old man,

children.text: tāṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā janatāṃ saharṣāṃ vākyaṃ sa saṃvigna idaṃ jagāda ||
children.translated_text: and seeing that same crowd full of joy, he, distressed, spoke these words:

children.text: evaṃ jarā hanti ca nirviśeṣaṃ smṛtiṃ ca rūpaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca
children.translated_text: 'Thus old age destroys without distinction memory, beauty, and prowess,
and yet the world does not feel alarm, even while seeing such a thing directly.

children.text: evaṃ gate sūta nivartayāśvān śīghraṃ gṛhāṇyeva bhavānprayātu
children.translated_text: Since this is so, charioteer, turn back the horses; let your honor go quickly to the palace.

children.text: udyānabhūmau hi kuto ratirme jarābhaye cetasi vartamāne ||
children.translated_text: For how could I have pleasure in the park when fear of old age is present in my mind?'

children.text: athājñayā bhartṛsutasya tasya nivartayāmāsa rathaṃ niyantā
children.translated_text: Then, at the command of his lord's son, the driver turned the chariot back.

children.text: tataḥ kumāro bhavanaṃ tadeva cintāvaśaḥ śūnyamiva prapede ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the prince, subject to thought, entered that very palace as if it were empty.

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva na śarma lebhe jarā jareti praparīkṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But when even there he found no comfort, pondering again and again, 'old age, old age,'

children.text: tato narendrānumataḥ sa bhūyaḥ krameṇa tenaiva bahirjagāma ||
children.translated_text: then, with the king's permission, he went outside again in due course by that same route.

children.text: athāparaṃ vyādhiparītadehaṃ ta eva devāḥ sasṛjurmanuṣyam
children.translated_text: Then those same gods created another man, his body overcome by disease.
Seeing him, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, his gaze fixed on that man, addressed the charioteer:
'With swollen belly, body shaking with breath, shoulders and arms drooping, and limbs thin and pale,

children.text: ambeti vācaṃ karuṇaṃ bruvāṇaḥ paraṃ samāśritya naraḥ ka eṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: crying pitiably, "Mother," and leaning on another person, who is this man?'
Then the charioteer said to him, 'Gentle sir, arisen and grown from the disturbance of the bodily elements,
this very great calamity called disease has made this man dependent, though he had strength.'

children.text: ityūcivān rājasutaḥ sa bhūyastaṃ sānukampo naramīkṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The king's son, looking at that man again with compassion, said further:

children.text: asyaiva jātaḥ pṛthageṣa doṣaḥ sāmānyato rogabhayaṃ prajānām ||
children.translated_text: 'Has this defect arisen as his alone and separately, or is the fear of disease common among creatures?'

children.text: tato babhāṣe sa rathapraṇetā kumāra sādhāraṇa eṣa doṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the driver of the chariot said, 'Prince, this defect is common.

children.text: evaṃ hi rogaiḥ paripīḍyamāno rujāturo harṣamupaiti lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, even while thus oppressed by diseases and tormented by pain, the world comes to delight.'

children.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sa viṣaṇṇacetāḥ prāvepatāmbūrmigataḥ śaśīva
children.translated_text: Hearing this meaning, he became despondent in mind and trembled like the moon in water stirred by waves.

children.text: idaṃ ca vākyaṃ karuṇāyamānaḥ provāca kiṃcinmṛdunā svareṇa ||
children.translated_text: And, moved by compassion, he spoke these words in a somewhat gentle voice:

children.text: idaṃ ca rogavyasanaṃ prajānāṃ paśyaṃśca viśrambhamupaiti lokaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Seeing this calamity of disease among creatures, the world still becomes confident.
Ah, vast is the ignorance of men, who laugh though they are not freed from fears of disease.
Let the chariot be turned back from the journey outside; let it go to the king's palace itself.

children.text: śrutvā ca me rogabhayaṃ ratibhyaḥ pratyāhataṃ saṃkucatīva cetaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, having heard of the danger of disease, my mind recoils from pleasures and seems to shrink.'

children.text: tato nivṛttaḥ sa nivṛttaharṣaḥ pradhyānayuktaḥ praviveśa veśma
children.translated_text: Then, turned back and with his joy turned back, absorbed in deep reflection, he entered the dwelling.

children.text: taṃ dvistathā prekṣya ca saṃnivṛttaṃ paryeṣaṇaṃ bhūmipatiścakāra ||
children.translated_text: And when the king saw him returned twice in this way, he made an inquiry.

children.text: śrutvā nimittaṃ tu nivartanasya saṃtyaktamātmānamanena mene
children.translated_text: Hearing the reason for his return, he thought that he himself had been abandoned by him.

children.text: mārgasya śaucādhikṛtāya caiva cukrośa ruṣṭo 'pi ca nogradaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He scolded the officer appointed to purify the road, yet, though angry, he did not impose a harsh punishment.

children.text: bhūyaśca tasmai vidadhe sutāya viśeṣayuktaṃ viṣayapracāram
children.translated_text: Again he arranged for that son a specially elaborate display of sense pleasures,
hoping that, because the senses are fickle, he might at least become attached and not abandon them.

children.text: yadā ca śabdādibhirindriyārthairantaḥpure naiva suto 'sya reme
children.translated_text: And when his son did not delight in the women's quarters through sounds and the other objects of the senses,

children.text: tato bahirvyādiśati sma yātrāṃ rasāntaraṃ syāditi manyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he ordered a journey outside, thinking, 'There may be another kind of pleasure.'

children.text: snehācca bhāvaṃ tanayasya buddhvā sa rāgadoṣān avicintya kāṃścit
children.translated_text: From affection, and because he understood his son's disposition, he gave no thought to any possible faults of passion.

children.text: yogyāḥ samājñāpayati sma tatra kalāsvabhijñā iti vāramukhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He ordered the chief courtesans there, women fit for the task and skilled in the arts.

children.text: tato viśeṣeṇa narendramārge svalaṃkṛte caiva parīkṣite ca
children.translated_text: Then, when the royal road had been especially adorned and also carefully inspected,

children.text: vyatyasya sūtaṃ ca rathaṃ ca rājā prasthāpayāmāsa bahiḥ kumāram ||
children.translated_text: the king changed the charioteer and the chariot and sent the prince outside.

children.text: tatastathā gacchati rājaputre taireva devairvihito gatāsuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as the king's son was going in that way, a dead man, arranged by those same gods, was there.

children.text: taṃ caiva mārge mṛtamuhyamānaṃ sūtaḥ kumāraśca dadarśa nānyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only the charioteer and the prince saw him on the road, dead and being carried away; no one else did.

children.text: athābravīd rājasutaḥ sa sūtaṃ naraiścaturbhir hriyate ka eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king's son said to the charioteer, 'Who is this, being borne by four men,
followed by sorrowing people, who is adorned and yet enclosed?'

children.text: tataḥ sa śuddhātmabhireva devaiḥ śuddhādhivāsair abhibhūtacetāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the driver, his mind overpowered by the pure-hearted gods dwelling in pure abodes,
spoke this matter, though it should not have been spoken, meaningfully to his lord.
'Bereft of intellect, senses, life-breath, and qualities, asleep, unconscious, become like grass and wood,

children.text: saṃvardhya saṃrakṣya ca yatnavadbhiḥ priyapriyaistyajyata eṣa ko 'pi ||
children.translated_text: this man, though carefully raised and protected by those dear to him, is abandoned by his beloved people.'

children.text: iti praṇetuḥ sa niśamya vākyaṃ saṃcukṣubhe kiṃciduvāca cainam
children.translated_text: Hearing the driver's words, the prince was somewhat shaken and said to him,
'Is this the <s>dharma</s> (law) of this man alone, or is such an end the fate of all creatures?'

children.text: tataḥ praṇetā vadati sma tasmai sarvaprajānāmidamantakarma
children.translated_text: Then the driver said to him, 'This work of death belongs to all creatures.

children.text: hīnasya madhyasya mahātmano vā sarvasya loke niyato vināśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the low, the middling, or the great-souled, destruction is fixed for everyone in the world.'

children.text: tataḥ sa dhīro 'pi narendrasūnuḥ śrutvaiva mṛtyuṃ viṣasāda sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king's son, though steadfast, at the mere hearing of death became despondent at once,

children.text: aṃsena saṃśliṣya ca kūbarāgraṃ provāca nihrādavatā svareṇa ||
children.translated_text: and, leaning his shoulder against the front of the chariot-pole, he spoke in a resonant voice:

children.text: iyaṃ ca niṣṭhā niyatā prajānāṃ pramādyati tyaktabhayaśca lokaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This is the fixed end of creatures, and the world is heedless, having cast away fear.

children.text: manāṃsi śaṅke kaṭhināni nṝṇāṃ svasthāstathā hyadhvani vartamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think men's minds are hard indeed, since they remain at ease while traveling on this road.

children.text: tasmādrathaḥ sūta nivartyatāṃ no vihārabhūmerna hi deśakālaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, charioteer, let our chariot be turned back; this is not the place or time for pleasure grounds.

children.text: jānanvināśaṃ katham ārtikāle sacetanaḥ syādiha hi pramattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing destruction, how could a conscious person be heedless here in a time of affliction?'

children.text: iti bruvāṇe 'pi narādhipātmaje nivartayāmāsa sa naiva taṃ ratham
children.translated_text: Even as the prince, son of the lord of men, was speaking thus, the charioteer did not turn that chariot back.

children.text: viśeṣayuktaṃ tu narendraśāsanātsa padmaṣaṇḍaṃ vanameva niryayau ||
children.translated_text: Rather, by the king's special command, he went out to the forest, the cluster of lotus ponds.
Then the prince saw that pleasant grove, with young flowering trees and delighted, intoxicated cuckoos flying about,

children.text: vimānavatsa kamalacārudīrghikaṃ dadarśa tadvanamiva nandanaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: with lovely long lotus ponds like celestial palaces, a grove like the <s>Nandana</s> grove.
Then the king's son was forcibly led into that grove, crowded with groups of excellent women,
like a newly vowed ascetic, fearful of obstacles, led to the dwelling of the lord of <s>Alakā</s>, surrounded by excellent <s>apsarases</s>.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye saṃvegotpattir nāma tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the third canto, named 'The Arising of Disquiet.'
Then from that city garden the women, their eyes restless with curiosity,
went out to meet the king's son when he had arrived, as if he were a chosen bridegroom.
Approaching him, their eyes widened and blossoming with wonder,
they performed the gesture of greeting for him with hands like lotus buds.
They stood surrounding him, their minds seized by <s>Manmatha</s>,
as if drinking him in with motionless eyes opened wide by delight.

children.text: taṃ hi tā menire nāryaḥ kāmo vigrahavāniti
children.translated_text: For those women thought him to be <s>Kāma</s> embodied,
adorned with his shining natural marks as if with ornaments.
Some, because of his gentleness and also his firmness, understood him to be

children.text: avatīrṇo mahīṃ sākṣād gūḍhāṃśuś candramā iti ||
children.translated_text: the moon himself, with hidden rays, descended upon the earth.
Drawn by his beauty, they displayed restrained languor,
and, striking one another with glances, they sighed softly.

children.text: evaṃ tā dṛṣṭimātreṇa nāryo dadṛśureva tam
children.translated_text: In this way the women merely looked at him with their gaze;
they neither spoke nor laughed, held in check by his majesty.
Seeing them thus inactive and bewildered by love,
the wise <s>Udāyī</s>, the chaplain's son, spoke these words:
'All of you know every art and are skilled at grasping emotion.
Endowed with beauty and cleverness, you have attained preeminence by your own qualities.
With these qualities you could adorn even the excellent <s>Uttara Kurus</s>,
and even <s>Kubera</s>'s pleasure ground, let alone this earth.
You are able to stir even passionless seers,
and to captivate even gods surrounded by <s>apsarases</s>.
Through knowledge of feeling, gesture, and the excellence of beauty and cleverness,

children.text: strīṇāmeva ca śaktāḥ stha saṃrāge kiṃ punarnṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: you are able to inflame even women themselves; how much more, then, men.
Since you are of such a kind, yet are separated from your proper sphere,
I am not pleased with this sort of behavior, with this straightforwardness of yours.
This behavior of yours would be fitting for new brides,

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ hi syādapi vā gopayoṣitām ||
children.translated_text: whose eyes are contracted by shyness, or perhaps for cowherd girls.
Even if this man is steadfast and great through the power of his splendor,
one must conclude here that the power of women too is great.
For in ancient times the great seer <s>Vyāsa</s>, though hard for even the gods to assail,
was struck by the foot of <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, a courtesan.
And the mendicant <s>Manthāla Gautama</s>, through the leg of a chief courtesan,
formerly gave up his life, wishing to please her for that very purpose.
A woman, though inferior in class and station, satisfied <s>Gautama</s>,
the great seer of long austerity and long life.
Likewise <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, the sage's son, inexperienced with women...

children.text: upāyairvividhaiḥ śāntā jagrāha ca jahāra ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntā</s>, by various stratagems, both captivated and carried him away.
And the great seer <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, though deeply immersed in great austerity,
when carried away by the apsaras <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, thought ten years to be a single day.
Women brought such sages as these, one after another, to alteration;
how much more the son of a king, in the playful first bloom of youth?

children.text: tadevaṃ sati viśrabdhaṃ prayatadhvaṃ tathā yathā
children.translated_text: Therefore, this being so, strive with confidence in such a way
that this glory of the king's line does not turn away from here.

children.text: yā hi kāścidyuvatayo haranti sadṛśaṃ janam
children.translated_text: For any young women who captivate a man suited to themselves are women;

children.text: nikṛṣṭotkṛṣṭayorbhāvaṃ yā gṛhṇanti tu tāḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but those who seize the disposition of the low and the high alike: they are truly women.

children.text: ityudāyivacaḥ śrutvā tā viddhā iva yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of <s>Udayin</s>, those women were as if pierced;
they braced themselves for the capture of the prince.

children.text: tā bhrūbhiḥ prekṣitair hāvair hasitair laḍitair gataiḥ
children.translated_text: With eyebrows, glances, gestures, smiles, playful motions, and gaits,
the women made enticing movements, as if timid and afraid.
But because of the king's commission and because of the prince's gentleness,
they quickly shed their lack of confidence, through intoxication and through love.
Then the prince, surrounded by the company of women, wandered through the grove,
like a bull elephant accompanied by a herd of females in a forest of the <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: sa tasmin kānane ramye jajvāla strīpuraḥsaraḥ
children.translated_text: In that lovely grove he blazed, with women going before him,
and shone like <s>Vivasvān</s> in a pleasure-ground, surrounded by apsarases.
Some women there, as if bent aside by intoxication,
touched him with their hard, full, close-set, lovely breasts.
One, weak with the tender creeper of her long, soft arm slipping from her shoulder,
pretended to stumble falsely and embraced him by force.
Another, with a copper-red lower lip and a mouth scented with wine,
breathed into his ear, 'Listen to a secret.'
Another, moist with unguent, spoke as though issuing a command,
'Show devotion here,' out of a desire to clasp his hand.
Yet another, again and again under the pretext of intoxication, let her dark-blue garment slip down;
with her girdle visible she shone like night with flashing lightning.
Some, with gold girdles ringing aloud,
wandered here and there, showing him their hips covered by thin cloth.
Others grasped a flowering mango branch and hung down from it,
displaying breasts like golden jars.
One lotus-eyed woman came from a lotus pond, holding a lotus,
and stood beside his lotus face like the splendor of a lotus.
One sang a sweet song, apt in meaning, with expressive gesture,
as if urging him, composed as he was, by her glances: 'You are being cheated.'
Another, with a lovely face drawing the bow of her brows,
covered herself and imitated his behavior with dignified grace.
One, with full lovely breasts and earrings shaken by laughter,
laughed loudly at him, saying, 'May you succeed, sir!'
As he was going away, still others bound him with ropes of garlands;
some seized him with goads of speech, sweet but reproachful.
One, eager for a contest, seized a mango creeper

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ tu kasyeti papraccha madaviklavā ||
children.translated_text: and, unsteady with intoxication, asked, 'Whose flower is this?'
Another made her gait and posture like those of a man

children.text: uvācainaṃ jitaḥ strībhir jaya bho pṛthivīmimām ||
children.translated_text: and said to him, 'Conquered by women, sir, conquer this earth!'
Then one with restless eyes, smelling a blue lotus,
addressed the king's son with words somewhat indistinct from intoxication:
'Look, lord, at the mango tree covered with honey-scented flowers,
where a cuckoo sings as if shut inside a golden cage.
'Look at this aśoka, increasing the sorrow of lovers,
where bees hum as if being burned by fire.
'Look at the tilaka tree embraced by a mango shoot,
like a man in white clothes by a woman with yellow-painted limbs.
'Look at the blossoming kuruvaka, like bright lac that has been pressed out,
bowed down as if rebuked by the radiance of women's nails.
'And look at this young aśoka, covered thickly with shoots,
standing as if ashamed by the beauty of our hands.
'Look at the long pond covered with bank-born sinduvāraka shrubs,
like a woman lying wrapped in pale silk.

children.text: dṛśyatāṃ strīṣu māhātmyaṃ cakravāko hyasau jale
children.translated_text: 'See the greatness of women among females: for that cakravāka in the water
follows his wife from behind, trailing her like a servant.
'Listen to the call of the intoxicated cuckoo as it cries;
another cuckoo sings after it each moment, like an echo.
'Can it be that spring has brought intoxication even to the birds,
but not to a man who, thinking the unthinkable, imagines himself wise?'
In this way those young women, their minds unrestrained by <s>Manmatha</s>,
approached the prince with all those various stratagems.
Yet even while being thus enticed, he, his senses enclosed by firmness,

children.text: martavyamiti sodvego na jaharṣa na vivyathe ||
children.translated_text: anxious with the thought, 'I must die,' neither rejoiced nor was disturbed.
Seeing that they had no abiding in reality, that best of men
reflected with a mind at once troubled and steadfast.

children.text: kiṃ tvimā nāvagacchanti capalaṃ yauvanaṃ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'How is it that these women do not understand that youth is unstable,
since old age will destroy one who is intoxicated by beauty?
'Surely they do not see anyone's collapse into disease,

children.text: tathā hṛṣṭā bhayaṃ tyaktvā jagati vyādhidharmiṇi ||
children.translated_text: for they are so delighted, having cast off fear, in a world whose nature is sickness.
And clearly they are unacquainted with death, which carries everything away.

children.text: tataḥ svasthā nirudvignāḥ krīḍanti ca hasanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, they remain at ease and untroubled, playing and laughing.

children.text: jarāṃ vyādhiṃ ca mṛtyuṃ ca ko hi jānansacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: For what conscious person, knowing old age, disease, and death,
would stand at ease, or sit, or lie down, much less laugh?

children.text: yastu dṛṣṭvā paraṃ jīrṇaṃ vyādhitaṃ mṛtameva ca
children.translated_text: But one who, after seeing another person aged, sick, and dead,
remains at ease and unalarmed is just like one without consciousness.
For when a tree is being separated from its flowers and even from its fruits,

children.text: patati chidyamāne vā taruranyo na śocate ||
children.translated_text: or when it falls or is cut down, another tree does not grieve.
Seeing him thus intent on meditation, with longing gone from sense objects,
<s>Udāyin</s>, skilled in the science of conduct, spoke to him in friendship:

children.text: ahaṃ nṛpatinā dattaḥ sakhā tubhyaṃ kṣamaḥ kila
children.translated_text: "I was given by the king to you as a suitable friend, indeed;

children.text: yasmāt tvayi vivakṣā me tayā praṇayavattayā ||
children.translated_text: therefore I wish to speak to you with that affectionate intimacy.
Keeping one back from what is harmful, setting one forward in what is beneficial,
and not abandoning one in misfortune: this is the threefold mark of a friend.
So if I, having pledged friendship, were to disregard you as you turn away from <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human aims),

children.text: yadi tvā samupekṣeya na bhavenmitratā mayi ||
children.translated_text: there would be no friendship in me.
Therefore, as a friend, I tell you: for one young and handsome,
this kind of lack of courtesy toward women is not fitting for you.
Even with an untruth it is proper to accommodate women,
both to remove their embarrassment and for one's own delight.
Deference and compliance are what bind women's hearts;
for virtues are the source of affection, and women desire respect.
Therefore, broad-eyed one, even if your heart is turned away,
you ought to respond with a courtesy suited to this beauty of yours.
Courtesy is a remedy for women; courtesy is the highest ornament.
Beauty without courtesy is like a forest without flowers.
Or rather, what use is mere courtesy? Let there be acceptance with real feeling.
Having obtained rare pleasures, you ought not despise them.

children.text: kāmaṃ paramiti jñātvā devo 'pi hi puraṃdaraḥ
children.translated_text: For knowing desire to be supreme, even the god <s>Puraṃdara</s>
once desired <s>Ahalyā</s>, the wife of the sage <s>Gautama</s>.
<s>Agastya</s> also sought <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the wife of <s>Soma</s>;
therefore he obtained <s>Lopāmudrā</s>, who resembled her, so tradition says.
In <s>Mamatā</s>, the wife of <s>Utathya</s>,
the great ascetic <s>Bṛhaspati</s> begot <s>Bharadvāja</s> in the <s>Mārutī</s> woman.
