And in the queen of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, while she was making an offering,
<s>Candramas</s>, best of sacrificers, begot <s>Budha</s>, whose deeds were divine.
Long ago, too, <s>Parāśara</s>, filled with passion, approached the maiden <s>Kālī</s>,
born from one born in water, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
With desire for intercourse, in the despised <s>Akṣamālā</s>, a <s>Mātaṅgī</s>,
the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> begot the son <s>Kapiñjalāda</s>.
And the royal seer <s>Yayāti</s>, even when his youth had passed away,
sported with the apsaras <s>Viśvācī</s> in the <s>Caitraratha</s> forest.
The <s>Kaurava</s> <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, though he knew that contact with a woman ended in destruction,
was captivated by <s>Mādrī</s>'s beauty and virtues and pursued pleasure born of desire.
And <s>Karāla Janaka</s>, after carrying off a brahmin girl,

children.text: avāpa bhraṃśamapyevaṃ na tu seje na manmatham ||
children.translated_text: incurred downfall even so, yet he did not withstand <s>Manmatha</s>.
Great men such as these enjoyed even censured sense objects
for the sake of pleasure, and all the more those endowed with good qualities.
But you, strong, handsome, and young, despise sense objects
that have come to you rightly, and to which this world is attached.
After hearing this smooth speech of his, supported by traditional examples,
the prince, with a voice like the rumble of a thundercloud, replied:
"This statement is fitting in you and shows friendship;

children.text: atra ca tvānuneṣyāmi yatra mā duṣṭhu manyase ||
children.translated_text: and here I shall explain myself to you, so that you do not think ill of me.
I do not despise sense objects; I know the world has them as its essence.

children.text: anityaṃ tu jaganmatvā nātra me ramate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But because I consider the world impermanent, my mind does not delight in them.

children.text: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca yadi na syādidaṃ trayam
children.translated_text: If old age, disease, and death, this triad, did not exist,
I too would have delight in lovely sense objects.
Even if this very body of women were always the same,

children.text: doṣavatsvapi kāmeṣu kāmaṃ rajyeta me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my mind might indeed be attached to pleasures, though they are full of faults.
But when their beauty has been drunk away by old age,
and has become unwelcome even to themselves, only through delusion could there be delight in it.
A person whose nature is death, disease, and old age,
sporting unalarmed with those whose nature is death, disease, and old age, is equal to beasts and birds.
As for what you said, that even those great men were ruled by desire,
precisely here one should feel alarm, since even they came to an end.

children.text: māhātmyaṃ na ca tanmanye yatra sāmānyataḥ kṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: And I do not consider that greatness, where there is destruction in common with all;
nor is either attachment to sense objects, or an argument for it, compatible with self-possession.
As for what you said, that one should behave toward women even with an untruth,
I do not approve of any untruth, even under the name of courtesy.

children.text: na cānuvartanaṃ tanme rucitaṃ yatra nārjavam
children.translated_text: Nor do I like that compliance in which there is no honesty.

children.text: sarvabhāvena saṃparko yadi nāsti dhigastu tat ||
children.translated_text: If there is no contact with one's whole being, shame on it.
Why indeed should the mind of one who is unsteady, trusting, attached,
seeing no fault, and already filled with passion, be deceived?
And if those who have fallen in love deceive one another in this way,

children.text: nanu naiva kṣamaṃ draṣṭuṃ narāḥ strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely men are not fit to be seen by women, nor women by men.
Therefore, since this is so, you ought not mislead me, afflicted by suffering
and subject to old age and death, into ignoble pleasures."

children.text: aho 'tidhīraṃ balavacca te manaścaleṣu kāmeṣu ca sāradarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, your mind is exceedingly firm and strong, seeing what is essential amid unstable pleasures,

children.text: bhaye 'titīvre viṣayeṣu sajjase nirīkṣamāṇo maraṇādhvani prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for, while observing people on the road to death, you cling to sense objects in this most terrible danger.
But I, timid and utterly shaken, thinking about the danger of old age, calamity, and disease,

children.text: labhe na śāntiṃ na dhṛtiṃ kuto ratiṃ niśāmayandīptamivāgninā jagat ||
children.translated_text: find neither peace nor steadfastness; how then could I find delight, seeing the world as if blazing with fire?

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ mṛtyuriti prajānato narasya rāgo hṛdi yasya jāyate
children.translated_text: For a man who knows without doubt, 'Death is certain,' yet in whose heart passion arises,

children.text: ayomayīṃ tasya paraimi cetanāṃ mahābhaye rajyati yo na roditi ||
children.translated_text: I judge his consciousness to be made of iron, if he delights in great danger and does not weep.

children.text: atho kumāraśca viniścayātmikāṃ cakāra kāmāśrayaghātinīṃ kathām
children.translated_text: Then the prince made a speech grounded in firm resolve and striking down the refuge of desire;
and the sun, its disk pleasing to people's eyes, went down behind the mountain.
Then the women, whose ornaments and garlands had been borne in vain, and whose arts and endearments had proved fruitless,

children.text: sva eva bhāve vinigṛhya manmathaṃ puraṃ yayurbhagnamanorathāḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: restraining <s>Manmatha</s> within themselves, went back to the city with their hopes broken.

children.text: tataḥ purodyānagatāṃ janaśriyaṃ nirīkṣya sāyaṃ pratisaṃhṛtāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the splendor of the people in the city garden drawn back again at evening,
the king's son entered his dwelling, contemplating impermanence as present everywhere.

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā rājā viṣayavimukhaṃ tasya tu mano na śiśye tāṃ rātriṃ hṛdayagataśalyo gaja iva
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that his mind was turned away from objects of sense, the king did not sleep that night, like an elephant with a dart lodged in its heart;

children.text: atha śrānto mantre bahuvividhamārge sasacivo na so 'nyatkāmebhyo niyamanamapaśyatsutamateḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, wearied in counsel with his ministers over many different courses, he saw no other restraint for his son's mind than pleasures.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye strīvighātano nāma caturthaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth canto, called <s>Strīvighātana</s>, 'The Foiling of the Women,' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>.
Thus, though being enticed by objects of sense, even by very precious ones, the son of the <s>Śākya</s> king

children.text: na jagāma dhṛtiṃ na śarma lebhe hṛdaye siṃha ivātidigdhaviddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not come to steadiness or obtain ease, like a lion deeply wounded in the heart by a poisoned arrow.
Then one day, escorted by capable ministers' sons and by friends skilled in varied conversation,
desiring to see the forest land and seeking calm, he set out beyond the city with the king's permission.
With a new golden bit and jingling bells,

children.text: abhiruhya sa kanthakaṃ sadaśvaṃ prayayau ketumiva drumābjaketuḥ ||
children.translated_text: handsome with swaying chowries and golden trappings, he mounted the excellent horse <s>Kanthaka</s> and went forth like a banner, he whose emblem was tree and lotus.

children.text: sa vikṛṣṭatarāṃ vanāntabhūmiṃ vanalobhācca yayau mahīguṇācca
children.translated_text: Out of longing for the forest, and because of the quality of the land, he went to a more remote woodland region,
and he saw the earth being ploughed, its furrow lines twisting like waves on water.
Its grass and darbha had been split by the plough and scattered, and it was strewn with tiny worms, insects, and creatures killed.

children.text: samavekṣya rasāṃ tathāvidhāṃ tāṃ svajanasyeva vadhe bhṛśaṃ śuśoca ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the soil in such a condition, he grieved deeply, as if at the killing of his own kin.
Seeing also the men who were ploughing, their complexions altered by wind, sunrays, and dust,

children.text: vahanaklamaviklavāṃśca dhuryān paramāryaḥ paramāṃ kṛpāṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: and the draft animals exhausted and distressed by the burden of hauling, the supremely noble one felt supreme compassion.
Then, dismounting from the horse's back, he walked slowly over the ground, overcome by grief,

children.text: jagato jananavyayaṃ vicinvan kṛpaṇaṃ khalvidamityuvāca cārtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: pondering the birth and destruction of the world; afflicted, he said, 'This is indeed pitiable.'
And seeking solitude in his mind, he held back those friends who were following him,
and in a lonely place, near a tree with lovely leaves moving all around, he went to the root of a <s>jambū</s> tree.

children.text: niṣasāda sa yatra śaucavatyāṃ bhuvi vaidūryanikāśaśādvalāyām
children.translated_text: There he sat on clean ground, on grass resembling lapis lazuli,
pondering the arising and passing away of the world, and he took hold of the path to steadiness of mind.
Having at once attained steadiness of mind, freed from afflictions such as longing for sense objects,
he attained the tranquil first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), accompanied by thought and reflection, of a taintless kind.

children.text: adhigamya tato vivekajaṃ tu paramaprītisukhaṃ manaḥsamādhim
children.translated_text: Then, having attained concentration of mind born of seclusion, with supreme joy and happiness,

children.text: idameva tataḥ paraṃ pradadhyau manasā lokagatiṃ niśāmya samyak ||
children.translated_text: from there he reflected on this further matter, after properly observing the course of the world in his mind:

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ bata yajjanaḥ svayaṃ sannavaśo vyādhijarāvināśadharmā
children.translated_text: 'Alas, it is pitiable that a person, being himself such, powerless and by nature subject to sickness, old age, and destruction,

children.text: jarayārditamāturaṃ mṛtaṃ vā paramajño vijugupsate madāndhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mad-blind through utter ignorance, feels disgust for another who is afflicted by old age, sick, or dead.

children.text: iha cedahamīdṛśaḥ svayaṃ san vijugupseya paraṃ tathāsvabhāvam
children.translated_text: If I, being myself such here, were to feel disgust for another of the same nature,

children.text: na bhavetsadṛśaṃ hi tatkṣamaṃ vā paramaṃ dharmamimaṃ vijānato me ||
children.translated_text: that would not be fitting or proper for me, who understand this supreme <s>dharma</s> (truth).'
As he thus saw correctly the faults of the world, its sickness, old age, and calamity,
the inward pride arising from strength, youth, and life vanished in an instant.

children.text: na jaharṣa na cāpi cānutepe vicikitsāṃ na yayau na tandrinidre
children.translated_text: He neither rejoiced nor regretted; he did not fall into doubt, lethargy, or sleep;

children.text: na ca kāmaguṇeṣu saṃrarañje na vididveṣa paraṃ na cāvamene ||
children.translated_text: he did not become attached to the qualities of desire, nor did he hate another or look down on him.

children.text: iti buddhiriyaṃ ca nīrajaskā vavṛdhe tasya mahātmano viśuddhā
children.translated_text: Thus this stainless, purified understanding grew in that great-souled one,
and, unseen by other men, a man in the garb of a mendicant approached.
The son of the king asked him, 'Tell me, who are you?' and then he answered him,
'Bull among men, fearing birth and death, I am a <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant), gone forth for the sake of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: jagati kṣayadharmake mumukṣurmṛgaye 'haṃ śivamakṣayaṃ padaṃ tat
children.translated_text: Seeking release in a world whose nature is decay, I search for that auspicious, imperishable state,
with equal understanding toward kin and strangers, my passion and hatred turned away from sense objects.

children.text: nivasan kvacideva vṛkṣamūle vijane vāyatane girau vane vā
children.translated_text: Dwelling anywhere at all, at the root of a tree, in a deserted abode, on a mountain, or in a forest,
I wander without possessions and without expectation, living on whatever alms come, for the sake of the supreme goal.'

children.text: iti paśyata eva rājasūnoridamuktvā sa nabhaḥ samutpapāta
children.translated_text: Having said this while the king's son was still looking on, he rose up into the sky.

children.text: sa hi tadvapuranyabuddhadarśī smṛtaye tasya sameyivāndivaukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a heaven-dweller had come in that form, visible to him but unnoticed by others, for the sake of reminding him.

children.text: gaganaṃ khagavadgate ca tasmin nṛvaraḥ saṃjahṛṣe visismiye ca
children.translated_text: When that being had gone through the sky like a bird, the best of men rejoiced and was amazed.
Then, grasping from that the sign of <s>dharma</s> (truth), he set his mind on the manner of going forth.
Then, like <s>Indra</s>, with the horses of his senses conquered, wishing to enter the city, he mounted his horse.

children.text: parivārajanaṃ tvavekṣamāṇastata evābhimataṃ vanaṃ na bheje ||
children.translated_text: But, looking at the people of his retinue, he did not from that very place seek the forest he desired.

children.text: sa jarāmaraṇakṣayaṃ cikīrṣurvanavāsāya matiṃ smṛtau nidhāya
children.translated_text: Desiring to bring about the destruction of old age and death, and setting his mind in remembrance on dwelling in the forest,

children.text: praviveśa punaḥ puraṃ na kāmādvanabhūmeriva maṇḍalaṃ dvipendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he entered the city again not from desire, like the lord of elephants entering an enclosure from the forest land.

children.text: sukhitā bata nirvṛtā ca sā strī patirīdṛkṣa ihāyatākṣa yasyāḥ
children.translated_text: "Blessed indeed and fulfilled is that woman, O long-eyed one, whose husband here is such as you."

children.text: iti taṃ samudīkṣya rājakanyā praviśantaṃ pathi sāñjalirjagāda ||
children.translated_text: Thus, watching him as he entered, the princess said with joined hands on the road.

children.text: atha ghoṣamimaṃ mahābhraghoṣaḥ pariśuśrāva śamaṃ paraṃ ca lebhe
children.translated_text: Then he, whose voice was like a great cloud, heard this utterance and attained supreme calm.

children.text: śrutavānsa hi nirvṛteti śabdaṃ parinirvāṇavidhau matiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: For, hearing the word <s>nirvṛtā</s> (fulfilled, released), he set his mind on the manner of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final extinction).
Then he whose stature was like the peak of a golden mountain, with elephant-like arms, a cloud-like voice, and bull-like eyes,
whose longing had arisen for the imperishable <s>dharma</s> (truth), and whose face and stride were like the moon and a lion, went to his residence.
Then, with the gait of a lion, he approached the king, who was being attended by groups of ministers,

children.text: samitau marutāmiva jvalantaṃ maghavantaṃ tridive sanatkumāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Sanatkumāra</s> approaching blazing <s>Maghavan</s> in heaven in the assembly of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: praṇipatya ca sāñjalirbabhāṣe diśa mahyaṃ naradeva sādhvanujñām
children.translated_text: Bowing with joined hands, he said, "Grant me proper permission, O lord of men.
I wish to go forth for the sake of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), for separation is fixed for every person."

children.text: iti tasya vaco niśamya rājā kariṇevābhihato drumaścacāla
children.translated_text: Hearing his speech, the king shook like a tree struck by an elephant,
and, taking his lotus-like joined hands, said this with his throat choked by tears.

children.text: pratisaṃhara tāta buddhimetāṃ na hi kālastava dharmasaṃśrayasya
children.translated_text: "Withdraw this thought, dear son; this is not the time for you to take refuge in <s>dharma</s> (religious duty).

children.text: vayasi prathame matau calāyāṃ bahudoṣāṃ hi vadanti dharmacaryām ||
children.translated_text: For they say the practice of <s>dharma</s> (religion) has many faults in the first age of life, when judgment is unsteady.
For one whose senses are curious about sense-objects and whose resolve is not strong enough for the hardships of vows,
the youthful mind, especially when inexperienced in seclusion, turns away from the forest.

children.text: mama tu priyadharma dharmakālastvayi lakṣmīmavasṛjya lakṣmabhūte
children.translated_text: But for me, dear lover of <s>dharma</s>, it is the time for <s>dharma</s>, once I have handed royal fortune over to you, who are the embodiment of fortune.

children.text: sthiravikrama vikrameṇa dharmastava hitvā tu guruṃ bhavedadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O firm in valor, your <s>dharma</s> lies in valor; but if you abandon your father, it would become <s>adharma</s> (wrong).

children.text: tadimaṃ vyavasāyamutsṛja tvaṃ bhava tāvannirato gṛhasthadharme
children.translated_text: Therefore give up this resolve; for now be devoted to the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of a householder.

children.text: puruṣasya vayaḥsukhāni bhuktvā ramaṇīyo hi tapovanapraveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After enjoying the pleasures appropriate to a man's ages, entry into a grove of austerity is fitting."

children.text: iti vākyamidaṃ niśamya rājñaḥ kalaviṅkasvara uttaraṃ babhāṣe
children.translated_text: Hearing this statement of the king, he whose voice was like a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird replied,

children.text: yadi me pratibhūścaturṣu rājan bhavasi tvaṃ na tapovanaṃ śrayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: "If you will be my surety in four matters, O king, I will not resort to the austerity grove.

children.text: na bhavenmaraṇāya jīvitaṃ me viharetsvāsthyamidaṃ ca me na rogaḥ
children.translated_text: Let my life not exist for death, and let this health of mine continue, not disease.

children.text: na ca yauvanamākṣipejjarā me na ca saṃpattimimāṃ haredvipattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let old age not seize my youth, and let misfortune not carry off this prosperity."

children.text: iti durlabham artham ūcivāṃsaṃ tanayaṃ vākyamuvāca śākyarājaḥ
children.translated_text: When his son had stated this hard-to-obtain condition, the <s>Śākya</s> king said in reply,
"Abandon this thought, which has gone too far; excessive longing is laughable and out of proper sequence."

children.text: atha merugururguruṃ babhāṣe yadi nāsti krama eṣa nāsmi vāryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he, weighty as <s>Meru</s>, said to his elder, "If this is not the proper sequence, I am not to be restrained;

children.text: śaraṇājjvalanena dahyamānānna hi niścikramiṣuḥ kṣamaṃ grahītum ||
children.translated_text: for it is not right to hold back one who wishes to escape from a shelter that is being burned by fire.

children.text: jagataśca yadā dhruvo viyogo nanu dharmāya varaṃ svayaṃviyogaḥ
children.translated_text: And when separation from the world is certain, is not self-separation for the sake of <s>dharma</s> better?
Surely death would helplessly separate me while I had not achieved my own aim and remained unsatisfied."

children.text: iti bhūmipatirniśamya tasya vyavasāyaṃ tanayasya nirmumukṣoḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this resolve of his son, who longed for release, the lord of the earth,

children.text: abhidhāya na yāsyatīti bhūyo vidadhe rakṣaṇamuttamāṃśca kāmān ||
children.translated_text: again declared, "He shall not go," and arranged guards and the finest pleasures.
Though the ministers instructed him properly, out of honor and affection and on the basis of śāstra,

children.text: guruṇā ca nivārito 'śrupātaiḥ praviveśāvasathaṃ tataḥ sa śocan ||
children.translated_text: and though his father held him back with falling tears, he then entered his dwelling sorrowing.
With faces kissed by swinging earrings and breasts shaken by deep sighs,
women with restless eyes, like young does, looked up at him.
For he, bright like a golden mountain and causing madness in the hearts of excellent women,
captured their very selves through their ears, limbs, and eyes by the qualities of his speech, touch, and form.

children.text: vigate divase tato vimānaṃ vapuṣā sūrya iva pradīpyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the day had passed, shining with his body like the sun,
he mounted the palace, wishing to destroy darkness with his own radiance, like the sun rising on <s>Meru</s>.
It had golden, blazing lamp-trees and an interior filled with the incense of fine black aloeswood;

children.text: adhiruhya sa vajrabhakticitraṃ pravaraṃ kāñcanamāsanaṃ siṣeve ||
children.translated_text: ascending it, he occupied the excellent golden seat variegated with diamond inlay.
Then, at night, the finest women attended him, who was like <s>Indra</s>, with musical instruments,
like crowds of apsarases attending the son of <s>Kubera</s> on the moon-bright summit of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: paramairapi divyatūryakalpaiḥ sa tu tairnaiva ratiṃ yayau na harṣam
children.translated_text: Yet even with those supreme, divine-like instruments he did not attain delight or joy;

children.text: paramārthasukhāya tasya sādhor abhiniścikramiṣā yato na reme ||
children.translated_text: for, because that holy man wished to go forth toward the happiness of the highest truth, he took no pleasure.
Then there, when the gods, the excellent <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s> foremost in austerity, understood his resolve,
sleep was brought upon the women all at once, and their bodily movements were distorted.

children.text: abhavacchayitā hi tatra kācidviniveśya pracale kare kapolam
children.translated_text: For one woman lay there, placing her cheek upon her trembling hand.
having set aside even her beloved vīṇā, decorated with golden leaf-patterns, which lay in her lap as if sulking.
Another lay asleep, a flute clinging to her hand and her white garment slipped from her breasts;
she shone like a river with lotuses visited by straight rows of bees and with banks laughing in water-foam.
With two arms soft as the heart of fresh lotuses and joined with shining golden armlets,

children.text: svapiti sma tathāparā bhujābhyāṃ parirabhya priyavanmṛdaṅgameva ||
children.translated_text: another slept, clasping a mṛdaṅga as if it were her lover.
So too, other women, adorned with new gold ornaments and wearing unsurpassed yellow garments,
fell helpless under deep sleep, like branches of karṇikāra broken by an elephant.
Another, asleep while leaning on the side of a window, her body-stem bent like a bow,
with a lovely necklace hanging down, shone like a carved <s>śālabhañjikā</s> on an archway.
Likewise another woman's bent lotus-face, its petal-lines marked by jeweled earrings,
appeared like a hundred-petaled lotus with half-curved stem, struck by a resting kāraṇḍava waterfowl.
Others lay just as they had been seated, their bodies bent down by the weight of their breasts;
embracing one another with nooses of arms bright with golden bracelets, they shone beautifully.

children.text: mahatīṃ parivādinīṃ ca kācidvanitāliṅgya sakhīmiva prasuptā
children.translated_text: One woman, asleep, embraced a great parivādinī lute as if it were a female friend;
she tossed about, its golden strings trembling, with her face brightened by disordered earrings.
Another young woman let a paṇava drum, its lovely strap slipped from her shoulder,
fall into the space between her thighs, and lay as if acting the part of a lover wearied at the end of sportive love-play.
Other women, though wide-eyed and though truly lovely-browed, became closed-eyed,
like lotus-plants whose lotus buds contract when the sun has set.
So too another lay with loosened, tangled hair, her ornaments and garment slipped from her hips,
her necklaces scattered, like a statue-woman broken by an elephant.
Still others, helpless and stripped of modesty, though self-possessed and endowed with bodily charms,

children.text: viniśaśvasurulbaṇaṃ śayānā vikṛtāḥ kṣiptabhūjā jajṛmbhire ca ||
children.translated_text: lay distorted, sighed heavily, flung out their arms, and yawned.
Others, unconscious, with ornaments and garlands cast off and the fastenings of their new clothes loosened,
lay with unblinking, white, motionless eyes; they did not shine, looking almost lifeless.
Another lay with her mouth gaping, limbs spread wide, saliva falling from her mouth, and private parts exposed;

children.text: aparā madaghūrṇiteva śiśye na babhāse vikṛtaṃ vapuḥ pupoṣa ||
children.translated_text: as if reeling with intoxication, she had no beauty and showed a distorted body.

children.text: iti sattvakulānvayānurūpaṃ vividhaṃ sa pramadājanaḥ śayānaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that company of women, sleeping in varied ways according to their nature, family, and lineage,
had the appearance of a pond whose lotuses have been bent and broken by the wind.

children.text: samavekṣya tathā tathā śayānā vikṛtāstā yuvatīradhīraceṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those young women lying in those various ways, distorted and uncontrolled in movement,
the king's son began to condemn them, though their bodies were beautiful and their speech charming.
'In the living world, this is the nature of women: unclean and distorted in just this way.
Yet a man, deceived by garments and ornaments, comes to passion in the sphere of women.

children.text: vimṛśedyadi yoṣitāṃ manuṣyaḥ prakṛtiṃ svapnavikāramīdṛśaṃ ca
children.translated_text: If a person were to consider women's nature and this alteration that comes in sleep,
surely he would not foster heedlessness here; but, struck down by imagining their virtues, he comes to passion.'

children.text: iti tasya tadantaraṃ viditvā niśi niścikramiṣā samudbabhūva
children.translated_text: Thus, after he had understood this truth, the wish to depart arose in him during the night;
then, when the gods understood his mind, the door of the palace stood open.
Then, condemning those young women as they slept, he descended from the palace roof;

children.text: avatīrya tataśca nirviśaṅko gṛhakakṣyāṃ prathamāṃ vinirjagāma ||
children.translated_text: and after descending from there, free from hesitation, he went out into the first court of the house.
Awakening the swift horse-attendant <s>Chandaka</s>, he spoke to him as follows:

children.text: hayamānaya kanthakaṃ tvarāvānamṛtaṃ prāptumito 'dya me yiyāsā ||
children.translated_text: 'Bring the horse <s>Kanthaka</s> quickly; today I wish to go from here to attain <s>amṛta</s>, the deathless state.

children.text: hṛdi yā mama tuṣṭiradya jātā vyavasāyaśca yathā matau niviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: The gladness that has arisen in my heart today, and the resolve fixed in my thought,

children.text: vijane 'pi ca nāthavānivāsmi dhruvamartho 'bhimukhaḥ sameta iṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the fact that even alone I seem to have a protector, make it certain that my desired goal has come toward me.

children.text: hriyameva ca saṃnatiṃ ca hitvā śayitā matpramukhe yathā yuvatyaḥ
children.translated_text: Since the young women lay before me after abandoning modesty and decorum,

children.text: vivṛte ca yathā svayaṃ kapāṭe niyataṃ yātumato mamādya kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and since the door-leaves opened by themselves, surely today is the appointed time for me to go.'

children.text: pratigṛhya tataḥ sa bharturājñāṃ viditārtho 'pi narendraśāsanasya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Chandaka</s> received his master's command, though he knew the meaning of the king's injunction;
as if urged in his mind by another power, he set his intention on bringing the horse.
Then he brought to his master that excellent horse, its mouth filled with a golden bit and its back covered with a light cloth,
endowed with strength, spirit, speed, and noble breed.
It had well-extended croup, tail-root, and hindquarters, and close, short body-hair, tail, and ears;
its back, belly, and flanks were properly curved and raised, and its muzzle, forehead, loins, and chest were broad.

children.text: upaguhya sa taṃ viśālavakṣāḥ kamalābhena ca sāntvayan kareṇa
children.translated_text: The broad-chested prince embraced him and soothed him with a lotus-like hand;
with sweet-syllabled speech he instructed him, as if wishing to enter the middle of an army.

children.text: bahuśaḥ kila śatravo nirastāḥ samare tvāmadhiruhya pārthivena
children.translated_text: 'Many times, it is said, enemies have been driven off in battle by the king after mounting you.
May I too, best of horses, rightly attain the deathless state; bring that about.

children.text: sulabhāḥ khalu saṃyuge sahāyā viṣayāvāptasukhe dhanārjane vā
children.translated_text: Helpers are indeed easy to find in battle, in the pleasure of gaining sense-objects, or in acquiring wealth;

children.text: puruṣasya tu durlabhāḥ sahāyāḥ patitasyāpadi dharmasaṃśraye vā ||
children.translated_text: but for a man fallen into danger, or seeking refuge in <s>dharma</s>, helpers are hard to find.'

children.text: iha caiva bhavanti ye sahāyaḥ kaluṣe karmaṇi dharmasaṃśraye vā
children.translated_text: And those here who become helpers in a stained action or in one supported by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: avagacchati me yathāntarātmā niyataṃ te 'pi janāstadaṃśabhājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as my inner self understands, those people too certainly share in that portion.

children.text: tadidaṃ parigamya dharmayuktaṃ mama niryāṇamito jagaddhitāya
children.translated_text: Therefore, having understood this departure of mine from here, joined with <s>dharma</s> and made for the welfare of the world,
O best of horses, exert yourself with speed and strength for your own welfare and for the welfare of the world.

children.text: iti suhṛdamivānuśiṣya kṛtye turagavaraṃ nṛvaro vanaṃ yiyāsuḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the best of horses, like a friend, in the task to be done, the lordly prince, wishing to go to the forest,
mounted the white horse, splendid in form, like the sun mounting an autumn cloud.

children.text: atha sa pariharanniśīthacaṇḍaṃ parijanabodhakaraṃ dhvaniṃ sadaśvaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that good horse, avoiding in the depth of night the fierce sound that would awaken the attendants,
went on with the noise of his jaws gone, his neighing calmed, and his steps set down cautiously.
Then, with forearms adorned by golden bracelets and with lotus-like hands, as though touching lotuses,
the <s>Yakṣas</s>, their bodies bent low, held his hooves on the tips of their hands as he moved in alarm.

children.text: guruparighakapāṭasaṃvṛtā yā na sukhamapi dviradair apāvriyante
children.translated_text: The city gates, shut with heavy bars and door panels, which could not easily be opened even by elephants,

children.text: vrajati nṛpasute gatasvanāstāḥ svayamabhavanvivṛtāḥ puraḥ pratolyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became open of themselves, without a sound, before the king's son as he went forth.

children.text: pitaramabhimukhaṃ sutaṃ ca bālaṃ janamanuraktamanuttamāṃ ca lakṣmīm
children.translated_text: Leaving behind his father, his little son, the devoted people, and unsurpassed royal fortune,
he, resolved in mind and without dependence, then went out from his father's city.

children.text: atha sa vimalapaṅkajāyatākṣaḥ puramavalokya nanāda siṃhanādam
children.translated_text: Then he, whose eyes were long like stainless lotuses, looked back at the city and uttered a lion's roar:
"Without having seen the far shore of birth and death, I shall not enter the city called <s>Kapila</s>."

children.text: iti vacanamidaṃ niśamya tasya draviṇapateḥ pariṣadgaṇā nananduḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of his, the assembled hosts of the lord of wealth rejoiced,
and the companies of gods, delighted in mind, wished him the fulfillment of his resolved vow.
Other heaven-dwellers, fire-like in form, knowing his undertaking to be exceedingly hard,

children.text: akṛṣata tuhine pathi prakāśaṃ ghanavivaraprasṛtā ivendupādāḥ ||
children.translated_text: drew light along the dewy path, like moonbeams issuing through a break in the clouds.
That horse, like the horse of <s>Hari</s>, moving as if urged on by thought itself,

children.text: aruṇaparuṣatāram antarikṣaṃ sa ca subahūni jagāma yojanāni ||
children.translated_text: traveled through the dawn-reddened, star-marked sky for many <s>yojanas</s> (leagues).

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'bhiniṣkramaṇo nāma pañcamaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, ends the fifth canto, named "The Going Forth."
Then, when the sun, the eye of the world, had risen for a short while,
that best of men saw the hermitage grounds of <s>Bhārgava</s>.
Seeing it, where the deer slept in trust and the birds stood at ease,

children.text: viśrānta iva yaddṛṣṭvā kṛtārtha iva cābhavat ||
children.translated_text: he became as if rested and as if his purpose had been accomplished.
To bring an end to wonder, and also for the honoring of austerity,
while preserving his own proper conduct, he descended from the horse's back.
Having descended, he touched the horse, as if thinking, "I have crossed over,"
and joyfully spoke to <s>Chandaka</s>, as though bathing him with his eyes.
By following this horse, whose speed is like that of <s>Tārkṣya</s>,
O gentle one, you have shown your devotion to me and this valor of your own.
In every way, even though I had another aim, you have held me in your heart,
for such is your affection for your master, and such too is your strength.
One without affection may be capable, and one without capability may be devoted;
but one who is both devoted and capable, like you, is hard to find on earth.
Therefore I am pleased with this very noble deed of yours,

children.text: yasya te mayi bhāvo 'yaṃ phalebhyo 'pi parāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since this feeling of yours toward me turns away even from rewards.

children.text: ko janasya phalasthasya na syādabhimukho janaḥ
children.translated_text: What person would not be favorable to a man who stands amid the fruits of success?
In adversity, even one's own kinsman most often becomes a stranger.

children.text: kulārthaṃ dhāryate putraḥ poṣārthaṃ sevyate pitā
children.translated_text: A son is maintained for the sake of the family; a father is served for the sake of support.
The world clings because of expectation; there is no natural kinship without a cause.
What is the use of saying much? In brief, you have done me a very great kindness.
Turn back, taking the horse; I have reached the place I wished for.
Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one, wishing to show compassion,
took off his ornaments and gave them to him, whose mind was distressed.
Taking from his crown the blazing jewel that served as a lamp,
he stood speaking these words, like <s>Mandara</s> with the sun upon it:

children.text: anena maṇinā chanda praṇamya bahuśo nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: "With this jewel, <s>Chanda</s>, after bowing many times to the king,
he should be informed with confidence unbroken, so that his sorrow may cease:
'I have entered the ascetic grove for the destruction of birth and death,

children.text: na khalu svargatarṣeṇa nāsnehena na manyunā ||
children.translated_text: not from thirst for heaven, nor from lack of affection, nor from anger.

children.text: tad evam abhiniṣkrāntaṃ na māṃ śocitumarhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore you should not grieve for me, who have gone forth in this way;

children.text: bhūtvāpi hi ciraṃ śleṣaḥ kālena na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for even if union has lasted a long time, in time it will no longer exist.
And since separation is certain, my thought is therefore set on liberation;

children.text: viprayogaḥ kathaṃ na syād bhūyo 'pi svajanāditi ||
children.translated_text: for how could separation from one's own people not occur again?'
"You should not grieve for me, who have gone forth for the abandonment of grief;
rather, passionate people attached to pleasures, the causes of grief, are the ones to be pitied.

children.text: ayaṃ ca kila pūrveṣāmasmākaṃ niścayaḥ sthiraḥ
children.translated_text: And this, it is said, was the firm resolve of our ancestors;

children.text: iti dāyādyabhūtena na śocyo 'smi pathā vrajan ||
children.translated_text: going on a path that has become my inheritance, I am not to be mourned.
For in adversity men may have heirs to wealth,

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ dharmadāyādāḥ durlabhāstu na santi vā ||
children.translated_text: but heirs to <s>dharma</s> on earth are rare, or else they do not exist at all.
Even if it should be said, 'He has gone to the forest at the wrong time,'

children.text: akālo nāsti dharmasya jīvite cañcale sati ||
children.translated_text: there is no wrong time for <s>dharma</s>, when life is unsteady.
Therefore my resolve is that today itself the highest good must be sought by me;

children.text: jīvite ko hi viśrambho mṛtyau pratyarthini sthite ||
children.translated_text: for what confidence can there be in life, when death stands present as an adversary?"
In these and similar words, dear one, the lord of the earth should be informed by you,

children.text: prayatethāstathā caiva yathā māṃ na smared api ||
children.translated_text: and strive also in such a way that he may not even remember me.
You should even speak of my lack of virtue before the king;
through lack of virtue affection is abandoned, and when affection is abandoned one is not grieved.
Hearing this speech, <s>Chanda</s>, shaken by anguish,
replied with folded hands, in a voice choked with tears:
By this intention of yours, which brings distress to your kinsmen,

children.text: bhartaḥ sīdati me ceto nadīpaṅka iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my lord, my mind sinks like an elephant in river mud.
Whose tears would this resolve of yours, such as it is, not cause to arise,
even in a heart made of iron, much more in one bewildered by affection?
Where is this delicacy, fit for a couch in a palace,
and where is the ground of an ascetic grove, covered with sharp shoots of darbha grass?

children.text: śrutvā tu vyavasāyaṃ te yadaśvo 'yaṃ mayāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: As for this horse having been brought by me when I heard your resolve,
that, lord, I was made to do by force, indeed by fate itself.
For how, being under my own control and knowing this purpose of yours,
could I have brought the horse that would be the grief of <s>Kapilavāstu</s>?
Therefore, mighty-armed one, you ought not abandon the old king, longing for his son,

children.text: snigdhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca rājānaṃ saddharmamiva nāstikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: loving and aged, as an unbeliever abandons true <s>dharma</s>.
Nor should you forget that second mother, exhausted by bringing you up,

children.text: devīṃ nārhasi vismartuṃ kṛtaghna iva satkriyām ||
children.translated_text: the queen, as an ungrateful man forgets a good service.
You ought not abandon the lady who has a young son, who is virtuous, praised by her family, and devoted to her husband,

children.text: devīmarhasi na tyaktuṃ klībaḥ prāptāmiva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: as a coward abandons fortune when it has come to him.
You ought not abandon your son, the child of <s>Yaśodharā</s>, praiseworthy and best among bearers of fame and virtue,
still a child, as a man lost in vice abandons the highest fame.

children.text: atha bandhuṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tyaktumeva kṛtā matiḥ
children.translated_text: But if your mind is firmly set on abandoning both kinsmen and kingdom,

children.text: māṃ nārhasi vibho tyaktuṃ tvatpādau hi gatirmama ||
children.translated_text: you ought not abandon me, lord, for your feet are my refuge.

children.text: nāsmi yātuṃ puraṃ śakto dahyamānena cetasā
children.translated_text: I am not able to go to the city with my mind burning,
after leaving you in the forest, like <s>Sumantra</s> leaving <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: kiṃ hi vakṣyati māṃ rājā tvadṛte nagaraṃ gatam
children.translated_text: For what will the king say to me when I have gone to the city without you?
And what shall I say to the women of your inner palace, accustomed to seeing you?
And as for what you said, that lack of virtue should be spoken of before the king,
how shall I say that false thing of you, faultless as a sage?
Even if, with a bashful heart and a faltering tongue,
I were somehow to say it, who could believe it?
For a man who would describe, or believe in, the moon's fierceness
would describe, or believe in, your faults, O discerner of faults.
For one who is always compassionate, ever sensitive to pity,

children.text: snigdhatyāgo na sadṛśo nivartasva prasīda me ||
children.translated_text: abandoning those who love you is not fitting; turn back and be gracious to me.
Hearing this speech of <s>Chanda</s>, who was overcome by grief,

children.text: svasthaḥ paramayā dhṛtyā jagāda vadatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of speakers, composed with supreme firmness, said:
Regarding separation from me, <s>Chanda</s>, let this distress be abandoned;
for separation is surely fixed among embodied beings born in different lots.
Even if, from affection, I myself were not to abandon my own people,
death will make us, helpless, abandon one another.
She by whom I was borne in the womb, with great longing and with pains,

children.text: tasyā niṣphalayatnāyāḥ kvāhaṃ mātuḥ kva sā mama ||
children.translated_text: that mother whose efforts have borne no fruit: where am I, and where is she for me?
As birds come together on a tree for lodging and then fly apart,
so the meeting of beings inevitably ends in separation.

children.text: sametya ca yathā bhūyo vyapayānti balāhakāḥ
children.translated_text: And as clouds, having come together, again drift apart,

children.text: saṃyogo viprayogaśca tathā me prāṇināṃ mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so do I regard the union and separation of living beings.
Since this world passes on, each one deceiving another,
possessiveness is therefore not fitting in a meeting that is like a dream.
Trees are separated from the leaf-color that is born together with them;
how then will the separation of one being from another not occur?

children.text: tadevaṃ sati saṃtāpaṃ mā kārṣīḥ saumya gamyatām
children.translated_text: Therefore, since this is so, do not make grief for yourself, dear one; go.

children.text: lambate yadi tu sneho gatvāpi punarāvraja ||
children.translated_text: But if affection still clings, come back again even after going.
And tell the people in <s>Kapilavāstu</s> who are anxious on my account:

children.text: tyajyatāṃ tadgataḥ snehaḥ śrūyatāṃ cāsya niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let their affection directed toward me be abandoned, and let this resolve of mine be heard.
Either, having brought birth and death to an end, he will surely come quickly,
or, with his aim unaccomplished and his undertaking unfinished, he will go to death.
Hearing his words, <s>Kanthaka</s>, the best of horses,

children.text: jihvayā lilihe pādau bāṣpamuṣṇaṃ mumoca ca ||
children.translated_text: licked his feet with his tongue and shed hot tears.
With his hand, webbed, marked with a svastika, and bearing a wheel at its center,
the prince stroked him and spoke to him as to a friend:

children.text: muñca kanthaka mā bāṣpaṃ darśiteyaṃ sadaśvatā
children.translated_text: Let it go, <s>Kanthaka</s>; do not weep. Your excellence as a good horse has been shown.
Endure it; this effort of yours will soon become fruitful.

children.text: maṇitsaruṃ chandakahastasaṃsthaṃ tataḥ sa dhīro niśitaṃ gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: Then the steadfast one took the sharp sword, with a jeweled hilt, that rested in <s>Chandaka</s>'s hand,
and drew it from its sheath, bright with golden fittings, like a venomous serpent from a hole.

children.text: niṣkāsya taṃ cotpalapattranīlaṃ cicheda citraṃ mukuṭaṃ sakeśam
children.translated_text: Having drawn out that blade, blue like a lotus petal, he cut off his splendid diadem together with his hair,
and, its cloth streamers scattering in the air, he threw it up like a swan into a lake.

children.text: pūjābhilāṣeṇa ca bāhumānyād divaukasastaṃ jagṛhuḥ praviddham
children.translated_text: Out of desire to worship it and from great respect, the dwellers in heaven caught it as it was thrown,

children.text: yathāvadenaṃ divi devasaṅghā divyairviśeṣair mahayāṃ ca cakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in heaven the hosts of gods honored it properly with divine distinctions.
But after casting off the state of having ornaments and a wife, and making his head exiled from splendor,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāṃśukaṃ kāñcanahaṃsacihnaṃ vanyaṃ sa dhīro 'bhicakāṅkṣa vāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the steadfast one, seeing his garment marked with golden haṃsas, longed for forest clothing.

children.text: tato mṛgavyādhavapur divaukā bhāvaṃ viditvāsya viśuddhabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a heaven-dweller in the form of a deer-hunter, pure in disposition, knowing his intention,
approached him wearing an ochre robe; the descendant of the <s>Śākya</s> king addressed him:

children.text: śivaṃ ca kāṣāyamṛṣidhvajaste na yujyate hiṃsramidaṃ dhanuśca
children.translated_text: "Your ochre robe, the auspicious banner of seers, does not fit with this cruel bow.

children.text: tatsaumya yadyasti na saktiratra mahyaṃ prayacchedamidaṃ gṛhāṇa ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, if you have no attachment to it, give this to me and take this one."
The hunter said, "O granter of wishes, with this I gain the trust of deer at close range and kill them.

children.text: arthastu śakropama yadyanena hanta pratīcchānaya śuklametat ||
children.translated_text: But if you have a use for it, O one like <s>Śakra</s>, then take it, and hand over that white garment."

children.text: pareṇa harṣeṇa tataḥ sa vanyaṃ jagrāha vāso 'ṃśukamutsasarja
children.translated_text: Then with supreme joy he took the forest garment and gave up his fine cloth.

children.text: vyādhastu divyaṃ vapureva bibhrattacchuklamādāya divaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: But the hunter, displaying his celestial body, took that white garment and went to heaven.

children.text: tataḥ kumāraśca sa cāśvagopastasmiṃstathā yāti visismiyāte
children.translated_text: Then the prince and the keeper of the horse were amazed as he went in that way,

children.text: āraṇyake vāsasi caiva bhūyas tasminnakārṣṭāṃ bahumānamāśu ||
children.translated_text: and at once they felt still greater reverence for that forest robe.
Then, dismissing tear-faced <s>Chanda</s>, he, his courage and glory strengthened by the ochre robe,
the great-souled one went toward the hermitage, like the moon wrapped in twilight clouds.

children.text: tatastathā bhartari rājyaniḥspṛhe tapovanaṃ yāti vivarṇavāsasi
children.translated_text: Then, as his master, indifferent to kingship and clad in a faded garment, went to the ascetic grove,

children.text: bhujau samutkṣipya tataḥ sa vājibhṛd bhṛśaṃ vicukrośa papāta ca kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: the keeper of the steed raised both arms, cried out violently, and fell to the ground.

children.text: vilokya bhūyaśca ruroda sasvaraṃ hayaṃ bhujābhyāmupaguhya kanthakam
children.translated_text: Looking back again, he wept aloud, embracing the horse <s>Kanthaka</s> with both arms;

children.text: tato nirāśo vilapan muhurmuhur yayau śarīreṇa puraṃ na cetasā ||
children.translated_text: then, hopeless and lamenting again and again, he went to the city in body, but not in mind.

children.text: kvacitpradadhyau vilalāpa ca kvacit kvacit pracaskhāla papāta ca kvacit
children.translated_text: At times he pondered, at times he lamented; at times he stumbled, and at times he fell.

children.text: ato vrajan bhaktivaśena duḥkhitaścacāra bahvīr avaśaḥ pathi kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going from there, grieved and under the power of devotion, he helplessly performed many actions along the road.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye chandakanivartano nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, ends the sixth canto, named "The Turning Back of <s>Chandaka</s>."

children.text: tato visṛjyāśrumukhaṃ rudantaṃ chandaṃ vanacchandatayā nirāsthaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, free from attachment because his desire was for the forest, having dismissed weeping, tear-faced <s>Chanda</s>,

children.text: sarvārthasiddho vapuṣābhibhūya tamāśramaṃ siddha iva prapede ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, overwhelming others by his beauty, entered that hermitage like a <s>siddha</s> (perfected being).
That king's son, moving with the gait of a lion, entered the deer-ground like a deer,
and, though parted from royal splendor, he seized the eyes of all the hermits by the splendor of his body.
Those with yokes in their hands, and likewise wheel-bearers with their wives, stood still from curiosity;
they looked at him, like <s>Indra</s>, and did not move on, like draught-beasts with heads half-lowered.
And Brahmins who had gone outside for firewood returned with fuel-sticks, flowers, and sacred grasses in their hands;
though austerity was their chief concern and their minds were disciplined, they went to see him and did not go to their huts.
Delighted peacocks cried out, rising up as if they had seen a dark rain-cloud,
and the restless-eyed deer, forest-roamers, left the young grass and stood facing him.
Seeing that lamp of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line, blazing like the rising sun,
the cows that gave milk for oblations, filled with joy, let milk flow even after the milking had been done.
"Could this be the eighth of the <s>Vasus</s>, or one of the <s>Aśvins</s> fallen from heaven?"
Such loud words arose there among the sages, born of wonder at seeing him.
Like a second body of the lordly mountain, like the radiance of the moving and unmoving world,

children.text: sa dyotayāmāsa vanaṃ hi kṛtsnaṃ yadṛcchayā sūrya ivāvatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he lit up the entire forest, as if the sun had descended there by chance.
Then, duly honored and invited by those hermitage-dwellers,
he in turn honored the upholders of <s>dharma</s> (religious discipline) with a voice like a rain-cloud full of water.

children.text: kīrṇaṃ tathā puṇyakṛtā janena svargābhikāmena vimokṣakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Desiring liberation, he walked through that hermitage, crowded with merit-making people who desired heaven,
that steadfast one observing the varied austerities.
Having observed the forms of austerity among those rich in austerity there in the ascetic grove, the gentle one,
wishing to know the truth, spoke this to a certain ascetic who was walking beside him:

children.text: tatpūrvamadyāśramadarśanaṃ me yasmādimaṃ dharmavidhiṃ na jāne
children.translated_text: "Since today is my first sight of a hermitage, and I do not know this rule of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tasmādbhavānarhati bhāṣituṃ me yo niścayo yatprati vaḥ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore you should tell me what settled aim it is toward which you are engaged."
Then that twice-born ascetic, living in austerity, spoke to the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, whose stride was like a bull's,

children.text: krameṇa tasmai kathayāṃcakāra tapoviśeṣāṃstapasaḥ phalaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and explained to him in order the different kinds of austerity and the fruit of austerity.

children.text: agrāmyamannaṃ salile prarūḍhaṃ parṇāni toyaṃ phalamūlameva
children.translated_text: Uncultivated food, what grows in water, leaves, water, and fruits and roots alone,

children.text: yathāgamaṃ vṛttiriyaṃ munīnāṃ bhinnāstu te te tapasāṃ vikalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: according to tradition, are the livelihood of sages; but the particular alternatives of austerity are many and various.

children.text: uñchena jīvanti khagā ivānye tṛṇāni kecinmṛgavaccaranti
children.translated_text: Some live by gleaning like birds; some graze on grasses like deer.
Some, become like anthills, sustain themselves on the forest wind together with snakes.
Others have a livelihood gained by effort with stones; some eat food crushed by their own teeth.

children.text: kṛtvā parārthaṃ śrapaṇaṃ tathānye kurvanti kāryaṃ yadi śeṣamasti ||
children.translated_text: And others, after cooking for another's sake, attend to their own need only if something remains.
Some, with masses of matted hair wet with water, twice offer into the fire with mantras,

children.text: mīnaiḥ samaṃ kecid apo vigāhya vasanti kūrmollikhitaiḥ śarīraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: while some plunge into the waters and live among fish, their bodies scratched by turtles.
By such austerities, accumulated over time, some go to heaven and others to the human world;

children.text: duḥkhena mārgeṇa sukhaṃ hyupaiti sukhaṃ hi dharmasya vadanti mūlam ||
children.translated_text: for by a painful path one reaches happiness, and they say that happiness is the basis of <s>dharma</s>.
Having heard these and similar words of that ascetic rich in austerity, the young prince, son of the lord of men,

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvo 'pi na saṃtutoṣa śanairidaṃ cātmagataṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: Even though he had not seen the truth there, he was not satisfied, and softly spoke this within himself:

children.text: duḥkhātmakaṃ naikavidhaṃ tapaśca svargapradhānaṃ tapasaḥ phalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>tapas</s> (ascetic practice) is manifold and made of suffering, and the fruit of tapas is chiefly heaven;

children.text: lokāśca sarve pariṇāmavantaḥ svalpe śramaḥ khalvayamāśramāṇām ||
children.translated_text: yet all worlds are subject to change, so this toil of the hermitages is indeed for a small reward.

children.text: priyāṃśca bandhūnviṣayāṃśca hitvā ye svargahetorniyamaṃ caranti
children.translated_text: Those who abandon dear kinsmen and objects of sense and practice restraint for the sake of heaven,

children.text: te viprayuktāḥ khalu gantukāmā mahattaraṃ bandhanameva bhūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they, after becoming separated, are indeed eager to go again into a still greater bondage.
And whoever, by bodily hardships under the name of tapas, seeks renewed becoming for the sake of desire,
not examining the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), seeks only suffering by means of suffering.

children.text: trāsaśca nityaṃ maraṇātprajānāṃ yatnena cecchanti punaḥprasūtim
children.translated_text: Creatures are always terrified of death, yet with effort they desire birth again;

children.text: satyāṃ pravṛttau niyataśca mṛtyustatraiva magnā yata eva bhītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when becoming is real, death is inevitable; they are sunk in the very thing from which they are afraid.
Some enter hardship for the sake of gain here; others undertake toil for the sake of heaven;
seeking happiness, wretched with hope and unfulfilled, the world of living beings falls into misfortune.

children.text: na khalvayaṃ garhita eva yatno yo hīnam utsṛjya viśeṣagāmī
children.translated_text: This effort is not wholly to be blamed, when it abandons the lower and moves toward something higher;

children.text: prājñaiḥ samānena pariśrameṇa kāryaṃ tu tadyatra punarna kāryam ||
children.translated_text: but with the same exertion the wise should do that work after which no work remains to be done.

children.text: śarīrapīḍā tu yadīha dharmaḥ sukhaṃ śarīrasya bhavatyadharmaḥ
children.translated_text: But if bodily pain here is <s>dharma</s> (merit), then bodily pleasure becomes <s>adharma</s> (wrong);

children.text: dharmeṇa cāpnoti sukhaṃ paratra tasmādadharmaṃ phalatīha dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and since by dharma one obtains happiness hereafter, dharma here would bear fruit as adharma.

children.text: yataḥ śarīraṃ manaso vaśena pravartate cāpi nivartate ca
children.translated_text: Since the body acts and also ceases to act under the control of the mind,

children.text: yukto damaścetasa eva tasmāccittādṛte kāṣṭhasamaṃ śarīram ||
children.translated_text: discipline of the mind alone is therefore fitting; without thought, the body is like a log.
If merit is desired through purity of food, then deer too possess merit,

children.text: ye cāpi bāhyāḥ puruṣāḥ phalebhyo bhāgyāparādhena parāṅmukhārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and so do outsiders among men, whose purposes, through failure of fortune, are turned away from fruit.

children.text: duḥkhe 'bhisaṃdhistvatha puṇyahetuḥ sukhe 'pi kāryo nanu so 'bhisaṃdhiḥ
children.translated_text: But if an intention toward pain is the cause of merit, then surely that intention should also be applied even in pleasure;

children.text: atha pramāṇaṃ na sukhe 'bhisaṃdhirduḥkhe pramāṇaṃ nanu nābhisaṃdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but if intention in pleasure is no criterion, then surely intention in pain is no criterion either.

children.text: tathaiva ye karmaviśuddhihetoḥ spṛśanty apas tīrthamiti pravṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise those who, for the sake of purifying karma, set out to touch waters, thinking, 'This is a <s>tīrtha</s>,'

children.text: tatrāpi toṣo hṛdi kevalo 'yaṃ na pāvayiṣyanti hi pāpamāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there too this is only satisfaction in the heart, for waters will not purify sin.
For if whatever water has been touched by the virtuous is regarded as a <s>tīrtha</s> on earth,
then I consider virtues alone to be the <s>tīrtha</s>; waters are, without doubt, simply waters.

children.text: iti sma tattadbahuyuktiyuktaṃ jagāda cāstaṃ ca yayau vivasvān
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke, furnished with many arguments about each matter, and <s>Vivasvān</s> (the Sun) set;

children.text: tato havirdhūmavivarṇavṛkṣaṃ tapaḥpraśāntaṃ sa vanaṃ viveśa ||
children.translated_text: then he entered the forest, its trees discolored by the smoke of oblations, peaceful with austerity.
There the blazing <s>agnihotra</s> fires had been raised up, and it was filled with seers who had performed their ablutions;
its shrines resounded with the murmur of recitation, as if it were the active workshop of <s>dharma</s>.
There, moon-like, he stayed for several nights, examining the austerities;
after fully considering and assessing every austerity, he went away from that ground of ascetic practice.
Then the hermitage-dwellers followed him, their minds absorbed in the majesty of his form,
like great seers following <s>dharma</s> as it departs from a land being overcome by ignoble men.
Then he looked at those ascetics, rich in tapas, with matted hair, bark garments, and ragged cloth;
and, honoring their austerities, he stood at the root of an auspicious, beautiful tree.
Then the residents of the hermitage approached that best of men and stood surrounding him;

children.text: vṛddhaśca teṣāṃ bahumānapūrvaṃ kalena sāmnā giramityuvāca ||
children.translated_text: and their elder, with reverence, spoke these words in a gentle, conciliatory voice:

children.text: tvayyāgate pūrṇa ivāśramo 'bhūt sampadyate śūnya eva prayāte
children.translated_text: When you came, the hermitage became as though full; when you go, it becomes empty.
Therefore, dear one, you ought not to leave it, as one who wishes to live ought not to leave the beloved life in his body.

children.text: brahmarṣirājarṣisurarṣijuṣṭaḥ puṇyaḥ samīpe himavān hi śailaḥ
children.translated_text: For nearby is the holy mountain <s>Himavān</s>, frequented by brahman-seers, royal seers, and divine seers;
through its nearness, these austerities of the ascetics become greatly increased.
Likewise, holy <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) all around are like stairways to the expanse of heaven;
they are frequented by righteous, self-possessed men, and by divine seers and great seers.
Moreover, from here the northern direction alone is more fit to be served for the sake of a higher dharma;

children.text: na tu kṣamaṃ dakṣiṇato budhena padaṃ bhavedekamapi prayātum ||
children.translated_text: but it is not fit for a wise man to take even a single step southward.
Or if in this ascetic grove you have seen someone inactive, fallen into confused observance, or impure,

children.text: dṛṣṭastvayā yena na te vivatsā tadbrūhi yāvadrucito 'stu vāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of whom you do not wish to dwell here, say so, so that your residence may be as you like.

children.text: ime hi vāñchanti tapaḥsahāyaṃ taponidhānapratimaṃ bhavantam
children.translated_text: For these men desire you as a companion in tapas, you who are like a treasury of austerity;
dwelling together with you, equal to <s>Indra</s>, would bring prosperity even to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
When this had been said among the ascetics by the foremost ascetic,

children.text: bhavapraṇāśāya kṛtapratijñaḥ svaṃ bhāvam antargatam ācacakṣe ||
children.translated_text: the foremost of sages, vowed to the destruction of becoming, disclosed his own inner disposition.
By upright-minded sages who uphold <s>dharma</s>, to whom a guest is dear and who are like kinsmen,

children.text: evaṃvidhairmā prati bhāvajātaiḥ prītiḥ parā me janitaśca mānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through such feelings toward me, supreme joy has been produced in me, and respect as well.
With these affectionate, pleasing, heart-reaching words, in brief, I am as if bathed;

children.text: ratiśca me dharmanavagrahasya vispanditā saṃprati bhūya eva ||
children.translated_text: and my delight, as one newly undertaking <s>dharma</s>, has now been stirred still more.
You, being thus disposed, offering refuge, and showing me such marked favor,

children.text: yāsyāmi hitveti mamāpi duḥkhaṃ yathaiva bandhūṃstyajatastathaiva ||
children.translated_text: The thought, "I shall go, leaving [this]," is painful for me too, just as it was when I left my kinsmen.
But this <s>dharma</s> of yours is for heaven; my longing, however, is for non-rebirth.

children.text: asminvane yena na me vivatsā bhinnaḥ pravṛttyā hi nivṛttidharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason I do not wish to dwell in this forest; for the <s>dharma</s> of cessation is different from that of active engagement.

children.text: tannāratirme na parāpacāro vanādito yena parivrajāmi
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not dislike on my part, nor an insult to others, because of which I wander forth from this forest.

children.text: dharme sthitāḥ pūrvayugānurūpe sarve bhavanto hi maharṣikalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For all of you, like great seers, stand in a <s>dharma</s> corresponding to the ancient age.

children.text: tato vacaḥ sūnṛtamarthavacca suślakṣṇam ojasvi ca garvitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the prince's speech, truthful, meaningful, well-polished, powerful, and confident,
those ascetics came to a special and profound esteem for him.

children.text: kaściddvijastatra tu bhasmaśāyī prāṃśuḥ śikhī dāravacīravāsāḥ
children.translated_text: But a certain twice-born man there, who slept on ashes, tall, wearing a topknot and bark-cloth garments,
tawny-eyed, with a thin long nose and a pot in one hand, spoke these words:

children.text: dhīmannudāraḥ khalu niścayaste yastvaṃ yuvā janmani dṛṣṭadoṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "O wise one, your resolve is indeed noble, since you, though young, have seen the faults in birth.

children.text: svargāpavargau hi vicārya samyagyasyāpavarge matirasti so 'sti ||
children.translated_text: For, after considering heaven and release correctly, the man whose mind is set on release is truly a man.

children.text: yajñaistapobhirniyamaiśca taistaiḥ svargaṃ yiyāsanti hi rāgavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Those possessed of passion wish to go to heaven by sacrifices, austerities, and various restraints;

children.text: rāgeṇa sārdhaṃ ripuṇeva yuddhvā mokṣaṃ parīpsanti tu sattvavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but men of true spirit, having fought with passion as with an enemy, seek <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: tadbuddhireṣā yadi niścitā te tūrṇaṃ bhavān gacchatu vindhyakoṣṭham
children.translated_text: Therefore, if this intention of yours is settled, let your honor go quickly to <s>Vindhyakoṣṭha</s>.

children.text: asau munistatra vasatyarāḍo yo naiṣṭhike śreyasi labdhacakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the sage <s>Arāḍa</s> lives, who has gained vision in the final good.

children.text: tasmādbhavāñchroṣyati tattvamārgaṃ satyāṃ rucau sampratipatsyate ca
children.translated_text: From him your honor will hear the path of truth, and, if your inclination is sincere, you will understand it.

children.text: yathā tu paśyāmi matistathaiṣā tasyāpi yāsyatyavadhūya buddhim ||
children.translated_text: Yet, as I see it, this understanding of yours will go on, sweeping aside even his doctrine.
For this [face], with a clear high nose, broad elongated eyes, coppery lower lip, and white sharp teeth,

children.text: idaṃ hi vaktuṃ tanuraktajihvaṃ jñeyārṇavaṃ pāsyati kṛtsnameva ||
children.translated_text: with a slender red tongue fit for speech, will drink in the whole ocean of what is to be known.

children.text: gambhīratā yā bhavatastvagādhā yā dīptatā yāni ca lakṣaṇāni
children.translated_text: That unfathomable depth of yours, that brilliance, and those marks,
show that you will attain teacherhood on earth, such as was not attained even by seers in the former age."
Then the king's son, saying "Excellent," honored that company of seers in return and departed.
Those hermits too, after attending on him according to rule, entered the ascetic grove.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye tapovanapraveśo nāma saptamaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, ends the seventh canto, named "Entering the Ascetic Grove."

children.text: tatasturaṅgāvacaraḥ sa durmanāstathā vanaṃ bhartari nirmame gate
children.translated_text: Then that horseman, downcast in mind, when his unattached master had gone thus to the forest,

children.text: cakāra yatnaṃ pathi śokanigrahe tathāpi caivāśru na tasya cikṣiye ||
children.translated_text: made an effort on the road to restrain his grief; and yet his tears did not cease.

children.text: yamekarātreṇa tu bharturājñayā jagāma mārgaṃ saha tena vājinā
children.translated_text: The road which, by his master's command, he had traveled in one night with that horse,
that very road he traversed in eight days, brooding over separation from his master.

children.text: hayaśca saujā vicacāra kanthakastatāma bhāvena babhūva nirmadaḥ
children.translated_text: And the strong horse <s>Kanthaka</s> went along; he pined away in feeling and became dispirited.
Though adorned in the same way with ornaments, bereft of him he seemed to have lost his splendor.

children.text: nivṛtya caivābhimukhastapovanaṃ bhṛśaṃ jiheṣe karuṇaṃ muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: And turning back to face the ascetic grove, he neighed loudly and plaintively again and again.

children.text: kṣudhānvito 'pyadhvani śaṣpamambu vā yathā purā nābhinananda nādade ||
children.translated_text: Though afflicted by hunger on the road, he neither welcomed nor took grass or water as before.

children.text: tato vihīnaṃ kapilāhvayaṃ puraṃ mahātmanā tena jagaddhitātmanā
children.translated_text: Then the two gradually approached the city called <s>Kapila</s>, bereft of that great-souled one whose soul was for the good of the world,
as if it were empty, like the sky deprived of the sun.
Although its waters were beautiful with lotuses and it was adorned with trees bearing flowers,

children.text: tadeva tasyopavanaṃ vanopamaṃ gatapraharṣairna rarāja nāgaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that same pleasure-grove of his, forest-like, did not shine, because the townspeople had lost their joy.

children.text: tato bhramadbhirdiśi dīnamānasair anujjvalair bāṣpahatekṣaṇair naraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with people wandering in every direction, downhearted, dimmed, their eyes stricken by tears,
the two approached the city slowly, as if they themselves were being extinguished and as if the city had undergone a mourning bath.

children.text: niśāmya ca srastaśarīragāminau vināgatau śākyakularṣabheṇa tau
children.translated_text: And seeing those two coming back without the bull of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, their bodies drooping as they moved,

children.text: mumoca bāṣpaṃ pathi nāgaro janaḥ purā rathe dāśaratherivāgate ||
children.translated_text: the townspeople shed tears on the road, as in ancient times when the chariot of <s>Dāśarathi</s> returned.

children.text: atha bruvantaḥ samupetamanyavo janāḥ pathi chandakamāgatāśravaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the people, speaking, overcome with grief and with tears rising, followed <s>Chandaka</s> along the road,
asking from behind, "Where is that prince, the delight of city and kingdom, carried off by you?"

children.text: tataḥ sa tān bhaktimato 'bravījjanānnarendraputraṃ na parityajāmyaham
children.translated_text: Then he said to those devoted people, "I did not abandon the son of the king.

children.text: rudannahaṃ tena tu nirjane vane gṛhasthaveṣaśca visarjitāviti ||
children.translated_text: Rather, in the lonely forest, I, weeping, and the attire of a householder were dismissed by him."

children.text: idaṃ vacastasya niśamya te janāḥ suduṣkaraṃ khalviti niścayaṃ yayuḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this statement of his, the people came to the conclusion, "It is indeed very hard to do."

children.text: pataddhi jahruḥ salilaṃ na netrajaṃ mano nininduśca phalotthamātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They shed falling water born from their eyes, and blamed their own fate, sprung from the fruits [of former acts].

children.text: athocuradyaiva viśāma tadvanaṃ gataḥ sa yatra dviparājavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then they said, "Today itself let us enter that forest where he of the stride of an elephant king has gone.

children.text: jijīviṣā nāsti hi tena no vinā yathendriyāṇāṃ vigame śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: For without him we have no desire to live, just as embodied beings have none when the senses depart.

children.text: idaṃ puraṃ tena vivarjitaṃ vanaṃ vanaṃ ca tattena samanvitaṃ puram
children.translated_text: This city, deprived of him, is a forest; and that forest, endowed with him, is a city.

children.text: na śobhate tena hi no vinā puraṃ marutvatā vṛtravadhe yathā divam ||
children.translated_text: For without him our city does not shine, as heaven would not shine without <s>Marutvat</s> at the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: punaḥ kumāro vinivṛtta ityatho gavākṣamālāḥ pratipedire 'ṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the women, thinking, "The prince has returned again," went to the rows of lattice windows.

children.text: viviktapṛṣṭhaṃ ca niśāmya vājinaṃ punargavākṣāṇi pidhāya cukruśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But seeing the horse's back empty, they closed the lattice windows again and cried.

children.text: praviṣṭadīkṣastu sutopalabdhaye vratena śokena ca khinnamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: But the ruler of men, having undertaken consecration to recover his son, his mind worn down by vow and grief,

children.text: jajāpa devāyatane narādhipaścakāra tāstāśca yathāśayāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: muttered prayers in the temple and performed those various rites according to his intention.
Then he, the horse-attendant, his eyes filled with tears, took the horse,

children.text: viveśa śokābhihato nṛpakṣayaṃ yudhāpinīte ripuṇeva bhartari ||
children.translated_text: and, stricken by grief, entered the royal residence, as when a master has been carried off by an enemy in war.
And as he entered the palace of the king, looking around with eyes streaming tears,

children.text: svareṇa puṣṭena rurāva kanthako janāya duḥkhaṃ prativedayanniva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kanthaka</s> cried out with a full voice, as if announcing sorrow to the people.
Then the birds moving within the dwelling, and the honored horses tied nearby,
echoed the sound of that horse, thinking that the king's son was arriving.
And the people near the inner apartments of the lord of men, deceived by excessive joy,

children.text: yathā hayaḥ kanthaka eṣa heṣate dhruvaṃ kumāro viśatīti menire ||
children.translated_text: thought, "Since this horse <s>Kanthaka</s> is neighing, surely the prince is entering."
Then, after that extreme joy, stunned by grief and with eyes eager for the sight of the prince,

children.text: gṛhād viniścakramur āśayā striyaḥ śaratpayodādiva vidyutaścalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the women came out from the houses in hope, flickering like lightning from autumn clouds.
With loose-hanging hair, wearing soiled garments, and with faces whose unpainted eyes were struck by tears,

children.text: striyo na rejurmṛjayā vinākṛtā divīva tārā rajanīkṣayāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the women did not shine, deprived of adornment, like stars in heaven reddened at the end of night.
With feet coppery though not reddened, without anklets, without earrings, and with faces on bare, straight necks,

children.text: svabhāvapīnair jaghanair amekhalair ahārayoktrair muṣitairiva stanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with naturally full hips without girdles, and with breasts seeming robbed, lacking their necklace-bands,

children.text: nirīkṣya tā bāṣpaparītalocanā nirāśrayaṃ chandakamaśvameva ca
children.translated_text: seeing those tear-filled women, and <s>Chandaka</s> bereft, together with only the horse,
the palace women, their faces downcast, wept like cows in the forest abandoned by a bull.

children.text: tataḥ sabāṣpā mahiṣī mahīpateḥ pranaṣṭavatsā mahiṣīva vatsalā
children.translated_text: Then the king's queen, affectionate <s>Gautamī</s>, like a cow whose calf has been lost,

children.text: pragṛhya bāhū nipapāta gautamī vilolaparṇā kadalīva kāñcanī ||
children.translated_text: stretched out her arms and fell down like a golden plantain tree with trembling leaves.

children.text: hatatviṣo 'nyāḥ śithilāṃsabāhavaḥ striyo viṣādena vicetanā iva
children.translated_text: Other women, their radiance struck down, their shoulders and arms slack, as if made senseless by sorrow,

children.text: na cukruśurnāśru jahurna śaśvasurna celurāsurlikhitā iva sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: neither cried out, nor shed tears, nor breathed, nor moved; they stood as if painted.
Other women, unsteady and overcome by grief for their lord, with faces pouring streams from their eyes,
sprinkled their breasts from which sandal paste had gone, as a mountain sprinkles rocks with waterfalls.

children.text: mukhaiśca tāsāṃ nayanāmbutāḍitai rarāja tadrājaniveśanaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: And with their faces beaten by the water of their eyes, that royal residence then shone
like a lake in the rainy season, with lotuses streaming water after being struck by cloud-showers.
The noble women, with rounded, plump fingers, close together, unadorned, and with hidden veins,

children.text: urāṃsi jaghnuḥ kamalopamaiḥ karaiḥ svapallavairvātacalā latā iva ||
children.translated_text: struck their breasts with lotus-like hands, like creepers moved by wind with their own shoots.

children.text: karaprahārapracalaiśca tā babhustathāpi nāryaḥ sahitonnataiḥ stanaiḥ
children.translated_text: And the women appeared with their joined, high breasts trembling from the blows of their hands,
like rivers with pairs of cakravāka birds, their lotuses shaken by a forest wind.

children.text: yathā ca vakṣāṃsi karairapīḍayaṃstathaiva vakṣobhirapīḍayan karān
children.translated_text: Just as they pressed their breasts with their hands, so too they pressed their hands with their breasts;
there the helpless women, languid with grief, caused mutual pain between fingertips and breasts.
Then <s>Yaśodharā</s>, her eyes deeply reddened with anger, her voice hoarse and choked by sorrow,
her breasts shaken by sighs, plunged in deep grief and streaming tears, spoke:

children.text: niśi prasuptāmavaśāṃ vihāya māṃ gataḥ kva sa chandaka manmanorathaḥ
children.translated_text: "Abandoning me while I slept helplessly at night, where has he gone, <s>Chandaka</s>, he who was my heart's desire?

children.text: upāgate ca tvayi kanthake ca me samaṃ gateṣu triṣu kampate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now that you and <s>Kanthaka</s> have come back, while the three of you went together, my mind trembles.

children.text: anāryamasnigdhamamitrakarma me nṛśaṃsa kṛtvā kimihādya rodiṣi
children.translated_text: After doing to me an ignoble, unaffectionate, enemy-like deed, cruel man, why do you weep here today?

children.text: niyaccha bāṣpaṃ bhava tuṣṭamānaso na saṃvadatyaśru ca tacca karma te ||
children.translated_text: Restrain your tears; be pleased at heart. Your tears and that deed of yours do not agree.

children.text: priyeṇa vaśyena hitena sādhunā tvayā sahāyena yathārthakāriṇā
children.translated_text: With you as his dear, obedient, helpful, virtuous companion, one who acted according to the purpose,

children.text: gato 'ryaputro hyapunarnivṛttaye ramasva diṣṭyā saphalaḥ śramastava ||
children.translated_text: the noble prince has gone, never to return; take your pleasure, for by fate your labor has borne fruit.
Better for a man is a discerning enemy than an undiscerning friend unskilled in proper action;

children.text: suhṛdbruveṇa hyavipaścitā tvayā kṛtaḥ kulasyāsya mahānupaplavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for by you, calling yourself a friend but lacking insight, a great calamity has been made for this family.
These women are indeed pitiable, their ornaments cast off, their red eyes clouded by unceasing tears;

children.text: sthite 'pi patyau himavanmahīsame pranaṣṭaśobhā vidhavā iva striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though their lord, equal to <s>Himavat</s> and the earth, still lives, they have lost their beauty like widows.
And these rows of palaces, with their latticed arms flung wide and with the long continuous cries of clinging doves,
deprived of him together with the women of the inner apartments, seem to be weeping bitterly.

children.text: anarthakāmo 'sya janasya sarvathā turaṅgamo 'pi dhruvameṣa kanthakaḥ
children.translated_text: This horse <s>Kanthaka</s> too is surely, in every way, a seeker of harm for all these people;

children.text: jahāra sarvasvamitastathā hi me jane prasupte niśi ratnacauravat ||
children.translated_text: for in just this way he stole all I possessed from here at night, while the people slept, like a jewel-thief.

children.text: yadā samarthaḥ khalu soḍhumāgatāniṣuprahārānapi kiṃ punaḥ kaśāḥ
children.translated_text: When he is indeed able to bear even the strikes of arrows that come at him, how much more the lashes of whips,

children.text: gataḥ kaśāpātabhayātkathaṃ nvayaṃ śriyaṃ gṛhītvā hṛdayaṃ ca me samam ||
children.translated_text: how then did this one go from fear of the fall of a whip, taking my fortune and my heart together?
Today, after doing an ignoble act, he neighs loudly, as if filling the royal residence;

children.text: yadā tu nirvāhayati sma me priyaṃ tadā hi mūkasturagādhamo 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: but when he was carrying away my beloved, then this lowest of horses became mute.

children.text: yadi hyaheṣiṣyata bodhayan janaṃ khuraiḥ kṣitau vāpyakariṣyata dhvanim
children.translated_text: For if he had neighed, waking the people, or even made a sound with his hooves on the ground,
or had produced a great noise with his jaws, this sorrow of mine would not have been like this."

children.text: itīha devyāḥ paridevitāśrayaṃ niśamya bāṣpagrathitākṣaraṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing here the queen's speech, grounded in lamentation and with its syllables bound together by tears,

children.text: adhomukhaḥ sāśrukalaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ śanairidaṃ chandaka uttaraṃ jagau ||
