children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, face downcast, tearful, and with folded hands, slowly gave this reply.

children.text: vigarhituṃ nārhasi devi kanthakaṃ na cāpi roṣaṃ mayi kartumarhasi
children.translated_text: Lady, you should not blame <s>Kanthaka</s>, nor should you be angry with me.

children.text: anāgasau svaḥ samavehi sarvaśo gato nṛdevaḥ sa hi devi devavat ||
children.translated_text: Know that we two are wholly without fault, O lady; for that lord of men has gone like a god.

children.text: ahaṃ hi jānannapi rājaśāsanaṃ balātkṛtaḥ kairapi daivatairiva
children.translated_text: For although I knew the king's command, I was compelled as if by certain deities;
I quickly brought this horse, and likewise followed him on the road, free from fatigue.
Even this best of horses, as he went, did not touch the earth with the tips of his hooves, as if they were held up in the air.

children.text: tathaiva daivādiva saṃyatānano hanusvanaṃ nākṛta nāpyaheṣata ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, as if by divine power, with his mouth restrained, he made no sound with his jaws and did not neigh.
When the prince was going out, the gate opened by itself,

children.text: tamaśca naiśaṃ raviṇeva pāṭitaṃ tato 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: and the darkness of night was split as if by the sun; from this too, understand that this was a divine ordinance.

children.text: yadapramatto 'pi narendraśāsanād gṛhe pure caiva sahasraśo janaḥ
children.translated_text: Although, by the lord of men's command, thousands of people were vigilant in the palace and in the city,

children.text: tadā sa nābudhyata nidrayā hṛtastato 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: then they did not wake, overcome by sleep; from this too, understand that this was a divine ordinance.

children.text: yataśca vāso vanavāsasaṃmataṃ nisṛṣṭamasmai samaye divaukasā
children.translated_text: And since a garment suitable for forest-dwelling was given to him at the right time by a heavenly being,

children.text: divi praviddhaṃ mukuṭaṃ ca taddhṛtaṃ tato 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: and since the crown he cast into the sky was caught, from this too, understand that this was a divine ordinance.

children.text: tadevamāvāṃ naradevi doṣato na tatprayātaṃ prati gantumarhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore, O queen, you should not regard us two as at fault with respect to his departure.

children.text: na kāmakāro mama nāsya vājinaḥ kṛtānuyātraḥ sa hi daivatairgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was not my own will, nor this horse's; he went, attended on his journey by the gods.

children.text: iti prayāṇaṃ bahudevam adbhutaṃ niśamya tāstasya mahātmanaḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing of that wondrous departure, filled with many gods, the women of that great-souled one

children.text: pranaṣṭaśokā iva vismayaṃ yayurmanojvaraṃ pravrajanāttu lebhire ||
children.translated_text: fell into amazement, as if their grief had vanished, but from his going forth they suffered a fever of the mind.
Then <s>Gautamī</s>, her eyes swimming with despondency, grieving like a female kurarī bird whose chick is lost,

children.text: vihāya dhairyaṃ virurāva gautamī tatāma caivāśrumukhī jagāda ca ||
children.translated_text: abandoned firmness, wailed aloud, grew faint, and, her face wet with tears, spoke:
Those locks of his, deep-waved, soft, black, lovely, grown separately from their roots,
fit to encircle a king's diadem, have been scattered upon the ground.
Long-armed, lion-gaited, with eyes like a great bull's, with a splendor bright as gold,
broad-chested and with a voice like a deep drum: can even one such as he be fit for dwelling in a hermitage?
Surely this earth is unfortunate, now that that unsurpassed lord of noble deeds

children.text: gatastato 'sau guṇavān hi tādṛśo nṛpaḥ prajābhāgyaguṇaiḥ prasūyate ||
children.translated_text: has gone away; for such a virtuous king is born through the merits of his subjects' good fortune.
Those two feet, soft, with toes joined by well-formed webbing, with hidden ankles, tender as lotus fibers,

children.text: vanāntabhūmiṃ kaṭhināṃ kathaṃ nu tau sacakramadhyau caraṇau gamiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and marked with wheels in their centers: how will they travel over the hard ground of the forest's edge?
That vigorous body, accustomed to beds and seats on palace terraces, honored with costly garments, aloes, and sandalwood,

children.text: kathaṃ nu śītoṣṇajalāgameṣu taccharīramojasvi vane bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: how will it fare in the forest amid the arrival of cold, heat, and rain?

children.text: kulena sattvena balena varcasā śrutena lakṣmyā vayasā ca garvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Proud in lineage, courage, strength, splendor, learning, fortune, and youth,

children.text: pradātumevābhyucito na yācituṃ kathaṃ sa bhikṣāṃ parataścariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he is fit only to give, not to ask; how will he go about for alms from others?

children.text: śucau śayitvā śayane hiraṇmaye prabodhyamāno niśi tūryanisvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having slept on a clean golden bed and been awakened at night by the sounds of musical instruments,

children.text: kathaṃ bata svapsyati so 'dya me vratī paṭaikadeśāntarite mahītale ||
children.translated_text: how, alas, will that vow-observer of mine now sleep on the earth, separated from it only by a strip of cloth?

children.text: imaṃ pralāpaṃ karuṇaṃ niśamya tā bhujaiḥ pariṣvajya parasparaṃ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this piteous lament, those women embraced one another with their arms,

children.text: vilocanebhyaḥ salilāni tatyajurmadhūni puṣpebhya iveritā latāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and shed water from their eyes, like shaken creepers releasing nectar from their flowers.
Then <s>Yaśodharā</s> fell upon the ground like a female cakravāka bird separated from her mate,
and, distraught, she slowly lamented this and that again and again, with a voice choked and stammering.

children.text: sa māmanāthāṃ sahadharmacāriṇīmapāsya dharmaṃ yadi kartumicchati
children.translated_text: If, casting me aside though I am helpless and his companion in <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty), he wishes to practice <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kuto 'sya dharmaḥ sahadharmacāriṇīṃ vinā tapo yaḥ paribhoktumicchati ||
children.translated_text: where is his <s>dharma</s>, if he wishes to experience asceticism without his companion in <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: śṛṇoti nūnaṃ sa na pūrvapārthivān mahāsudarśaprabhṛtīn pitāmahān
children.translated_text: Surely he has not heard of the ancient kings, his forefathers beginning with <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>,

children.text: vanāni patnīsahitānupeyuṣastathā hi dharmaṃ madṛte cikīrṣati ||
children.translated_text: who went to the forests together with their wives; for in just this way he wishes to perform <s>dharma</s> without me.

children.text: makheṣu vā vedavidhānasaṃskṛtau na daṃpatī paśyati dīkṣitāvubhau
children.translated_text: Or does he not see at sacrifices that husband and wife are both consecrated by the ordinance of the Veda,

children.text: samaṃ bubhukṣū parato 'pi tatphalaṃ tato 'sya jāto mayi dharmamatsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: both desiring to enjoy its fruit equally even in the hereafter? Therefore rivalry over <s>dharma</s> has arisen in him toward me.

children.text: dhruvaṃ sa jānanmama dharmavallabho manaḥ priyerṣyākalahaṃ muhurmithaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely my beloved, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, knowing my heart and our repeated quarrels born of jealous love,
fears discomfort, and, abandoning me, an angry woman, happily wishes to take the apsarases in <s>Mahendra</s>'s world.

children.text: iyaṃ tu cintā mama kīdṛśaṃ nu tā vapurguṇaṃ bibhrati tatra yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: But this is my thought: what kind of bodily excellence do those women there possess,

children.text: vane yadarthaṃ sa tapāṃsi tapyate śriyaṃ ca hitvā mama bhaktimeva ca ||
children.translated_text: for whose sake he practices austerities in the forest, abandoning prosperity and my very devotion?

children.text: na khalviyaṃ svargasukhāya me spṛhā na tajjanasyātmavato 'pi durlabham
children.translated_text: Indeed this is not a longing on my part for the happiness of heaven, nor is that hard to obtain even for a self-possessed person.

children.text: sa tu priyo māmiha vā paratra vā kathaṃ na jahyāditi me manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rather, this is my wish: how might that beloved not abandon me, whether here or hereafter?
If I am so unfortunate that I may not behold my husband's long-eyed, pure-smiling face,

children.text: na mandabhāgyo 'rhati rāhulo 'pyayaṃ kadācidaṅke parivartituṃ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: then this poor-fated <s>Rāhula</s> too will never deserve to turn about in his father's lap.

children.text: aho nṛśaṃsaṃ sukumāravarcasaḥ sudāruṇaṃ tasya manasvino manaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, cruel and very hard is the heart of that resolute man of delicate radiance,

children.text: kalapralāpaṃ dviṣato 'pi harṣaṇaṃ śiśuṃ sutaṃ yastyajatīdṛśaṃ bata ||
children.translated_text: who abandons such a child, his son, whose sweet babbling would gladden even an enemy.

children.text: mamāpi kāmaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudāruṇaṃ śilāmayaṃ vāpyayaso 'pi vā kṛtam
children.translated_text: My own heart too is surely very hard, or made of stone, or even fashioned from iron...

children.text: anāthavacchrīrahite sukhocite vanaṃ gate bhartari yanna dīryate ||
children.translated_text: when my husband, like one helpless, stripped of splendor though fit for pleasure, has gone to the forest, why does my heart not split apart?

children.text: itīha devī patiśokamūrchitā ruroda dadhyau vilalāpa cāsakṛt
children.translated_text: Thus the queen, fainting with grief for her husband, wept here, brooded, and lamented again and again;

children.text: svabhāvadhīrāpi hi sā satī śucā dhṛtiṃ na sasmāra cakāra no hriyam ||
children.translated_text: for though naturally steadfast, that faithful woman, through sorrow, remembered no firmness and paid no heed to modest restraint.
Then, seeing <s>Yaśodharā</s>, shaken by such grief and lamentation, fallen upon the earth,
the women cried out with tearful faces, like great lotuses beaten by rain.
But the king, after completing his recitation and performing the auspicious fire offering, came out from the temple;
struck by the people's anguished cry, he trembled like an elephant at the crash of a thunderbolt.

children.text: niśāmya ca chandakakanthakāvubhau sutasya saṃśrutya ca niścayaṃ sthiram
children.translated_text: Having seen both <s>Chandaka</s> and <s>Kanthaka</s>, and having heard of his son's firm resolve,

children.text: papāta śokābhihato mahīpatiḥ śacīpatervṛtta ivotsave dhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth fell, struck down by grief, like the banner of the lord of <s>Śacī</s> when the festival is over.

children.text: tato muhūrtaṃ sutaśokamohito janena tulyābhijanena dhāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, for a moment stupefied by grief for his son and held up by people of equal noble birth,

children.text: nirīkṣya dṛṣṭyā jalapūrṇayā hayaṃ mahītalastho vilalāpa pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king, on the ground, looked at the horse with eyes full of water and lamented.

children.text: bahūni kṛtvā samare priyāṇi me mahattvayā kanthaka vipriyaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: After doing many things dear to me in battle, O <s>Kanthaka</s>, you have done me a great unkindness;

children.text: guṇapriyo yena vane sa me priyaḥ priyo 'pi sannapriyavatpraveritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by you my beloved son, fond of virtue, though dear to me, was sent into the forest as if he were unloved.

children.text: tadadya māṃ vā naya tatra yatra sa vraja drutaṃ vā punarenamānaya
children.translated_text: Therefore today either take me to the place where he is, or go quickly and bring him back again;

children.text: ṛte hi tasmānmama nāsti jīvitaṃ vigāḍharogasya sadauṣadhādiva ||
children.translated_text: for without him there is no life for me, just as there is none for one with a grave disease without the right medicine.

children.text: suvarṇaniṣṭhīvini mṛtyunā hṛte suduṣkaraṃ yanna mamāra saṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Suvarṇaniṣṭhīvin</s> had been carried off by death, it was very hard that <s>Sañjaya</s> did not die;
but I, now that my son devoted to <s>dharma</s> (the spiritual law) has gone, long to release myself, like a man no longer master of himself.
For of the mighty lord, maker of the ten warrior lines, lord of creatures, knower of higher and lower, son of <s>Vivasvat</s>,

children.text: priyeṇa putreṇa satā vinākṛtaṃ kathaṃ na muhyeddhi mano manorapi ||
children.translated_text: how indeed would even <s>Manu</s>'s mind not be bewildered, deprived of a beloved and virtuous son?

children.text: ajasya rājñastanayāya dhīmate narādhipāyendrasakhāya me spṛhā
children.translated_text: I envy the wise son of King <s>Aja</s>, a lord of men and friend of <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: gate vanaṃ yastanaye divaṃ gato na moghabāṣpaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ jijīva ha ||
children.translated_text: when his son had gone to the forest, he went to heaven, and did not live pitiably with useless tears.

children.text: pracakṣva me bhadra tadāśramājiraṃ hṛtastvayā yatra sa me jalāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me, good man, the precinct of that hermitage where he was carried off by you, he who is my libation of water;

children.text: ime parīpsanti hi taṃ pipāsavo mamāsavaḥ pretagatiṃ yiyāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for these life-breaths of mine, thirsty and wishing to go the way of the dead, seek him.

children.text: iti tanayaviyogajātaduḥkhaḥ kṣitisadṛśaṃ sahajaṃ vihāya dhairyam
children.translated_text: Thus, from the sorrow born of separation from his son, the king abandoned his innate steadiness, equal to the earth;

children.text: daśaratha iva rāmaśokavaśyo bahu vilalāpa nṛpo visaṃjñakalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Daśaratha</s> subject to grief for <s>Rāma</s>, the king lamented much, almost unconscious.
Then the aged wise minister, endowed with learning, discipline, and virtue, and the priest,
spoke these fitting words to him in a composed way, their faces neither overwrought nor free from sorrow.

children.text: tyaja naravara śokamehi dhairyaṃ kudhṛtirivārhasi dhīra nāśru moktum
children.translated_text: Abandon grief, best of men; come back to firmness. O steadfast one, you ought not to shed tears like a man of poor courage.

children.text: srajamiva mṛditāmapāsya lakṣmīṃ bhuvi bahavo hi nṛpā vanānyabhīyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For many kings, casting off royal fortune like a crushed garland, have gone to the forests.

children.text: api ca niyata eṣa tasya bhāvaḥ smara vacanaṃ tadṛṣeḥ purāsitasya
children.translated_text: Moreover, this inclination of his is fixed; remember the word once spoken by that seer <s>Asita</s>.

children.text: na hi sa divi na cakravartirājye kṣaṇamapi vāsayituṃ sukhena śakyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For he cannot be made to dwell happily for even a moment in heaven or in the realm of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).

children.text: yadi tu nṛvara kārya eva yatnastvaritamudāhara yāvadatra yāvaḥ
children.translated_text: But if, best of kings, effort must indeed be made, give the order quickly, so that we may go there.

children.text: bahuvidham iha yuddhamastu tāvattava tanayasya vidheśca tasya tasya ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile let there be here a many-sided struggle between your son and that fate of his.

children.text: narapatiratha tau śaśāsa tasmād drutamita eva yuvāmabhiprayātam
children.translated_text: Then the lord of men commanded those two: 'Therefore go very quickly from this very place, both of you;

children.text: na hi mama hṛdayaṃ prayāti śāntiṃ vanaśakuneriva putralālasasya ||
children.translated_text: for my heart does not come to peace, like that of a forest bird longing for its young.'
At the king's command, saying 'So be it,' the minister and the priest went to that forest;

children.text: kṛtamiti savadhūjanaḥ sadāro nṛpatirapi pracakāra śeṣakāryam ||
children.translated_text: and the king too, together with the women and with his wives, carried out the remaining duties.
Thus in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the eighth canto, named <s>Antaḥpuravilāpa</s> (The Lament of the Inner Apartments), is complete.
Then those two, the minister and the priest, as if struck by the king with goads made of tears,
like excellent horses pricked on, went with all effort to that forest, swift because of affection.
Those two, weary from travel and with suitable attendants, reached that hermitage at the proper time;
putting aside royal splendor and acting humbly, they approached the dwelling of <s>Bhārgava</s> himself.

children.text: tau nyāyatastaṃ pratipūjya vipraṃ tenārcitau tāvapi cānurūpam
children.translated_text: They duly honored that Brahmin, and, after they too had been honored by him in fitting fashion,
when seated, they cut short the conversation and spoke their own business to <s>Bhārgava</s> seated on his seat.
Of the king sprung from the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line, pure in strength and pure in broad fame,

children.text: imaṃ janaṃ vettu bhavānadhītaṃ śrutagrahe mantraparigrahe ca ||
children.translated_text: may your reverence know this delegation as instructed in preserving sacred learning and in taking counsel.
His son, like <s>Jayanta</s> to that <s>Indra</s>-like king, wishes to cross beyond the fear of old age and death;
he is said to have come here for that reason. May your reverence know that we two have come for him.

children.text: tau so 'bravīdasti sa dīrghabāhuḥ prāptaḥ kumāro na tu nāvabuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: He replied to the two, 'Yes, that long-armed prince has come here, and not without understanding;
but realizing, "This <s>dharma</s> (religious discipline) leads back to rebirth," the seeker of release has gone toward <s>Arāḍa</s>.'

children.text: tasmāttatastāvupalabhya tattvaṃ taṃ vipramāmantrya tadaiva sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, after learning the truth from him, the two took leave of that Brahmin at once, then and there;

children.text: khinnāvakhinnāviva rājabhaktyā prasasratustena yataḥ sa yātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though weary, seeming unweary through loyalty to the king, they set out by the route by which he had gone.

children.text: yāntau tatastau mṛjayā vihīnamapaśyatāṃ taṃ vapuṣojjvalantam
children.translated_text: As they went, the two then saw him, without grooming yet shining with the radiance of his body,

children.text: upopaviṣṭaṃ pathi vṛkṣamūle sūryaṃ ghanābhogamiva praviṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: sitting by the road at the foot of a tree, like the sun entered into a mass of clouds.

children.text: yānaṃ vihāyopayayau tatastaṃ purohito mantradhareṇa sārdham
children.translated_text: Leaving the carriage, the priest then approached him together with the counselor,

children.text: yathā vanasthaṃ sahavāmadevo rāmaṃ didṛkṣur munir aurvaśeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the <s>Aurvaśeya</s> sage, together with <s>Vāmadeva</s>, wished to see <s>Rāma</s> dwelling in the forest.

children.text: tāvarcayāmāsatur arhatas taṃ divīva śukrāṅgirasau mahendram
children.translated_text: Those two honored that worthy one, as <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> honored great <s>Indra</s> in heaven;

children.text: pratyarcayāmāsa sa cārhatastau divīva śukrāṅgirasau mahendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he in return honored those two worthy men, as great <s>Indra</s> honored <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> in heaven.
Then, having received permission, those two sat down on either side of the banner of the <s>Śākya</s> clan;
and near him they shone like the two <s>Punarvasu</s> stars joined with the moon.
The priest addressed the king's son, blazing with splendor as he stayed at the foot of a tree,

children.text: yathopaviṣṭaṃ divi pārijāte bṛhaspatiḥ śakrasutaṃ jayantam ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Bṛhaspati</s> addresses <s>Jayanta</s>, son of <s>Śakra</s>, seated by the <s>Pārijāta</s> in heaven.

children.text: tvacchokaśalye hṛdayāvagāḍhe mohaṃ gato bhūmitale muhūrtam
children.translated_text: With the thorn of grief for you sunk deep in his heart, he fell senseless upon the ground for a moment;
Prince, what the king, raining water from his eyes, said to you, listen to it now.

children.text: jānāmi dharmaṃ prati niścayaṃ te paraimi te bhāvinametamartham
children.translated_text: I know your fixed resolve toward <s>dharma</s> (the religious path), and I understand this aim that lies before you;
but I am burned by a grief-fire, like fire itself, because you have taken refuge in the forest at the wrong time.

children.text: tadehi dharmapriya matpriyārtha dharmārthameva tyaja buddhimetām
children.translated_text: Therefore come, lover of <s>dharma</s> (the religious path); for my sake and for <s>dharma</s> itself, abandon this intention.

children.text: ayaṃ hi mā śokarayaḥ pravṛddho nadīrayaḥ kūlamivābhihanti ||
children.translated_text: For this swollen torrent of grief strikes me like a river's current beating against its bank.
Whatever action wind, sun, fire, and great thunderbolts have upon clouds, water, thickets, and mountains,
grief performs that same action upon us, by dragging away, drying up, burning, and splitting apart.

children.text: tadbhuṅkṣva tāvadvasudhādhipatyaṃ kāle vanaṃ yāsyasi śāstradṛṣṭe
children.translated_text: Therefore enjoy sovereignty over the earth for now; at the time approved by scripture you will go to the forest.

children.text: aniṣṭabandhau kuru mayyapekṣāṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu dayā hi dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Show regard for me, your afflicted kinsman, for compassion toward all beings is indeed <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct).

children.text: na caiṣa dharmo vana eva siddhaḥ pure 'pi siddhirniyatā yatīnām
children.translated_text: And this <s>dharma</s> is not accomplished only in the forest; success is assured for ascetics even in the city.

children.text: buddhiśca yatnaśca nimittamatra vanaṃ ca liṅgaṃ ca hi bhīrucihnam ||
children.translated_text: Understanding and effort are the causes here; the forest and the outward marks are signs of the timid.
Kings wearing diadems, with necklaces hanging on their shoulders and arms held firm by armlets,
even while moving in the lap of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (royal fortune), have attained the <s>mokṣadharma</s> (path of liberation) as householders.
The two younger brothers of <s>Dhruva</s>, mighty <s>Bali</s> and <s>Vajrabāhu</s>, <s>Vaibhrāja</s>, <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, and <s>Antideva</s>,

children.text: videharājaṃ janakaṃ tathaiva śālvadrumaṃ senajitaśca rājñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Videha</s> king <s>Janaka</s> likewise, <s>Śālvadruma</s>, and king <s>Senajit</s>:
know these household kings to have been trained in the rule of <s>dharma</s> leading to the highest good.

children.text: ubhe 'pi tasmādyugapadbhajasva cittādhipatyaṃ ca nṛpaśriyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore cultivate both at once: sovereignty over the mind and the splendor of kingship.

children.text: icchāmi hi tvāmupaguhya gāḍhaṃ kṛtābhiṣekaṃ salilārdrameva
children.translated_text: For I wish to embrace you tightly, freshly wet with the water of consecration,
and, while seeing you holding the royal parasol, to enter the forest with that very joy.
Thus spoke the lord of the earth to you, with a speech whose syllables were knotted by tears;

children.text: śrutvā bhavānarhati tatpriyārthaṃ snehena tatsneham anuprayātum ||
children.translated_text: having heard it, you ought, for his pleasure, to follow his affection with affection of your own.

children.text: śokāmbhasi tvatprabhave hyagādhe duḥkhārṇave majjati śākyarājaḥ
children.translated_text: For the <s>Śākya</s> king is sinking in an unfathomable water of grief, an ocean of suffering produced by you;
therefore lift him up, helpless and unsupported, like a masterless boat sunk in the ocean.

children.text: bhīṣmeṇa gaṅgodarasaṃbhavena rāmeṇa rāmeṇa ca bhārgaveṇa
children.translated_text: By <s>Bhīṣma</s>, born from <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s womb, and by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: śrutvā kṛtaṃ karma pituḥ priyārthaṃ pitustvam apyarhasi kartumiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: a deed was done for the sake of their fathers; you too ought to do what your father desires.
Consider the queen who raised you, who has not departed to the southern quarter frequented by <s>Agastya</s>,
like an affectionate cow whose calf is lost, constantly afflicted and crying piteously.

children.text: haṃsena haṃsīmiva viprayuktāṃ tyaktāṃ gajeneva vane kareṇum
children.translated_text: Separated from you like a female swan from a male swan, abandoned like a cow elephant by an elephant in the forest,

children.text: ārtāṃ sanāthāmapi nāthahīnāṃ trātuṃ vadhūmarhasi darśanena ||
children.translated_text: your wife, though she has a protector, is afflicted and protectorless; you ought to save her by showing yourself.
And your only son, a child undeserving of suffering, bearing hidden anguish within,
that <s>Rāhula</s>, release from grief for his kinsman, like the full moon from the assault of <s>Rāhu</s>.
With the fire of grief, whose fuel is separation from you, whose smoke is sighing, and whose flame is darkness,

children.text: tvaddarśanāmbvicchati dahyamānamantaḥpuraṃ caiva puraṃ ca kṛtsnam ||
children.translated_text: the inner palace and the whole city, burning, longs for the water of seeing you.

children.text: sa bodhisattvaḥ paripūrṇasattvaḥ śrutvā vacastasya purohitasya
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his being fully perfected, heard the words of that priest;
having reflected for a moment, he, virtuous and knowing virtue, spoke this respectful reply:

children.text: avaimi bhāvaṃ tanaye pitṝṇāṃ viśeṣato yo mayi bhūmipasya
children.translated_text: I understand the feeling of fathers toward a son, especially that which the king has toward me;
yet, although I know it, afraid of the dangers of sickness and old age, I abandon my own people because there is no other way.

children.text: draṣṭuṃ priyaṃ kaḥ svajanaṃ hi necchennānte yadi syātpriyaviprayogaḥ
children.translated_text: For who would not wish to see dear kinsfolk, if at the end there were no separation from what is dear?

children.text: yadā tu bhūtvāpi ciraṃ viyogastato guruṃ snigdhamapi tyajāmi ||
children.translated_text: But since, even after a long time together, separation comes, therefore I leave even a respected and affectionate person.

children.text: maddhetukaṃ yattu narādhipasya śokaṃ bhavānāha na tatpriyaṃ me
children.translated_text: As for the grief of the lord of men caused by me, which you mention, that is not pleasing to me;
for he is distressed, amid meetings that are like dreams, over a separation still to come.

children.text: evaṃ ca te niścayametu buddhirdṛṣṭvā vicitraṃ jagataḥ pracāram
children.translated_text: Therefore let your understanding come to this certainty, after seeing the varied course of the world:

children.text: saṃtāpaheturna suto na bandhurajñānanaimittika eṣa tāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the cause of anguish is not son or kinsman; this suffering has ignorance as its cause.

children.text: yathādhvagānamiha saṃgatānāṃ kāle viyogo niyataḥ prajānām
children.translated_text: As separation in time is certain here for travelers who have come together,

children.text: prājño janaḥ ko nu bhajeta śokaṃ bandhupratijñātajanairvihīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so, when creatures are bereft of people merely called relatives, what wise person would indulge in grief?

children.text: ihaiti hitvā svajanaṃ paratra pralabhya cehāpi punaḥ prayāti
children.translated_text: Here one comes after leaving one's own people elsewhere; having obtained them here too, one again goes away;

children.text: gatvāpi tatrāpyaparatra gacchatyevaṃ jane tyāgini ko 'nurodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even after going there, one goes on elsewhere; among people who thus leave one another, what attachment can there be?

children.text: yadā ca garbhātprabhṛti pravṛttaḥ sarvāsvavasthāsu vadhāya mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: And since death has been active from the womb onward, for killing in every condition,
why did Your Honor, loving your son, say that my resort to the forest was untimely?
There is an improper time for the attainment of sense-objects, and a proper time too is prescribed for accomplishing worldly aims,

children.text: kālo jagatkarṣati sarvakālānnirvāhake śreyasi nāsti kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but time drags the world away at every moment; for the saving highest good there is no fixed time.

children.text: rājyaṃ mumukṣurmayi yacca rājā tadapyudāraṃ sadṛśaṃ pituśca
children.translated_text: And that the king wishes to hand over the kingdom to me is noble and fitting for a father,

children.text: pratigrahītuṃ mama na kṣamaṃ tu lobhādapathyānnamivāturasya ||
children.translated_text: but it is not proper for me to accept it, like unwholesome food accepted through greed by a sick man.

children.text: kathaṃ nu mohāyatanaṃ nṛpatvaṃ kṣamaṃ prapattuṃ viduṣā nareṇa
children.translated_text: How could a wise man properly attain kingship, an abode of delusion,

children.text: sodvegatā yatra madaḥ śramaśca parāpacāreṇa ca dharmapīḍā ||
children.translated_text: where there are anxiety, intoxication, toil, and the oppression of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) through wrongs done to others?
For kingship is lovely and also a support of calamity, like a golden palace on fire, like the finest food mixed with poison,

children.text: grāhākulaṃ cāmbviva sāravindaṃ rājyaṃ hi ramyaṃ vyasanāśrayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and like water with lotuses but filled with crocodiles.

children.text: itthaṃ ca rājyaṃ na sukhaṃ na dharmaḥ pūrve yathā jātaghṛṇā narendrāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus kingship is neither happiness nor <s>dharma</s>; in former times, when kings had come to feel disgust,
they abandoned their kingdoms at the advance of age, when unavoidable suffering was present, and went only to the forest.

children.text: varaṃ hi bhuktāni tṛṇānyaraṇye toṣaṃ paraṃ ratnamivopagṛhya
children.translated_text: Better indeed are grasses eaten in the wilderness, after taking hold of contentment as a supreme jewel,
and not a life spent with faults that come easily with royal splendor, unseen like black serpents.

children.text: ślāghyaṃ hi rājyāni vihāya rājñāṃ dharmābhilāṣeṇa vanaṃ praveṣṭum
children.translated_text: For it is praiseworthy for kings to abandon kingdoms and enter the forest from longing for <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: bhagnapratijñasya na tūpapannaṃ vanaṃ parityajya gṛhaṃ praveṣṭum ||
children.translated_text: but it is not proper for one whose vow is broken to abandon the forest and enter the house.

children.text: jātaḥ kule ko hi naraḥ sasattvo dharmābhilāṣeṇa vanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: For what spirited man, born in a noble family and entered into the forest from longing for <s>dharma</s>,
would cast off the ocher robe, shameless in his freedom, and resort even to the city of <s>Purandara</s>?

children.text: lobhāddhi mohādathavā bhayena yo vāntamannaṃ punarādadīta
children.translated_text: For one who, from greed or from delusion or from fear, would take up again food he had vomited,

children.text: lobhātsa mohādathavā bhayena saṃtyajya kāmān punarādadīta ||
children.translated_text: that man, from greed or from delusion or from fear, would take up again the desires he had abandoned.
And one who somehow escaped from a burning shelter and then entered that very place again,
would, after abandoning household life and seeing its faults, desire through delusion to take it up again.

children.text: yā ca śrutirmokṣamavāptavanto nṛpā gṛhasthā iti naitadasti
children.translated_text: And the report that kings who were householders attained liberation is not true;

children.text: śamapradhānaḥ kva ca mokṣadharmo daṇḍapradhānaḥ kva ca rājadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where is the discipline of liberation, in which tranquility is chief, and where is royal duty, in which punishment is chief?

children.text: śame ratiścecchithilaṃ ca rājyaṃ rājye matiścecchamaviplavaśca
children.translated_text: If there is delight in tranquility, the kingdom is slack; if there is intent on kingship, tranquility is disturbed.

children.text: śamaśca taikṣṇyaṃ ca hi nopapannaṃ śītoṣṇayor aikyam ivodakāgnyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: For tranquility and severity do not go together, like the unity of cold and heat, or of water and fire.
Therefore either those lords of the earth, from firm certainty, abandoned kingdoms and attained tranquility,
or, while still marked by kingship, because their senses were restrained, they merely imagined themselves makers of a liberation that was not final.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca rājye 'stu śamo yathāvatprāpto vanaṃ nāhamaniścayena
children.translated_text: Let there be proper tranquility in their kingship; I have not gone to the forest from uncertainty.

children.text: chittvā hi pāśaṃ gṛhabandhusaṃjñaṃ muktaḥ punarna pravivikṣurasmi ||
children.translated_text: For, having cut the snare called house and kin, I am free and do not wish to enter it again.
Hearing the king's son speak in this way, in keeping with the virtues of self-knowledge, free from longing,
reasoned and forceful, the counselor too gave a reply.

children.text: yo niścayo dharmavidhau tavāyaṃ nāyaṃ na yukto na tu kālayuktaḥ
children.translated_text: This resolve of yours concerning the rule of <s>dharma</s> is not improper, but it is not suited to the time;

children.text: śokāya dattvā pitaraṃ vayaḥsthaṃ syāddharmakāmasya hi te na dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for if you hand your aged father over to grief, for you who desire <s>dharma</s> it would not be <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nūnaṃ ca buddhistava nātisūkṣmā dharmārthakāmeṣvavicakṣaṇā vā
children.translated_text: Surely your understanding is not very subtle, or it is unskilled regarding <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire,

children.text: hetoradṛṣṭasya phalasya yastvaṃ pratyakṣam arthaṃ paribhūya yāsi ||
children.translated_text: since you despise a visible good and go away for the sake of an unseen result whose cause is unseen.
Some say that rebirth exists, while others, firm in their doctrine, say that it does not exist;
since this matter is thus doubtful, it is therefore proper to enjoy the royal fortune that is present.

children.text: bhūyaḥ pravṛttiryadi kācidasti raṃsyāmahe tatra yathopapattau
children.translated_text: If there is some further existence, we shall take pleasure there according to what comes about;

children.text: atha pravṛttiḥ parato na kācitsiddhau 'prayatnājjagato 'sya mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but if there is no further existence hereafter, the liberation of this world is accomplished without effort.

children.text: astīti kecitparalokamāhurmokṣasya yogaṃ na tu varṇayanti
children.translated_text: Some say that another world exists, but they do not describe a means to liberation;

children.text: agneryathā hyauṣṇyam apāṃ dravatvaṃ tadvatpravṛttau prakṛtiṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: for they say that activity follows nature, just as heat belongs to fire and liquidity to water.

children.text: kecitsvabhāvāditi varṇayanti śubhāśubhaṃ caiva bhavābhavau ca
children.translated_text: Some describe good and evil, and coming-to-be and non-coming-to-be, as due to inherent nature;

children.text: svābhāvikaṃ sarvamidaṃ ca yasmādato 'pi mogho bhavati prayatnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and since all this is natural, for that reason effort too becomes useless.

children.text: yadindriyāṇāṃ niyataḥ pracāraḥ priyāpriyatvaṃ viṣayeṣu caiva
children.translated_text: The fixed activity of the senses, and lovableness and unlovableness among objects,

children.text: saṃyujyate yajjarayārtibhiśca kastatra yatno nanu sa svabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the fact that one is joined with old age and ailments: what effort is there in that? Surely that is nature.

children.text: adbhirhutāśaḥ śamamabhyupaiti tejāṃsi cāpo gamayanti śoṣam
children.translated_text: Fire comes to cessation through waters, and fiery things make waters dry up;

children.text: bhinnāni bhūtāni śarīrasaṃsthānyaikyaṃ ca gatvā jagadudvahanti ||
children.translated_text: the elements, though separate, when established in bodies come to unity and sustain the world.
That the state of one in the womb is formed with hands, feet, belly, back, and head,

children.text: yadātmanastasya ca tena yogaḥ svābhāvikaṃ tatkathayanti tajjñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that the self belonging to it is connected with that body: those who know declare that to be natural.

children.text: kaḥ kaṇṭakasya prakaroti taikṣṇyaṃ vicitrabhāvaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇāṃ vā
children.translated_text: Who makes the sharpness of a thorn, or the varied condition of beasts and birds?

children.text: svabhāvataḥ sarvamidaṃ pravṛttaṃ na kāmakāro 'sti kutaḥ prayatnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All this proceeds by nature; there is no willful making, so where could effort come from?

children.text: sargaṃ vadantīśvaratastathānye tatra prayatne puruṣasya ko 'rthaḥ
children.translated_text: Others likewise say that creation comes from <s>Īśvara</s>; then what purpose is there in a person's effort?

children.text: ya eva heturjagataḥ pravṛttau heturnivṛttau niyataḥ sa eva ||
children.translated_text: The very cause fixed for the world's arising is also the cause fixed for its cessation.
Some say that manifestation and the destruction of existence have the self alone as their cause.
but they declare that manifestation occurs without effort, and they say that the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> comes through effort.

children.text: naraḥ pitṝṇām anṛṇaḥ prajābhir vedair ṛṣīṇāṃ kratubhiḥ surāṇām
children.translated_text: A man is free from debt to the ancestors by offspring, to the seers by the Vedas, and to the gods by sacrifices;

children.text: utpadyate sārdhamṛṇaistribhistairyasyāsti mokṣaḥ kila tasya mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is born together with those three debts, and he who has release from them, for him, they say, there is release.

children.text: ityevametena vidhikrameṇa mokṣaṃ sayatnasya vadanti tajjñāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, according to this prescribed sequence, those who know that doctrine say that <s>mokṣa</s> belongs to one who makes effort;
for even those who strive, seekers of liberation, incur weariness through exertion.

children.text: tatsaumya mokṣe yadi bhaktirasti nyāyena sevasva vidhiṃ yathoktam
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, if you have devotion to <s>mokṣa</s>, follow the rule rightly, just as it has been taught.
In this way there will be success in this matter, and the burning grief of the lord of men will be destroyed.

children.text: yā ca pravṛttā tava doṣabuddhistapovanebhyo bhavanaṃ praveṣṭum
children.translated_text: And as for the thought of fault that has arisen in you about entering a house from the ascetic groves,

children.text: tatrāpi cintā tava tāta mā bhūt pūrve 'pi jagmuḥ svagṛhānvanebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not be anxious about that either, dear son; in former times too men went from forests to their own homes.
Even while dwelling in an ascetic grove, King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, surrounded by his subjects, went to the city.
So too <s>Rāma</s>, coming from the ascetic grove, protected the earth when it had been injured by ignoble men.

children.text: tathaiva śālvādhipatirdrumākhyo vanāt sasūnur nagaraṃ viveśa
children.translated_text: Likewise the ruler of <s>Śālva</s>, named <s>Druma</s>, entered the city from the forest together with his son;
and <s>Rantideva</s> of the <s>Sāṃkṛti</s> line, having become a brahmarṣi, received sovereignty from the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Men of this kind, blazing with <s>dharma</s> and fame, left the forests and came to their houses.
Therefore there is no fault in going home from an ascetic grove, precisely for the sake of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tato vacastasya niśamya mantriṇaḥ priyaṃ hitaṃ caiva nṛpasya cakṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the minister's speech, dear and beneficial, from the king's very eye,
complete, unconfused, unattached, and unhurried, the king's son, standing firm in resolve, spoke these words:

children.text: ihāsti nāstīti ya eṣa saṃśayaḥ parasya vākyairna mamātra niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Whether there is this or there is not, this doubt cannot be settled for me here by another's words.

children.text: avetya tattvaṃ tapasā śamena ca svayaṃ grahīṣyāmi yadatra niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Having discerned the truth by ascetic practice and tranquillity, I myself shall grasp what is certain in this matter.

children.text: na me kṣamaṃ saṃśayajaṃ hi darśanaṃ grahītumavyaktaparasparāhatam
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for me to accept a view born of doubt, indistinct and mutually contradictory;

children.text: budhaḥ parapratyayato hi ko vrajejjano 'ndhakāre 'ndha ivāndhadeśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what wise man would proceed on another's conviction, like a blind man in darkness with a blind guide?

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvasya sato 'pi kiṃ tu me śubhāśubhe saṃśayite śubhe matiḥ
children.translated_text: But though I have not seen the truth, when good and evil are uncertain, my mind is set on the good.

children.text: vṛthāpi khedo hi varaṃ śubhātmanaḥ sukhaṃ na tattve 'pi vigarhitātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For hardship, even if fruitless, is preferable for a good-natured man; not pleasure, even if true, for one whose self is blameworthy.

children.text: imaṃ tu dṛṣṭvāgamamavyavasthitaṃ yaduktam āptais tad avehi sādhviti
children.translated_text: But seeing this scriptural tradition to be unsettled, as for what was said by trustworthy men, 'Understand that as sound,'

children.text: prahīṇadoṣatvamavehi cāptatāṃ prahīṇadoṣo hyanṛtaṃ na vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: understand freedom from faults to be trustworthiness; for one whose faults are abandoned will not speak falsely.

children.text: gṛhapraveśaṃ prati yacca me bhavānuvāca rāmaprabhṛtīnnidarśanam
children.translated_text: And as to what you said to me about entering a house, citing <s>Rāma</s> and the others as examples,

children.text: na te pramāṇaṃ na hi dharmaniścayeṣvalaṃ pramāṇāya parikṣatavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are not authoritative; for men whose vows have been broken are not sufficient as authority in decisions about <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tadevamapyeva ravirmahī patedapi sthiratvaṃ himavān giristyajet
children.translated_text: Even so, the sun might fall to the earth, and the mountain <s>Himavān</s> might abandon its firmness,

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvo viṣayonmukhendriyaḥ śrayeya na tveva gṛhān pṛthagjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I, an ordinary man who has not seen the truth and whose senses face toward objects, would never resort to a house.

children.text: ahaṃ viśeyaṃ jvalitaṃ hutāśanaṃ na cākṛtārthaḥ praviśeyamālayam
children.translated_text: I would enter a blazing sacrificial fire; I would not enter a dwelling without having accomplished my purpose."

children.text: iti pratijñāṃ sa cakāra garvito yatheṣṭamutthāya ca nirmamo yayau ||
children.translated_text: Thus he made his proud vow and, rising up at will, went away, free from possessiveness.

children.text: tataḥ sabāṣpau sacivadvijāvubhau niśamya tasya sthirameva niścayam
children.translated_text: Then the two, the minister and the brahmin, tearful, hearing his decision as fixed,
with dejected faces, sorrowfully following after him, slowly and helplessly went back to the city.

children.text: tatsnehādatha nṛpateśca bhaktitastau sāpekṣaṃ pratiyayatuśca tasthatuśca
children.translated_text: Then, from affection for him and from devotion to the king, the two turned back with longing and also stood still;

children.text: durdharṣaṃ ravimiva dīptamātmabhāsā taṃ draṣṭuṃ na hi pathi śekaturna moktum ||
children.translated_text: for on the road they could neither look at him, unassailable like the sun and blazing with his own radiance, nor let him go.

children.text: tau jñātuṃ paramagatergatiṃ tu tasya pracchannāṃścarapuruṣāñchucīnvidhāya
children.translated_text: But in order to learn the course of that man whose goal was supreme, they appointed pure men as hidden spies,

children.text: rājānaṃ priyasutalālasaṃ nu gatvā drakṣyāvaḥ kathamiti jagmatuḥ kathaṃcit ||
children.translated_text: and thinking, "How shall we go and see the king, longing for his dear son?" they somehow departed.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye kumārānveṣaṇo nāma navamaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the ninth canto, named <s>Kumārānveṣaṇa</s>, "The Search for the Prince."
That king's son, with broad and full chest, left behind those two who were charged with oblation and mantra,

children.text: uttīrya gaṅgāṃ pracalattaraṅgāṃ śrīmadgṛhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with its moving waves, and went to the splendid abode, <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: śailaiḥ suguptaṃ ca vibhūṣitaṃ ca dhṛtaṃ ca pūtaṃ ca śivaistapodaiḥ
children.translated_text: Well guarded and adorned by mountains, sustained and purified by auspicious hot springs,

children.text: pañcācalāṅkaṃ nagaraṃ prapede śāntaḥ svayaṃbhūriva nākapṛṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: he reached the city marked by five hills, peaceful as <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> reaching the summit of heaven.

children.text: gāmbhīryamojaśca niśāmya tasya vapuśca dīptaṃ puruṣānatītya
children.translated_text: When the people there observed his depth, his vigor, and his radiant body surpassing men,
they marveled then, as if at the bull-bannered <s>Śiva</s>, firm in his ascetic vow.

children.text: taṃ prekṣya yo 'nyena yayau sa tasthau yastatra tasthau pathi so 'nvagacchat
children.translated_text: Whoever, after seeing him, was going elsewhere stopped; whoever stood there on the road followed him.

children.text: drutaṃ yayau yaḥ sa jagāma dhīraṃ yaḥ kaścidāste sma sa cotpapāta ||
children.translated_text: Whoever was going quickly went slowly, and whoever was seated sprang up.

children.text: kaścittamānarca janaḥ karābhyāṃ satkṛtya kaścicchirasā vavande
children.translated_text: One person honored him with joined hands; another, showing respect, bowed with his head.
Another greeted him with affectionate speech; no one went on without first paying him honor.

children.text: taṃ jihriyuḥ prekṣya vicitraveṣāḥ prakīrṇavācaḥ pathi maunamīyuḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him, people of varied dress and scattered speech grew bashful and fell silent on the road.
As if in the very presence of <s>dharma</s>, no one had a mind turned toward injustice.

children.text: anyakriyāṇāmapi rājamārge strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ vā bahumānapūrvam
children.translated_text: Even for women or men engaged in other activities on the royal road, with reverence,

children.text: taṃ devakalpaṃ naradevasūnuṃ nirīkṣamāṇā na tatarpa dṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: their sight was not satisfied as they gazed at that godlike son of the king of men.

children.text: bhruvau lalāṭaṃ mukhamīkṣaṇe vā vapuḥ karau vā caraṇau gatiṃ vā
children.translated_text: Whether at his brows, his forehead, his face, his eyes, his body, his hands, his feet, or his gait,

children.text: yadeva yastasya dadarśa tatra tadeva tasyātha babandha cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever each person saw of him there, on that very thing each person's eye then became fixed.
And seeing him, with the tuft of hair between his brows, long-eyed, his body blazing, his hands marked with auspicious webbing,

children.text: taṃ bhikṣuveṣaṃ kṣitipālanārhaṃ saṃcukṣubhe rājagṛhasya lakṣmīḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fortune of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was stirred by him, in a mendicant's dress though worthy to protect the earth.
Then <s>Śreṇya</s>, lord of the Magadhan court, from an outer palace saw the vast flood of people.

children.text: dadarśa papraccha ca tasya hetuṃ tatastamasmai puruṣaḥ śaśaṃsa ||
children.translated_text: He saw it and asked the reason for it; then a man reported it to him.

children.text: jñānaṃ paraṃ vā pṛthivīśriyaṃ vā viprairya ukto 'dhigamiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: "He of whom the brahmins said, 'He will attain supreme knowledge or the splendor of the earth,'

children.text: sa eṣa śākyādhipatestanūjo nirīkṣyate pravrajito janena ||
children.translated_text: this is that son of the <s>Śākya</s> ruler, gone forth, being gazed upon by the people."

children.text: tataḥ śrutārtho manasāgatāstho rājā babhāṣe puruṣaṃ tameva
children.translated_text: Then the king, having heard the matter and set it in his mind, spoke to that same man:
"Find out where he is going." Saying "So be it," the man then followed him.
With eyes not restless, seeing only the length of a yoke before him, his speech restrained and his slow gait controlled,

children.text: cacāra bhikṣāṃ sa tu bhikṣuvaryo nidhāya gātrāṇi calaṃ ca cetaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that best of mendicants went for alms, composing his limbs and his unsteady mind.

children.text: ādāya bhaikṣaṃ ca yathopapannaṃ yayau gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ viviktam
children.translated_text: Taking alms just as they came to him, he went to a secluded spring of the mountain.
After eating there according to rule, he climbed that mountain, <s>Pāṇḍava</s>.
There, in a hollow embraced by lodhra groves, its thickets filled with the cries of peacocks,

children.text: kāṣāyavāsāḥ sa babhau nṛsūryo yathodayasyopari bālasūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sun among men, clothed in ochre robes, shone like the young sun above <s>Udaya</s>.

children.text: tatrainamālokya sa rājabhṛtyaḥ śreṇyāya rājñe kathayāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: Seeing him there, that royal servant reported it to King <s>Śreṇya</s>.

children.text: saṃśrutya rājā sa ca bāhumānyāttatra pratasthe nibhṛtānuyātraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the king, hearing it, out of great respect set out there with a quiet retinue.
He ascended <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, that excellent mountain; his valor matched <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, and his body was like a mountain.
Wearing his diadem, with a lion's gait, that lion among men climbed like a lion with its mane tossing.

children.text: tataḥ sma tasyopari śṛṅgabhūtaṃ śāntendriyaṃ paśyati bodhisattvam
children.translated_text: Then on its summit he saw the Bodhisattva, with senses calmed,
sitting cross-legged and shining like the moon rising from a bank of clouds.

children.text: taṃ rūpalakṣmyā ca śamena caiva dharmasya nirmāṇamivopaviṣṭam
children.translated_text: Him, by beauty of form and by tranquillity, seated as if he were the embodied form of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: savismayaḥ praśrayavān narendraḥ svayaṃbhuvaṃ śakra ivopatasthe ||
children.translated_text: the king approached with wonder and reverence, like <s>Śakra</s> approaching <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.

children.text: taṃ nyāyato nyāyavidāṃ variṣṭhaṃ sametya papraccha ca dhātusāmyam
children.translated_text: Having come to him properly, to the foremost of those who know propriety, he asked about the balance of his bodily elements.

children.text: sa cāpyavocatsadṛśena sāmnā nṛpaṃ manaḥsvāsthyamanāmayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And he too, with fitting courtesy, told the king of his mental well-being and freedom from illness.

children.text: tataḥ śucau vāraṇakarṇanīle śilātale saṃniṣasāda rājā
children.translated_text: Then the king sat down on a clean stone slab, blue like an elephant's ear.
Having sat near him with his permission, and wishing to know his disposition, he said this:

children.text: prītiḥ parā me bhavataḥ kulena kramāgatā caiva parīkṣitā ca
children.translated_text: "I have the highest affection for your family, inherited in succession and also proved by experience.

children.text: jātā vivakṣā svavayo yato me tasmādidaṃ snehavaco nibodha ||
children.translated_text: Since a desire to speak has arisen in me, because your age is like my own, listen to this affectionate word.

children.text: ādityapūrvaṃ vipulaṃ kulaṃ te navaṃ vayo dīptamidaṃ vapuśca
children.translated_text: Your family is vast, descended from <s>Āditya</s>; your age is young, and this body is brilliant.

children.text: kasmādiyaṃ te matirakrameṇa bhaikṣāka evābhiratā na rājye ||
children.translated_text: Why has this thought of yours, out of due order, become devoted only to alms-begging and not to kingship?
For your body deserves red sandalwood; it does not deserve this contact with ochre cloth.

children.text: hastaḥ prajāpālanayogya eṣa bhoktuṃ na cārhaḥ paradattamannam ||
children.translated_text: This hand is fit for protecting subjects, and it is not fit to eat food given by another.

children.text: tatsaumya rājyaṃ yadi paitṛkaṃ tvaṃ snehātpiturnecchasi vikrameṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, if from affection for your father you do not wish to take your paternal kingdom by force,

children.text: na ca kramaṃ marṣayituṃ matiste bhuṅkṣvārdham asmadviṣayasya śīghram ||
children.translated_text: and if your mind cannot endure waiting for the proper succession, quickly enjoy half of my realm.

children.text: evaṃ hi na syātsvajanāvamardaḥ kālakrameṇāpi śamaśrayā śrīḥ
children.translated_text: For in this way there would be no trampling of your own people, and in due course prosperity would rest on peace.

children.text: tasmātkuruṣva praṇayaṃ mayi tvaṃ sadbhiḥ sahīyā hi satāṃ samṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore show affection toward me; for the prosperity of the good is stronger when joined with the good.

children.text: atha tvidānīṃ kulagarvitatvādasmāsu viśrambhaguṇo na te 'sti
children.translated_text: But if now, through pride in your family, there is no quality of trust toward us in you,

children.text: vyūḍhānyanīkāni vigāhya bāṇairmayā sahāyena parān jigīṣa ||
children.translated_text: then, plunging into arrayed armies, conquer your enemies with arrows, with me as your ally.
Therefore choose one of these two policies here, and duly pursue <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (power and wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure).

children.text: vyatyasya rāgādiha hi trivargaṃ pretyeha ca bhraṃśamavāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: For by inverting the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims) here out of passion and the like, people meet ruin both after death and in this life.

children.text: yo hyarthadharmau paripīḍya kāmaḥ syāddharmakāmau paribhūya cārthaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) that oppresses <s>artha</s> and <s>dharma</s>, or <s>artha</s> that disregards <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>,

children.text: kāmārthayoścoparameṇa dharmastyājyaḥ sa kṛtsno yadi kāṅkṣito 'rthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or <s>dharma</s> that comes by the cessation of <s>kāma</s> and <s>artha</s>: each is to be wholly abandoned if the goal is desired.
Therefore, by practicing the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims), make this beauty of yours fruitful.
For they say that the complete attainment of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> is the complete human aim for men.

children.text: tanniṣphalau nārhasi kartumetau pīnau bhujau cāpavikarṣaṇārhau
children.translated_text: You should not make fruitless these two full arms, fit for drawing a bow.

children.text: māndhātṛvaj jetum imau hi yogyau lokānapi trīniha kiṃ punargām ||
children.translated_text: For these are fit to conquer even the three worlds like <s>Māndhātṛ</s> here, how much more the earth.

children.text: snehena khalvetadahaṃ bravīmi naiśvaryarāgeṇa na vismayena
children.translated_text: Indeed I say this from affection, not from passion for sovereignty and not from amazement.

children.text: imaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā tava bhikṣuveṣaṃ jātānukampo 'smyapi cāgatāśruḥ ||
children.translated_text: For on seeing this mendicant's dress of yours, I have felt compassion and even tears have come.

children.text: yāvat svavaṃśapratirūpaṃ rūpaṃ na te jarābhyetyabhibhūya bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as old age has not yet come upon your form, a form worthy of your lineage, and overpowered it further,

children.text: tadbhuṅkṣva bhikṣāśramakāma kāmān kāle 'si kartā priyadharma dharmam ||
children.translated_text: therefore enjoy pleasures, you who desire the toil of begging; in time, lover of <s>dharma</s>, you will practice <s>dharma</s>.
An old man indeed can attain <s>dharma</s>; old age has no access to the enjoyment of pleasures.

children.text: ataśca yūnaḥ kathayanti kāmānmadhyasya vittaṃ sthavirasya dharmam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they assign pleasures to the young man, wealth to the man in middle life, and <s>dharma</s> to the elder.

children.text: dharmasya cārthasya ca jīvaloke pratyarthibhūtāni hi yauvanāni
children.translated_text: For in the world of living beings, youths are hostile to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.

children.text: saṃrakṣyamāṇānyapi durgrahāṇi kāmā yatastena pathā haranti ||
children.translated_text: Since desires, hard to control even when guarded, carry them away along that path.
Aged years are reflective, steady, devoted to firmness,

children.text: alpena yatnena śamātmakāni bhavantyagatyaiva ca lajjayā ca ||
children.translated_text: with little effort, and through sheer incapacity and shame, they become calm in nature.

children.text: ataśca lolaṃ viṣayapradhānaṃ pramattam akṣāntam adīrghadarśi
children.translated_text: Therefore youth is fickle, dominated by sense-objects, heedless, impatient, and short-sighted,
and after passing beyond that much-deceiving youth, people breathe freely as if they had crossed a wilderness.
Therefore let this unsteady, restless, heedless new age first pass away;

children.text: kāmasya pūrvaṃ hi vayaḥ śaravyaṃ na śakyate rakṣitumindriyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for early age is the first target of desire and cannot be guarded from the senses.

children.text: atho cikīrṣā tava dharma eva yajasva yajñaṃ kuladharma eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: But if your wish is solely for <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), perform a sacrifice; this is the <s>dharma</s> of your family.

children.text: yajñairadhiṣṭhāya hi nāgapṛṣṭhaṃ yayau marutvānapi nākapṛṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: For by sacrifices even <s>Marutvān</s>, mounted on the back of his elephant, went to the back of heaven.
Royal seers, their arms clasped by golden armlets and their bright, variegated diadems shining with jewels like lamps,

children.text: nṛparṣayastāṃ hi gatiṃ gatā makhaiḥ śrameṇa yāmeva maharṣayo yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: went through sacrifices to that same state which the great seers reached through toil.

children.text: ityevaṃ magadhapatirvaco babhāṣe yaḥ samyag valabhid iva bruvan babhāse
children.translated_text: Thus the lord of <s>Magadha</s> spoke his words; speaking rightly, he shone like <s>Valabhid</s>.

children.text: tacchrutvā na sa vicacāla rājasūnuḥ kailāso giririva naikacitrasānuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king's son did not waver, like Mount <s>Kailāsa</s> with its many bright peaks.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'śvaghoṣakṛte śreṇyābhigamano nāma daśamaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth canto, named <s>Śreṇyābhigamana</s>, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s> composed by <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>.
Then, thus addressed by the ruler of <s>Magadha</s> with a friend's voice but with a meaning contrary to his purpose,
the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, steady, unchanged, and pure in lineage and conduct, spoke these words:
This disposition of yours is no wonder, born as you are in the great <s>Haryaṅka</s> line,
that, being of pure conduct and desiring a friend's good, your behavior should be this way on a friend's side.

children.text: asatsu maitrī svakulānuvṛttā na tiṣṭhati śrīriva viklaveṣu
children.translated_text: Friendship among the bad, even when inherited through one's family, does not last, like fortune among the faint-hearted;
but the good, through successions of affection made by their forebears, make that very friendship grow.

children.text: ye cārthakṛcchreṣu bhavanti loke samānakāryāḥ suhṛdāṃ manuṣyāḥ
children.translated_text: And those people in the world who, when their friends are in difficulty, share the same purpose,

children.text: mitrāṇi tānīti paraimi buddhyā svasthasya vṛddhiṣviha ko hi na syāt ||
children.translated_text: I judge by my understanding to be friends; for who would not be there in times of prosperity for one who is at ease?

children.text: evaṃ ca ye dravyamavāpya loke mitreṣu dharme ca niyojayanti
children.translated_text: And those who, after obtaining wealth in the world, apply it to friends and to <s>dharma</s> (religious merit),

children.text: avāptasārāṇi dhanāni teṣāṃ bhraṣṭāni nānte janayanti tāpam ||
children.translated_text: their riches, having gained their true substance, do not cause pain at the end when they are lost.

children.text: suhṛttayā cāryatayā ca rājan khalveṣa yo māṃ prati niścayaste
children.translated_text: And, king, because of friendship and nobility, this decision of yours toward me is indeed such;
on this point I shall answer only in friendship; I would not speak any other reply here.

children.text: ahaṃ jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ viditvā mumukṣayā dharmamimaṃ prapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing the fear of old age and death, I have entered upon this <s>dharma</s> (path) out of a longing for liberation,

children.text: bandhūn priyānaśrumukhānvihāya prāgeva kāmān aśubhasya hetūn ||
children.translated_text: leaving dear kinsmen with tear-filled faces, and still more leaving desires, the causes of what is unwholesome.

children.text: nāśīviṣebhyo hi tathā bibhemi naivāśanibhyo gaganāccyutebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not fear venomous serpents so much, nor thunderbolts fallen from the sky,

children.text: na pāvakebhyo 'nilasaṃhitebhyo yathā bhayaṃ me viṣayebhya eva ||
children.translated_text: nor fires driven together with wind, as I fear sense-objects themselves.

children.text: kāmā hyanityāḥ kuśalārthacaurā riktāśca māyāsadṛśāśca loke
children.translated_text: For desires are impermanent, thieves of what is wholesome, empty, and like illusions in the world;

children.text: āśāsyamānā api mohayanti cittaṃ nṛṇāṃ kiṃ punarātmasaṃsthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even when merely hoped for, they bewilder men's minds; how much more when they are present within oneself.

children.text: kāmābhibhūtā hi na yānti śarma tripiṣṭape kiṃ bata martyaloke
children.translated_text: Those overcome by desires do not reach peace even in <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>, much less in the mortal world;

children.text: kāmaiḥ satṛṣṇasya hi nāsti tṛptiryathendhanairvātasakhasya vahneḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one who thirsts for desires has no satisfaction, just as fire, the friend of wind, is not satisfied by fuel.

children.text: jagatyanartho na samo 'sti kāmairmohācca teṣveva janaḥ prasaktaḥ
children.translated_text: In the world there is no misfortune equal to desires, and yet from delusion people are attached to those very things;
knowing the truth in this way, what wise man, afraid of misfortune, would himself desire misfortune?
Even after gaining the earth, whose garment is the sea, people wish to conquer the far shore of the great ocean;

children.text: lokasya kāmairna vitṛptirasti patadbhir ambhobhir ivārṇavasya ||
children.translated_text: the world is not satisfied by desires, just as the ocean is not satisfied by falling waters.
Even when the god rained a shower of gold, after all four continents had been conquered,
and even after gaining half the seat of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s> had no satisfaction in sense-objects.

children.text: bhuktvāpi rājyaṃ divi devatānāṃ śatakratau vṛtrabhayātpranaṣṭe
children.translated_text: Even after enjoying the kingship of the gods in heaven, when <s>Śatakratu</s> had fled from fear of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
<s>Nahuṣa</s>, unsatisfied with desires, fell after arrogantly making even the great seers carry him.

children.text: aiḍaśca rājā tridivaṃ vigāhya nītvāpi devīṃ vaśamurvaśīṃ tām
children.translated_text: And King <s>Aiḍa</s>, after entering heaven and bringing that goddess <s>Urvaśī</s> under his control,
wishing out of greed to seize gold from the seers, went to destruction, unsatisfied with sense-objects.
Those enjoyments passed from <s>Bali</s> to <s>Mahendra</s>, from <s>Mahendra</s> to <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and again from <s>Nahuṣa</s> to <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: svarge kṣitau vā viṣayeṣu teṣu ko viśvasedbhāgyakulākuleṣu ||
children.translated_text: who would trust such objects, whether in heaven or on earth, tossed about by fortune and lineage?
Even sages wearing bark garments, eating roots, fruits, and water, and carrying matted locks long as serpents,

children.text: yairnānyakāryā munayo 'pi bhagnāḥ kaḥ kāmasaṃjñānmṛgayeta śatrūn ||
children.translated_text: were broken by those enemies called desires, though they had no other business; who would seek them out?
And <s>Ugrāyudha</s>, though bearing fierce weapons and strongly armed, met death at <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s hands for their sake;

children.text: cintāpi teṣāmaśivā vadhāya sadvṛttināṃ kiṃ punaravratānām ||
children.translated_text: even the thought of them is inauspicious and deadly for people of good conduct; how much more for those without vows?
Recognizing in sense-objects a small taste, a great increase of bondage, and sheer dissatisfaction,

children.text: sadbhyaśca garhāṃ niyataṃ ca pāpaṃ kaḥ kāmasaṃjñaṃ viṣamādadīta ||
children.translated_text: as well as blame from the good and certain sin, who would take up the poison called desire?

children.text: kṛṣyādibhiḥ karmabhirarditānāṃ kāmātmakānāṃ ca niśamya duḥkham
children.translated_text: Having observed the suffering of those oppressed by labors such as farming, and of those whose nature is desire,
and the well-being of those who have no curiosity about desires, self-possessed people may rightly abandon desires.

children.text: jñeyā vipatkāmini kāmasaṃpatsiddheṣu kāmeṣu madaṃ hyupaiti
children.translated_text: For a lover of desire, success in desires should be known as calamity; when desires are attained, a man falls into intoxication.

children.text: madādakāryaṃ kurute na kāryaṃ yena kṣato durgatimabhyupaiti ||
children.translated_text: Through intoxication he does what should not be done and fails to do what should be done; wounded by that, he reaches a bad destiny.

children.text: yatnena labdhāḥ parirakṣitāśca ye vipralabhya pratiyānti bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those desires, gained with effort and guarded carefully, deceive a person and then depart again;
what self-possessed wise man in this world would delight in desires that are like borrowed goods?

children.text: anviṣya cādāya ca jātatarṣā yān atyajantaḥ pariyānti duḥkham
children.translated_text: When thirst has arisen, people seek them out and seize them; not abandoning them, they wander in suffering.

children.text: loke tṛṇolkāsadṛśeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, like burning straw-torches in the world, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: anātmavanto hṛdi yairvidaṣṭā vināśam archanti na yānti śarma
children.translated_text: Those without self-control, bitten in the heart by them, go to destruction and do not reach peace.

children.text: kruddhograsarpapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, resembling angry and terrible serpents, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: asthi kṣudhārtā iva sārameyā bhuktvāpi yānnaiva bhavanti tṛptāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who consume them are like dogs tormented by hunger over a bone: even after eating, they are never satisfied.

children.text: jīrṇāsthikaṅkālasameṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, like skeletons of old bones, what self-possessed person could take delight?
Because they are vulnerable alike to kings, thieves, water, and fire, they produce suffering.

children.text: teṣu praviddhāmiṣasaṃnibheṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, resembling bait thrown out, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: yatra sthitānāmabhito vipattiḥ śatroḥ sakāśādapi bāndhavebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: For those who remain in them, disaster stands on every side, from enemies and even from kinsmen.

children.text: hiṃsreṣu teṣvāyatanopameṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those violent desires, like dangerous haunts, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: girau vane cāpsu ca sāgare ca yān bhraṃśam archanti vilaṅghamānāḥ
children.translated_text: For their sake people overreach and come to ruin on mountains, in forests, in waters, and in the sea.

children.text: teṣu drumaprāgraphalopameṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, like fruit on the top of a tree, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: tīvraiḥ prayatnairvividhairavāptāḥ kṣaṇena ye nāśamiha prayānti
children.translated_text: Though obtained here by intense and varied efforts, they pass to destruction in a moment.

children.text: svapnopabhogapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, resembling enjoyments in a dream, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: yānarjayitvāpi na yānti śarma vivardhayitvā paripālayitvā
children.translated_text: Even after acquiring them, increasing them, and guarding them, people do not reach peace.

children.text: aṅgārakarṣūpratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In those desires, resembling trenches of burning coals, what self-possessed person could take delight?
For whose sake the <s>Kuru</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>Andhaka</s>, <s>Mekhala</s>, and <s>Daṇḍaka</s> peoples went to destruction,

children.text: sūnāsikāṣṭhapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: in those desires, like a butcher's knife and block, what self-possessed person could take delight?
For whose sake the two asuras <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, driven into mutual enmity, were destroyed,

children.text: sauhārdaviśleṣakareṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: in those desires, which bring about the rupture of friendship, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: yeṣāṃ kṛte vāriṇi pāvake ca kravyātsu cātmānam ihotsṛjanti
children.translated_text: For whose sake people here cast themselves into water, into fire, and among beasts that eat flesh,

children.text: sapatnabhūteṣvaśiveṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: in those inauspicious desires that become like rivals, what self-possessed person could take delight?

children.text: kāmārthamajñaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ karoti prāpnoti duḥkhaṃ vadhabandhanādi
children.translated_text: For the sake of desire, an ignorant man does base acts and meets suffering, such as execution and imprisonment.
For the sake of desire, the wretched world of living beings, made poor by hope, incurs death and toil.

children.text: gītair hriyante hi mṛgā vadhāya rūpārthamagnau śalabhāḥ patanti
children.translated_text: For deer are drawn by songs to be killed, and moths fall into fire for the sake of visible form.
A fish seeking bait swallows the iron hook; therefore sense-objects bear harm as their fruit.

children.text: kāmāstu bhogā iti yanmatiḥ syādbhogā na kecitparigaṇyamānāḥ
children.translated_text: But if someone thinks, 'Desires are enjoyments,' when they are examined, they are not enjoyments at all.

children.text: vastrādayo dravyaguṇā hi loke duḥkhapratīkāra iti pradhāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For things in the world, beginning with clothing, should be understood as countermeasures against suffering.

children.text: iṣṭaṃ hi tarṣapraśamāya toyaṃ kṣunnāśahetoraśanaṃ tathaiva
children.translated_text: Water is desired for the calming of thirst, and food likewise as the means for ending hunger.
A house is for shelter from wind, heat, and rain; clothing is for covering the loins and warding off cold.
A bed likewise is for preventing disturbance of sleep, and a vehicle for removing the fatigue of a journey.
So too a seat is for relief from standing, and bathing serves cleanliness, health, and strength.
Therefore sense-objects are causes for counteracting suffering for creatures; they are not enjoyments.
What wise person, engaged in a process of remedy, would accept the thought, 'I am enjoying pleasures'?

children.text: yaḥ pittadāhena vidahyamānaḥ śītakriyāṃ bhoga iti vyavasyet
children.translated_text: If a man burning with the heat of bile should decide that cooling treatment is enjoyment,

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāravidhau pravṛttaḥ kāmeṣu kuryātsa hi bhogasaṃjñām ||
children.translated_text: then, while engaged in counteracting suffering, he might apply the name 'enjoyment' to desires.

children.text: kāmeṣvanaikāntikatā ca yasmādato 'pi me teṣu na bhogasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: And because desires are not invariably pleasant, for this reason too I do not call them enjoyments.

children.text: ya eva bhāvā hi sukhaṃ diśanti ta eva duḥkhaṃ punarāvahanti ||
children.translated_text: For the very states that give happiness bring suffering again.

children.text: gurūṇi vāsāṃsyagurūṇi caiva sukhāya śīte hyasukhāya gharme
children.translated_text: Heavy garments and aloes are pleasant in cold weather, but unpleasant in heat.

children.text: candrāṃśavaścandanameva coṣṇe sukhāya duḥkhāya bhavanti śīte ||
children.translated_text: Moonbeams and sandalwood are pleasant in the heat, but become painful in the cold.
Because pairs of opposites, beginning with loss and gain, cling to everyone in the world,
for this reason too there is no person on earth who is wholly happy or wholly miserable.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vimiśrāṃ sukhaduḥkhatāṃ me rājyaṃ ca dāsyaṃ ca mataṃ samānam
children.translated_text: Seeing happiness and suffering to be mixed, I regard kingship and servitude as the same.

children.text: nityaṃ hasatyeva hi naiva rājā na cāpi saṃtapyata eva dāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a king certainly does not always laugh, nor is a servant always afflicted.

children.text: ājñā nṛpatve 'bhyadhiketi yatsyānmahānti duḥkhānyata eva rājñaḥ
children.translated_text: If authority is especially great in kingship, then from that very fact a king has great sufferings.

children.text: āsaṅgakāṣṭhapratimo hi rājā lokasya hetoḥ parikhedameti ||
children.translated_text: For a king is like a burden-bearing post; for the sake of the world he comes to exhaustion.
In a kingdom ready to desert him and full of enemies, if a king comes to trust, he is ruined.

children.text: athāpi viśrambhamupaiti neha kiṃ nāma saukhyaṃ cakitasya rājñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not find confidence here, what happiness can there be for a frightened king?

children.text: yadā ca jitvāpi mahīṃ samagrāṃ vāsāya dṛṣṭaṃ puramekameva
children.translated_text: And when, even after conquering the whole earth, only one city is seen as a dwelling place,

children.text: tatrāpi caikaṃ bhavanaṃ niṣevyaṃ śramaḥ parārthe nanu rājabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and within that too only one house is to be occupied, is not the state of kingship toil for another's sake?
Even for a king there is only one pair of garments, and likewise only a measure of food to hold back hunger.
So too there is one bed and one seat; the remaining distinctions are for the king's pride.
And if this desired fruit is for the sake of contentment, I have contentment even without kingship.

children.text: tuṣṭau ca satyāṃ puruṣasya loke sarve viśeṣā nanu nirviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when contentment exists for a person in the world, are not all distinctions without distinction?

children.text: tannāsmi kāmān prati saṃpratāryaḥ kṣemaṃ śivaṃ mārgamanuprapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I am not to be lured toward desires, having entered upon a secure and auspicious path.

children.text: smṛtvā suhṛttvaṃ tu punaḥ punarmā brūhi pratijñāṃ khalu pālayeti ||
children.translated_text: But remembering our friendship, tell me again and again, 'Indeed, keep your vow.'

children.text: na hyasmyamarṣeṇa vanaṃ praviṣṭo na śatrubāṇairavadhūtamauliḥ
children.translated_text: For I did not enter the forest out of resentment, nor with my crest struck down by enemies' arrows.

children.text: kṛtaspṛho nāpi phalādhikebhyo gṛhṇāmi naitadvacanaṃ yataste ||
children.translated_text: Nor, because I have come to desire fruits higher than these, do I accept this speech of yours.

children.text: yo dandaśūkaṃ kupitaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ muktvā vyavasyeddhi punargrahītum
children.translated_text: For if a man, after releasing an angry biting serpent, should resolve to seize it again,

children.text: dāhātmikāṃ vā jvalitāṃ tṛṇolkāṃ saṃtyajya kāmānsa punarbhajeta ||
children.translated_text: or if, after throwing away a blazing grass-torch whose nature is to burn, he should return to desires after abandoning them,

children.text: andhāya yaśca spṛhayedanandho baddhāya mukto vidhanāya cāḍhyaḥ
children.translated_text: then a man not blind would long for blindness, one freed would long for bondage, and a wealthy man for poverty;

children.text: unmattacittāya ca kalyacittaḥ spṛhāṃ sa kuryādviṣayātmakāya ||
children.translated_text: one of sound mind would long for a mad mind: such a man would feel longing for a person made of sense-objects.

children.text: bhaikṣopabhogīti ca nānukampyaḥ kṛtī jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ titīrṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is he to be pitied because he lives on alms: he is accomplished and wishes to cross beyond the fear of old age and death,

children.text: ihottamaṃ śāntisukhaṃ ca yasya paratra duḥkhāni ca saṃvṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: for he has here the supreme happiness of peace, and sufferings hereafter have been shut off.
But one who, even while living amid great fortune, is overpowered by thirst is the one to be pitied,

children.text: prāpnoti yaḥ śāntisukhaṃ na ceha paratra duḥkhaiḥ pratigṛhyate ca ||
children.translated_text: for he does not attain the happiness of peace here, and hereafter he is received by sufferings.

children.text: evaṃ tu vaktuṃ bhavato 'nurūpaṃ sattvasya vṛttasya kulasya caiva
children.translated_text: Yet for you to speak in this way is fitting for your character, conduct, and family,

children.text: mamāpi voḍhuṃ sadṛśaṃ pratijñāṃ sattvasya vṛttasya kulasya caiva ||
children.translated_text: and for me too to uphold my vow is fitting for my character, conduct, and family.

children.text: ahaṃ hi saṃsāraśareṇa viddho viniḥsṛtaḥ śāntim avāptukāmaḥ
children.translated_text: For I, pierced by the arrow of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), have gone forth, wishing to attain peace.

children.text: neccheyamāptuṃ tridive 'pi rājyaṃ nirāmayaṃ kiṃ bata mānuṣeṣu ||
children.translated_text: I would not wish to obtain even a painless kingdom in heaven; how much less among human beings.

children.text: trivargasevāṃ nṛpa yattu kṛtsnataḥ paro manuṣyārtha iti tvamāttha mām
children.translated_text: O king, as for what you said to me, that full service of the <s>trivarga</s> (the three aims) is the supreme human end,

children.text: anartha ityeva mamātra darśanaṃ kṣayī trivargo hi na cāpi tarpakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my view here is precisely that it is no true end, for the <s>trivarga</s> is perishable and does not satisfy.
