children.text: pade tu yasminna jarā na bhīrna ruṅ na janma naivoparamo na cādhayaḥ
children.translated_text: But the state in which there is no old age, no fear, no disease, no birth, no cessation, and no afflictions,

children.text: tameva manye puruṣārthamuttamaṃ na vidyate yatra punaḥ punaḥ kriyā ||
children.translated_text: that alone I consider the highest human goal, where repeated action is not found.

children.text: yad apyavocaḥ paripālyatāṃ jarā navaṃ vayo gacchati vikriyāmiti
children.translated_text: And as for what you said, 'Let old age be waited for; fresh youth passes into change,'

children.text: aniścayo 'yaṃ capalaṃ hi dṛśyate jarāpyadhīrā dhṛtimacca yauvanam ||
children.translated_text: this is uncertain: instability is indeed seen, for old age too lacks firmness, and youth can be firm.

children.text: svakarmadakṣaśca yadāntako jagad vayaḥsu sarveṣvavaśaṃ vikarṣati
children.translated_text: And since Death, skillful in its own work, drags the helpless world away at every age,

children.text: vināśakāle kathamavyavasthite jarā pratīkṣyā viduṣā śamepsunā ||
children.translated_text: how should old age be awaited by a wise man seeking peace, when the time of destruction is not fixed?

children.text: jarāyudho vyādhivikīrṇasāyako yadāntako vyādha ivāśivaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When Death stands like an inauspicious hunter, armed with old age and scattering arrows of disease,

children.text: prajāmṛgān bhāgyavanāśritāṃstudan vayaḥprakarṣaṃ prati ko manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: striking the deer of creatures who have taken shelter in the forest of fortune, what desire can there be for length of years?

children.text: ato yuvā vā sthaviro 'thavā śiśustathā tvarāvāniha kartumarhati
children.translated_text: Therefore, whether young, aged, or still a child, one ought to act here with such urgency

children.text: yathā bhaveddharmavataḥ kṛtātmanaḥ pravṛttiriṣṭā vinivṛttireva vā ||
children.translated_text: that for a disciplined person possessing <s>dharma</s> (the right path), either desired engagement or withdrawal may come about.

children.text: yadāttha cāpīṣṭaphalāṃ kulocitāṃ kuruṣva dharmāya makhakriyāmiti
children.translated_text: And as for what you also said, 'For <s>dharma</s>, perform the sacrificial rite that gives desired fruit and befits your family,'

children.text: namo makhebhyo na hi kāmaye sukhaṃ parasya duḥkhakriyayā yadiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: my respects to sacrifices; I do not desire a happiness that is sought by causing pain to another.

children.text: paraṃ hi hantuṃ vivaśaṃ phalepsayā na yuktarūpaṃ karuṇātmanaḥ sataḥ
children.translated_text: For to kill another helpless being out of longing for fruit is not fitting for a good person whose nature is compassion.

children.text: kratoḥ phalaṃ yadyapi śāśvataṃ bhavettathāpi kṛtvā kimu yatkṣayātmakam ||
children.translated_text: Even if the fruit of a sacrifice were eternal, still, after performing an act whose nature is destruction, what would be the point?

children.text: bhavecca dharmo yadi nāparo vidhirvratena śīlena manaḥśamena vā
children.translated_text: And even if this were <s>dharma</s>, if there were no other method through vows, conduct, or tranquillity of mind,

children.text: tathāpi naivārhati sevituṃ kratuṃ viśasya yasmin paramucyate phalam ||
children.translated_text: still one should not practice a sacrifice in which the fruit is said to come from slaughtering another.

children.text: ihāpi tāvatpuruṣasya tiṣṭhataḥ pravartate yatparahiṃsayā sukham
children.translated_text: Even here, while a man is alive, whatever pleasure arises through harming another

children.text: tadapyaniṣṭaṃ saghṛṇasya dhīmato bhavāntare kiṃ bata yanna dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: is undesirable to a compassionate wise person; how much more so in another existence, where it is not seen.

children.text: na ca pratāryo 'smi phalapravṛttaye bhaveṣu rājan ramate na me manaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor am I to be deceived into activity for the sake of fruit, O king; my mind does not delight in states of becoming.

children.text: latā ivāmbhodharavṛṣṭitāḍitāḥ pravṛttayaḥ sarvagatā hi cañcalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For activities everywhere are unsteady, like creepers beaten by rain from a cloud.
I came here from there because I wished to see the sage <s>Arāḍa</s>, who teaches liberation.

children.text: prayāmi cādyaiva nṛpāstu te śivaṃ vacaḥ kṣamethā mama tattvaniṣṭhuram ||
children.translated_text: And I shall depart this very day, O king; may there be welfare for you. Please forgive my words, harsh because they are true.

children.text: avendravad divyava śaśvadarkavad guṇair ava śreya ihāva gām ava
children.translated_text: Protect, like <s>Indra</s>, the heavenly realm; like the sun, always protect welfare here with your virtues and protect the earth.

children.text: avāyur āryairava satsutānava śriyaśca rājannava dharmamātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Protect your life with noble men; protect your good sons, your prosperity, O king, and your own <s>dharma</s>.
As a twice-born bird goes, freeing its body, in the interval marked by the arising of the enemy of snow,
so go within, freeing your mind, in the destruction of the enemy that destroys the foe of snow.
The king said, with joined hands and renewed longing, 'May you obtain your wish without hindrance.

children.text: avāpya kāle kṛtakṛtyatāmimāṃ mamāpi kāryo bhavatā tvanugrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having in time attained this fulfillment of your purpose, you must also show favor to me.'

children.text: sthiraṃ pratijñāya tatheti pārthive tataḥ sa vaiśvantaram āśramaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: After firmly promising the king, 'So be it,' he then went to the hermitage of <s>Vaiśvantara</s>.

children.text: parivrajantaṃ tamudīkṣya vismito nṛpo 'pi vavrāja puriṃ girivrajam ||
children.translated_text: And the king, astonished as he watched him going forth as a mendicant, returned to the city <s>Girivraja</s>.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye kāmavigarhaṇo nāmaikādaśaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the eleventh canto, named <s>Kāmavigarhaṇa</s>, 'Denunciation of Desires.'
Then the moon of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line approached the hermitage of the sage
<s>Arāḍa</s>, whose dwelling was tranquillity, as if filling it with his very body.
Seen from afar by that man of the <s>Kālāma</s> lineage,
and loudly addressed with 'Welcome!', he came near.
After the two of them had properly asked each other about the balance of the bodily elements,

children.text: dāravyor medhyayor vṛṣyoḥ śucau deśe niṣedatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they sat down in a clean place on two pure wooden seats.
Then that best of sages spoke to the seated son of the king,
as if drinking him in with two eyes widened by great respect:

children.text: viditaṃ me yathā saumya niṣkrānto bhavanādasi
children.translated_text: 'I know, gentle one, how you have gone forth from your home,

children.text: chittvā snehamayaṃ pāśaṃ pāśaṃ dṛpta iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having cut the noose made of affection, like a proud elephant cutting a snare.
In every respect your mind is both steadfast and wise.

children.text: yastvaṃ prāptaḥ śriyaṃ tyaktvā latāṃ viṣaphalāmiva ||
children.translated_text: You are one who, having obtained royal fortune, abandoned it like a creeper with poisonous fruit.
It is no wonder that kings of worn-out age went to the forest
after giving their royal fortune to their sons, like a garland left over after enjoyment.

children.text: idaṃ me matamāścaryaṃ nave vayasi yadbhavān
children.translated_text: What is astonishing to me is this: that in fresh youth you,
having obtained royal fortune and being within the range of sense objects, did not enjoy it at all.

children.text: tad vijñātum imaṃ dharmaṃ paramaṃ bhājanaṃ bhavān
children.translated_text: Therefore you are a supreme vessel for understanding this <s>dharma</s> (teaching).
Mount the raft of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and quickly cross the ocean of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering).

children.text: śiṣye yadyapi vijñāte śāstraṃ kālena varṇyate
children.translated_text: Although a <s>śāstra</s> is taught in time to a disciple only after he has been understood,
because of your depth and resolve, you need not be examined by me.
Having understood <s>Arāḍa</s>'s speech, that bull among men
became supremely pleased and then spoke in reply.
Even though you are dispassionate, this supreme graciousness of yours
makes me, though not yet successful, as if successful at this very moment.
For, like one wishing to see who finds a light, or one wishing to travel who finds a guide,
and like one wishing to cross who finds a raft, so I regard the sight of you.
Therefore you ought to speak that, if you think it should be spoken,
by which this person may be released from old age, death, and disease.
Thus <s>Arāḍa</s>, urged on by the very greatness of the prince,
briefly set forth the settled conclusion of his own <s>śāstra</s>.
Listen to this doctrine of ours, best of listeners,

children.text: yathā bhavati saṃsāro yathā caiva nivartate ||
children.translated_text: how <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) comes to be and how indeed it ceases.
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primary nature), <s>vikāra</s> (evolute), birth, death, and old age

children.text: tat tāvat sattvam ityuktaṃ sthirasattva parehi tat ||
children.translated_text: are, first of all, called <s>sattva</s> (being); O steadfast one, understand that.

children.text: tatra tu prakṛtiṃ nāma viddhi prakṛtikovida
children.translated_text: There, O knower of <s>prakṛti</s>, know what is named <s>prakṛti</s>:
the five elements, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-maker), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and the <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest).
Understand as <s>vikāra</s> the sense objects and the sense faculties,

children.text: pāṇipādaṃ ca vādaṃ ca pāyūpasthaṃ tathā manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hands, feet, speech, anus, generative organ, and also the mind.

children.text: asya kṣetrasya vijñānātkṣetrajña iti saṃjñi ca
children.translated_text: From the knowing of this <s>kṣetra</s> (field), one is designated <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field),
and those who reflect on the self describe the <s>ātman</s> (self) as <s>kṣetrajña</s>.
Here <s>Kapila</s> together with his disciples is remembered as <s>pratibuddha</s> (awakened),
but <s>Prajāpati</s> together with his son is here called <s>apratibuddha</s> (unawakened).

children.text: jāyate jīryate caiva bādhyate mriyate ca yat
children.translated_text: That which is born, ages, is afflicted, and dies
should be known as <s>vyakta</s> (manifest); the <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest) is the opposite.

children.text: ajñānaṃ karma tṛṣṇā ca jñeyāḥ saṃsārahetavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) should be known as the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
when a creature stands within this triad, it does not pass beyond that state of being.
It is because of <s>vipratyaya</s> (false cognition), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (egoism), doubt, and confusion,
because of non-distinction and false means, because of attachment and falling down, that it remains bound.
There <s>vipratyaya</s> is what proceeds in an inverted way:
it does an action otherwise and thinks what is to be thought in another way.
"I speak, I know, I go, I am standing"--
this is how <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (egoism) operates here in regard to what is not the self.
But when one sees undoubted things
as a single mass, like a lump of clay, O doubtless one, that is called doubt here.

children.text: ya evāhaṃ sa evedaṃ mano buddhiśca karma ca
children.translated_text: "That very I is this mind, intellect, and action,
and this aggregate itself is I"--whoever thinks so has <s>abhisaṃplava</s> (confounding).
Whoever, O knower of distinctions, knows no distinction between the awakened and the unawakened

children.text: prakṛtīnāṃ ca yo veda so 'viśeṣa iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and among the <s>prakṛtis</s> (constituents), he is remembered as having <s>aviśeṣa</s> (non-distinction).
Acts such as salutation, the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-formula, sprinkling, and aspersion
are declared by the wise, O knower of means, to be <s>anupāya</s> (no true means).
That by which a dull-witted person clings, through mind, speech, intellect, and actions,
to sense objects, O unattached one, is remembered as <s>abhiṣvaṅga</s> (attachment).
The suffering which one imagines as "this is mine" and "I belong to this"
should be known as <s>abhyavapāta</s> (downfall), by which one is cast into <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Thus the wise man understands <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as five-branched:
darkness, delusion, great delusion, and the two forms of <s>tāmisra</s> (dark passion).

children.text: tatrālasyaṃ tamo viddhi mohaṃ mṛtyuṃ ca janma ca
children.translated_text: Among these, know sloth as darkness, and birth and death as delusion;
but great delusion, O undeluded one, is to be understood simply as desire.
Because even great beings are bewildered by it here,
therefore, O mighty-armed one, it is remembered as great delusion.
They take anger itself to be <s>tāmisra</s>, O angerless one,
and they call despondency <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness), O one free from despondency.
Joined to this five-branched <s>avidyā</s>, a foolish person
is plunged into births in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is mostly suffering.

children.text: draṣṭā śrotā ca mantā ca kāryakaraṇameva ca
children.translated_text: Arriving at the thought, "I am the seer, the hearer, the thinker,
and also the product and the instrument," he revolves in <s>saṃsāra</s>.
By these causes here, wise one, the stream of birth proceeds;
from the absence of causes comes absence of result: you should understand this.
There the right-minded person who desires <s>mokṣa</s> should know the fourfold set:
the awakened and unawakened, and the manifest and unmanifest.
Having rightly known this fourfold set, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field),
leaving behind straightness and swiftness (reading uncertain), reaches the imperishable state.
For this purpose the brahmins in the world, speakers of the supreme Brahman,
practice <s>brahmacarya</s> here and have brahmins dwell with them.
Having heard these words of that sage, the king's son

children.text: abhyupāyaṃ ca papraccha padameva ca naiṣṭhikam ||
children.translated_text: asked about the means of attainment and the final state itself.

children.text: brahmacaryamidaṃ caryaṃ yathā yāvacca yatra ca
children.translated_text: How, for how long, and where this <s>brahmacarya</s> is to be practiced,
and the final limit of this <s>dharma</s> (teaching), you ought to explain.
Thus <s>Arāḍa</s>, according to the śāstra (teaching), with the meaning made clear and in brief,
explained that very dharma (path) to him in another formulation.
At the beginning, having left his home and taken on the sign of mendicancy,
he lives after adopting śīla (ethical discipline), broad in its range of practice.
Taking up supreme contentment with whatever comes, from wherever it comes,
he resorts to a secluded dwelling, free from the pairs of opposites, learned in śāstra and accomplished.

children.text: tato rāgādbhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā vairāgyācca paraṃ śivam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing danger in passion and the highest blessedness in dispassion,
he restrains the whole body of the senses and strives for the calming of the mind.

children.text: atho viviktaṃ kāmebhyo vyāpādādibhya eva ca
children.translated_text: Then, secluded from sensual desires and likewise from ill will and the rest,
he obtains the first dhyāna, born of seclusion and accompanied by vitarka (discursive thought).
And having attained the happiness of that dhyāna, continually reflecting on just that,
foolish people are carried away by the gain of an unprecedented happiness.
By such a calm as this, which condemns desire and hatred,
this person reaches <s>Brahmaloka</s>, deceived by satisfaction.
But the learned person, knowing vitarkas (thought applications) to disturb the mind,
obtains a dhyāna separated from them, endowed with joy and happiness.

children.text: hriyamāṇastayā prītyā yo viśeṣaṃ na paśyati
children.translated_text: Whoever is carried away by that joy and does not see a further distinction
reaches a radiant station among the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods.
But whoever separates the mind from that joy and happiness
obtains the third dhyāna, a happiness devoid of joy.

children.text: yastu tasminsukhe magno na viśeṣāya yatnavān
children.translated_text: But whoever is absorbed in that happiness and does not strive for a higher distinction

children.text: śubhakṛtsnaiḥ sa sāmānyaṃ sukhaṃ prāpnoti daivataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: shares that happiness with the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> deities.

children.text: tādṛśaṃ sukham āsādya yo na rajyatyupekṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached such happiness, the one who is equanimous and does not become attached
obtains the fourth dhyāna, free from pleasure and pain.
There some become settled in the belief that it is mokṣa (liberation), imagining so,
because pleasure and pain have been abandoned and because the mind has ceased from activity.

children.text: asya dhyānasya tu phalaṃ samaṃ devairbṛhatphalaiḥ
children.translated_text: But those who test with great wisdom say that the fruit of this dhyāna
is equality with the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods for a long time.
Having arisen from that samādhi (concentration), seeing the defects of embodied beings,
the wise person ascends to knowledge for the cessation of embodiment.
Then, abandoning that dhyāna and making a resolve toward a higher distinction,

children.text: kāmebhya iva sa prājño rūpādapi virajyate ||
children.translated_text: the wise one becomes dispassionate toward form, just as he had toward sensual desires.
First contemplating the openings that are in this body,
then, even in dense substances, he fixes his attention on space.
But another wise person, having gathered together the self that has gone into space,
attains a further distinction by seeing that very self as infinite.
Another, skilled in inward practice, turns the self back by the self,
and, seeing 'there is nothing at all,' is remembered as being in ākiṃcanya (nothingness).
Then, like the stalk from muñja grass, or like a bird from a cage,
the kṣetrajña (knower of the field), having escaped from the body, is called liberated.
This is that supreme brahman, without mark, fixed, and imperishable,
which the knowers of truth, the sages, call mokṣa (liberation).
Thus both the means and liberation have been shown by me to you.
If it is understood and if it pleases you, let it be undertaken as it truly is.
<s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, and the aged <s>Parāśara</s>,

children.text: imaṃ panthānamāsādya muktā hyanye ca mokṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and other seekers of liberation, having come to this path, were liberated.

children.text: iti tasya sa tadvākyaṃ gṛhītvā tu vicārya ca
children.translated_text: Thus, after receiving and considering that speech of his,
he, brought to readiness by the force of former causes, gave this reply:

children.text: śrutaṃ jñānamidaṃ sūkṣmaṃ parataḥ parataḥ śivam
children.translated_text: I have heard this subtle knowledge, more and more auspicious at each step,
but because the kṣetrajña is not abandoned, I understand it to be not final.
For although the kṣetrajña is held by you to be freed from transformations and prakṛti (material nature),
I think it still has the nature of production and indeed the nature of a seed.

children.text: viśuddho yadyapi hyātmā nirmukta iti kalpyate
children.translated_text: For even if the ātman (self) is conceived as purified and released,
because conditions will exist again, it will become unliberated.
Just as a seed does not sprout when season, soil, water, and the like are absent,
but sprouts by means of those several conditions, so too, in my view, is that self.
If mokṣa (liberation) is conceived through the abandonment of karma (action), ignorance, and thirst,
the absolute abandonment of those is not found while a real ātman (self) remains.
By abandoning these three again and again, only a distinction is perceived;
where the ātman remains, there this subtle triad also remains.
Because the faults are subtle, because the mind is inactive,
and because life is long, mokṣa is merely imagined.
And as for this abandonment of ahaṃkāra (ego-making) that is imagined,
when the ātman is real, abandonment of ahaṃkāra is not found.
And since this self, not free from number and the other qualities, does not become qualityless,
therefore, when qualitylessness is absent, mokṣa is not predicated of it.

children.text: guṇino hi guṇānāṃ ca vyatireko na vidyate
children.translated_text: For there is no separation between what possesses qualities and the qualities,
since fire without form and heat is not perceived.
Before the body there would be no embodied one, just as before qualities there would be no possessor of qualities;

children.text: tasmādādau vimuktaḥ san śarīrī badhyate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, though free at the beginning, the embodied one is bound again.

children.text: kṣetrajño viśarīraśca jño vā syādajña eva vā
children.translated_text: And the bodiless kṣetrajña would have to be either knowing or ignorant.

children.text: yadi jño jñeyamasyāsti jñeye sati na mucyate ||
children.translated_text: If it is knowing, it has something to be known; when an object of knowledge exists, it is not liberated.

children.text: athājña iti siddho vaḥ kalpitena kimātmanā
children.translated_text: But if, as you hold, it is ignorant, what use is an imagined ātman?
For even without an ātman, ignorance is well established, as in a piece of wood or a wall.
Since successive abandonment is still regarded as possessing qualities,
therefore I think complete fulfillment comes from abandoning everything.

children.text: iti dharmamarāḍasya viditvā na tutoṣa saḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, understanding <s>Arāḍa</s>'s dharma (teaching), he was not satisfied with it;
knowing it to be incomplete, he then went away.
Then, wishing to hear a more distinguished teaching, he went to the hermitage of <s>Udraka</s>.

children.text: ātmagrāhācca tasyāpi jagṛhe na sa darśanam ||
children.translated_text: But because that teaching too involved grasping at a self, he did not accept his doctrine.
For the sage <s>Udraka</s>, knowing the defect in both perception and non-perception,
had attained beyond nothingness the state consisting of neither perception nor non-perception.
Because, with a subtle object as support, beyond perception and non-perception,
one is neither non-percipient nor exactly percipient, his longing had gone there.
And because cognition remains just there, not moving on to anything else,
being subtle and weak, there is in that state neither non-percipience nor percipience.
And because the world, even after attaining that, turns back again,
the <s>bodhisattva</s>, seeking the highest, therefore abandoned <s>Udraka</s>.
Then, leaving his hermitage, resolved and intent on the highest good,
he resorted to the hermitage called <s>Nagarī</s>, belonging to the royal seer <s>Gaya</s>.
Then on the pure bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s>, he whose exertion was pure,
the sage who delighted in solitary dwelling, made his residence.
There he saw those who had come before him, uplifted by mastery over the five faculties,
five mendicants, vow-keepers, who had entered upon austerity.
And seeing him there, those mendicants, desiring liberation, attended upon him,
as sense-objects attend a lord whose wealth and health have been earned by merit.
Honored by them as they bowed low and followed him out of discipline,
by disciples remaining under his control, like the mind attended by restless senses,
he thought, 'This may be a means for bringing death and birth to an end,'
and so he began difficult austerities through fasting.
Practicing many kinds of fasting, hard for men to perform,
for six years, seeking tranquility, he made his own body emaciated.
At the times for food, with single grains of jujube, sesame, and rice,
he sustained himself, seeking the far shore of boundless <s>saṃsāra</s>.
The wasting of his body that was produced by that austerity
became all the more an increase in his splendor.
Though thin, yet with the beauty of his fame not thinned, he gladdened the eyes of others,
like the first moon of the bright fortnight in autumn gladdening the night-lotuses.
With only skin and bones remaining, all fat, flesh, and blood gone,
though wasted, he shone like the ocean, his depth undiminished.
Then the sage, his body plainly and fruitlessly afflicted by harsh austerity,
fearful of becoming and longing for Buddhahood, formed this thought:

children.text: nāyaṃ dharmo virāgāya na bodhāya na muktaye
children.translated_text: 'This <s>dharma</s> is not for dispassion, not for awakening, not for liberation.

children.text: jambumūle mayā prāpto yastadā sa vidhirdhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the method I attained then beneath the rose-apple tree is the true one.
And that cannot be attained by one who is weak.' Realizing this with renewed concern,
he reflected again for the sake of increasing the body's strength:
'Exhausted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, his mind made unsound by exertion,
how could a person, lacking ease, attain the fruit that is to be attained by the mind?
Ease is properly gained from the steady nourishment of the faculties;
when the faculties are nourished, soundness of mind is attained.
For one whose mind is sound and clear, <s>samādhi</s> arises;
for one whose mind is joined with <s>samādhi</s>, the discipline of meditation proceeds.
From the proceeding of meditation, those states are attained by which one obtains
that supreme deathless state, hard to reach, peaceful, and ageless.
Therefore this means has nourishment as its root.' Having reached that certainty,
the steadfast one formed a measured resolve about taking food.
Having bathed, he slowly climbed up from the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s>, emaciated,
as the trees on the bank, their branch-tips bent with devotion, gave him their hands.
Then the daughter of the chief cowherd, urged on by deities,
<s>Nandabalā</s>, joy arisen in her heart, came there.
Her arms were bright like white conch-shells, and she wore a dark-blue garment,
like the noble river <s>Yamunā</s>, with dark water and a garland of foam.
She, her joy increased by faith and the lotuses of her eyes opening,
bowed with her head and caused him to accept milk-rice.
By partaking of it, he made her one who had obtained the fruit of her birth;
with his six faculties nourished, he became capable of attaining awakening.
And the sage, his body fully refreshed, together with his own glory,
alone bore the radiance and steadiness of both the moon and the ocean.

children.text: āvṛtta iti vijñāya taṃ jahuḥ pañca bhikṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'He has turned back,' the five mendicants abandoned him,
as the five elements leave the self of a liberated sage.
Then, with resolve as his only companion, over ground spread with tender grass,
he went to the root of an <s>aśvattha</s> tree, firmly resolved on awakening.
Then at that time, awakened by the incomparable sound of his footstep, like the stride of an elephant-king,
<s>Kāla</s>, the foremost serpent, knowing that the great sage had come resolved on awakening, spoke a praise.
'O sage, since the earth, pressed by your feet, seems to rumble again and again,

children.text: yathā ca te rājati sūryavatprabhā dhruvaṃ tvamiṣṭaṃ phalamadya bhokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: and since your radiance shines like the sun, surely today you will enjoy the desired fruit.

children.text: yathā bhramantyo divi cāṣapaṅktayaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tvāṃ kamalākṣa kurvate
children.translated_text: Since lines of <s>cāṣa</s> birds, circling in the sky, make a clockwise circuit around you, lotus-eyed one,

children.text: yathā ca saumyā divi vānti vāyavastvamadya buddho niyataṃ bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and since gentle winds blow in the sky, today you will certainly become a Buddha.'
Then, praised by the foremost serpent, he took pure grasses from a grass-cutter,
and, having made his vow, sat down for awakening, taking refuge at the root of the pure great tree.
Then he assumed the supreme, unshakable cross-legged posture, compact like the coil of a sleeping serpent.

children.text: bhinadmi tāvadbhuvi naitadāsanaṃ na yāmi yāvat kṛtakṛtyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall break this seat upon the earth before I go; I will not leave until I have become one who has accomplished what had to be done.'

children.text: tato yayur mudamatulāṃ divaukaso vavāśire na mṛgagaṇā na pakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the dwellers in heaven went to incomparable joy; the herds of deer and the birds did not cry out,
and the forest trees, though struck by the wind, made no sound, when the Blessed One had taken his seat, fixed in resolve.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'rāḍadarśano nāma dvādaśaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, the twelfth canto, named 'The Seeing of <s>Arāḍa</s>.'
When that great seer, sprung from the line of royal seers, had made his vow for liberation,
and had sat down there, the world rejoiced there; but <s>Māra</s>, the enemy of the true <s>dharma</s> (teaching), was afraid.

children.text: yaṃ kāmadevaṃ pravadanti loke citrāyudhaṃ puṣpaśaraṃ tathaiva
children.translated_text: He whom in the world they call <s>Kāmadeva</s>, the brightly armed one, and likewise the flower-arrowed one,
that very lord over the course of desire, the hater of liberation, they call <s>Māra</s>.
His sons, <s>Vibhrama</s>, <s>Harṣa</s>, and <s>Darpa</s>, and his three daughters, <s>Arati</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, and <s>Tṛṣā</s>,

children.text: papracchurenaṃ manaso vikāraṃ sa tāṃśca tāścaiva vaco 'bhyuvāca ||
children.translated_text: asked him about the disturbance of his mind, and he spoke these words to those sons and those daughters.
'That sage sits there, wearing resolve as armor, drawing the arrow of insight upon the weapon of firmness,
wishing to conquer my sense-realms; therefore there is this despondency in my mind.

children.text: yadi hyasau māmabhibhūya yāti lokāya cākhyātyapavargamārgam
children.translated_text: For if he overcomes me and goes on to proclaim to the world the path of release,
then this domain of mine today will be empty, like that of the lord of <s>Videha</s> when he had fallen from his proper course.

children.text: tadyāvadevaiṣa na labdhacakṣur madgocare tiṣṭhati yāvadeva
children.translated_text: Therefore, while this man has not yet obtained sight, and so long as he still remains within my range,

children.text: yāsyāmi tāvadvratamasya bhettuṃ setuṃ nadīvega ivātivṛddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall go at once to break his vow, like an over-swollen river-current breaking a bridge.'

children.text: tato dhanuḥ puṣpamayaṃ gṛhītvā śarān jaganmohakarāṃśca pañca
children.translated_text: Then, taking up a bow made of flowers and five arrows that bewilder the world,
he went with his sons to the root of the aśvattha tree, the maker of unease in the minds of creatures.

children.text: atha praśāntaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pāraṃ titīrṣuṃ bhavasāgarasya
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the tranquil sage seated, wishing to cross to the far shore of the ocean of becoming,

children.text: viṣajya savyaṃ karamāyudhāgre krīḍan śareṇedamuvāca māraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, placing his left hand on the tip of his weapon and toying with an arrow, said this:

children.text: uttiṣṭha bhoḥ kṣatriya mṛtyubhīta cara svadharmaṃ tyaja mokṣadharmam
children.translated_text: 'Rise, kṣatriya, afraid of death. Follow your own <s>dharma</s> (duty); abandon the <s>dharma</s> of liberation.

children.text: bāṇaiśca yajñaiśca vinīya lokaṃ lokātpadaṃ prāpnuhi vāsavasya ||
children.translated_text: Subduing the world with arrows and sacrifices, win from the world the station of <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: panthā hi niryātum ayaṃ yaśasyo yo vāhitaḥ pūrvatamairnarendraiḥ
children.translated_text: For this is the glorious path for going forth, the one followed by the earliest kings;

children.text: jātasya rājarṣikule viśāle bhaikṣākam aślāghyamidaṃ prapattum ||
children.translated_text: for one born in a great family of royal seers, this recourse to begging is not praiseworthy.

children.text: athādya nottiṣṭhasi niścitātman bhava sthiro mā vimucaḥ pratijñām
children.translated_text: But if today, firm-minded one, you do not rise, then be steadfast; do not release your vow.

children.text: mayodyato hyeṣa śaraḥ sa eva yaḥ śūrpake mīnaripau vimuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For raised by me is that very arrow which was once released against <s>Śūrpaka</s>, the enemy of <s>Mīna</s>.

children.text: spṛṣṭaḥ sa cānena kathaṃcidaiḍaḥ somasya naptāpyabhavadvicittaḥ
children.translated_text: Touched by this arrow in some way, even <s>Aiḍa</s>, the grandson of <s>Soma</s>, became distraught,

children.text: sa cābhavacchantanurasvatantraḥ kṣīṇe yuge kiṃ bata durbalo 'nyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śantanu</s> too became no longer master of himself; in a declining age, how much less could some other weak man resist?

children.text: tatkṣipramuttiṣṭha labhasva saṃjñāṃ bāṇo hyayaṃ tiṣṭhati lelihānaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore rise quickly and regain awareness, for this arrow stands here licking its lips,
the arrow that I do not loose at those who obey their beloveds and love passion, just as I do not loose it at cakravāka birds.'
When, though addressed in this way, the unconcerned <s>Śākyamuni</s> did not break his seat,

children.text: śaraṃ tato 'smai visasarja māraḥ kanyāśca kṛtvā purataḥ sutāṃśca ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Māra</s> discharged the arrow at him, setting his daughters and sons before him.

children.text: tasmiṃstu bāṇe 'pi sa vipramukte cakāra nāsthāṃ na dhṛteścacāla
children.translated_text: But even when that arrow had been released against him, he paid it no regard and did not waver from his firmness.
Seeing him thus, <s>Māra</s> sank into despondency and, overcome with thought, slowly said:

children.text: śailendraputrīṃ prati yena viddho devo 'pi śambhuścalito babhūva
children.translated_text: 'Even the god <s>Śambhu</s>, pierced by this arrow toward the daughter of the lord of mountains, became shaken.

children.text: na cintayatyeṣa tameva bāṇaṃ kiṃ syādacitto na śaraḥ sa eṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This man does not even think of that same arrow. Could he be without a mind, or is this not that arrow?

children.text: tasmādayaṃ nārhati puṣpabāṇaṃ na harṣaṇaṃ nāpi raterniyogam
children.translated_text: Therefore this man does not deserve the flower-arrow, nor gladdening, nor any command of passion.
This man deserves terrors, threats, and blows from grim hosts of spirits.'

children.text: sasmāra māraśca tataḥ svasainyaṃ vighnaṃ śame śākyamuneścikīrṣan
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> summoned his own army, wishing to make an obstacle to <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s peace,
and followers of many kinds came around, with stakes, trees, spears, maces, and swords in their hands.
They had faces of boars, fish, horses, donkeys, and camels, and faces of tigers, bears, lions, and elephants;
they were one-eyed, many-faced, three-headed, pot-bellied, and hollow-bellied.
Some had strange thighs and pot-like knees; some were armed with tusks and armed with claws;
some had skull-like faces and many forms, some half-broken faces and great mouths.
They were ash-red, variegated with drops of blood, carrying skull-staffs, with tawny and smoky hair;
with dangling garlands and elephant-like hanging ears, dressed in hides and also naked.
Some had half-white faces and half-green bodies; they were coppery, smoky, tawny, and black;
their shoulders and arms were wrapped with serpents, and their girdles were crowded with loudly ringing bells.
Some were as tall as palm trees and held tridents; others were terrible with tusks and only the size of children;
some had ram-faces and bird-eyes, and some had cat-faces and human bodies.
They had disheveled hair, crests, half-shaven heads, red garments, and confused wrappings;
with delighted faces and frowning faces, some robbing radiance and others captivating the mind.

children.text: kecidvrajanto bhṛśam āvavalgur anyonyam āpupluvire tathānye
children.translated_text: Some, as they advanced, leapt about violently; others leapt upon one another.
Some played as they moved through the sky, and some roamed on the tops of trees.

children.text: nanarta kaścidbhramayaṃstriśūlaṃ kaścid vipusphūrja gadāṃ vikarṣan
children.translated_text: One danced while whirling a trident; another thundered as he dragged along a mace;
one bellowed with joy like a bull, and another blazed forth from the hairs of his body.
Groups of beings of this kind stood all around, encircling that root of the <s>bodhi</s> tree,
wishing both to seize him and to kill him, carrying out the command of their master.

children.text: taṃ prekṣya mārasya ca pūrvarātre śākyarṣabhasyaiva ca yuddhakālam
children.translated_text: Seeing that, in the first watch of the night, the time had come for battle between <s>Māra</s> and the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: na dyauścakāśe pṛthivī cakampe prajajvaluścaiva diśaḥ saśabdāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sky did not shine, the earth trembled, and the quarters blazed up with sound.

children.text: viṣvag vavau vāyurudīrṇavegastārā na rejurna babhau śaśāṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: The wind blew everywhere with violent speed; the stars did not glitter, and the moon did not shine.

children.text: tamaśca bhūyo vitatāna rātriḥ sarve ca saṃcukṣubhire samudrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Night spread still greater darkness, and all the oceans were thrown into turmoil.
The mountains and the <s>nāgas</s> devoted to <s>dharma</s>, unable to endure an obstruction to the Great Sage,

children.text: māraṃ prati krodhavivṛttanetrā niḥśaśvasuścaiva jajṛmbhire ca ||
children.translated_text: rolled their eyes in anger toward <s>Māra</s>, and they breathed out and opened their mouths wide.
But the divine seers of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> heavens, engaged for the accomplishment of the true <s>dharma</s>,
felt compassion in their minds for <s>Māra</s>; because of their dispassionate state, they did not fall into anger.

children.text: tadbodhimūlaṃ samavekṣya kīrṇaṃ hiṃsātmanā mārabalena tena
children.translated_text: When they saw that root of the <s>bodhi</s> tree covered by that violent army of <s>Māra</s>,
a cry of lamentation arose in the sky from those whose nature was <s>dharma</s> and who desired the liberation of the world.

children.text: upaplavaṃ dharmavidhestu tasya dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ mārabalaṃ maharṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Māra</s>'s army standing there as a disturbance to that course of <s>dharma</s>, the Great Seer

children.text: na cukṣubhe nāpi yayau vikāraṃ madhye gavāṃ siṃha ivopaviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was not shaken and underwent no change, sitting like a lion among cows.

children.text: mārastato bhūtacamūm udīrṇām ājñāpayāmāsa bhayāya tasya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> commanded his swollen army of beings to terrify him,

children.text: svaiḥ svaiḥ prabhāvairatha sāsya senā taddhairyabhedāya matiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: and his army, each by its own powers, set its mind on breaking his steadfastness.
Some had many dangling tongues that flickered, fangs sharp at the tips, and yellow-ringed eyes;

children.text: vidāritāsyāḥ sthiraśaṅkukarṇāḥ saṃtrāsayantaḥ kila nāma tasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: with mouths split open and ears like fixed spikes, they stood there as if terrifying him.

children.text: tebhyaḥ sthitebhyaḥ sa tathāvidhebhyaḥ rūpeṇa bhāvena ca dāruṇebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: At them as they stood in such a way, dreadful in form and disposition,

children.text: na vivyathe nodvivije maharṣiḥ krīḍatsubālebhya ivoddhatebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Great Sage did not tremble or grow alarmed, as if they were unruly children at play.
Then one, his gaze twisted by anger, raised a mace against him;

children.text: tastambha bāhuḥ sagadastato 'sya puraṃdarasyeva purā savajraḥ ||
children.translated_text: thereupon his arm, together with the mace, became rigid, like <s>Purandara</s>'s arm long ago together with the thunderbolt.

children.text: kecitsamudyamya śilāstarūṃśca viṣehire naiva munau vimoktum
children.translated_text: Some lifted rocks and trees, but were not able to hurl them at the sage;

children.text: petuḥ savṛkṣāḥ saśilāstathaiva vajrāvabhagnā iva vindhyapādāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they fell together with the trees and rocks, like the slopes of <s>Vindhya</s> shattered by a thunderbolt.

children.text: kaiścitsamutpatya nabho vimuktāḥ śilāśca vṛkṣāśca paraśvadhāśca
children.translated_text: Rocks, trees, and axes, hurled into the sky by some after they had leapt up,

children.text: tasthurnabhasyeva na cāvapetuḥ saṃdhyābhrapādā iva naikavarṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: remained in the sky itself and did not fall, like many-colored banks of twilight cloud.
Another hurled above him a blazing mass as large as a mountain peak;
as soon as it was released, while still in the sky, it split into a hundred pieces through his power.
Someone else, blazing in the sky like the risen sun, poured out a great shower of embers,
like <s>Meru</s> blazing at the end of an aeon and scattering dust from its golden caves.

children.text: tad bodhimūle pravikīryamāṇam aṅgāravarṣaṃ tu savisphuliṅgam
children.translated_text: But that shower of embers, with sparks, as it was scattered at the root of the <s>bodhi</s> tree,
became a shower of red lotus petals through the supreme seer's dwelling in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).
Though such scorching afflictions of body and mind were hurled down upon him,
<s>Śākyamuni</s> did not move at all from his seat, embracing his firm resolve like a kinsman.

children.text: athāpare nirjigilur mukhebhyaḥ sarpān vijīrṇebhya iva drumebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then others spewed snakes from their mouths, as if from decayed trees;

children.text: te mantrabaddhā iva tatsamīpe na śaśvasurnotsasṛpurna celuḥ ||
children.translated_text: near him those snakes, as if bound by a mantra, neither hissed, nor crawled away, nor moved.
Others became great clouds, with lightning and fierce thunderous crashes,
and released a shower of stones upon that tree; it became a beautiful shower of flowers.

children.text: cāpe 'tha bāṇo nihito 'pareṇa jajvāla tatraiva na niṣpapāta
children.translated_text: Then an arrow set on a bow by another blazed right there and did not fly,
like the anger of an uncontrolled, intolerant man smoldering within himself.

children.text: pañceṣavo 'nyena tu vipramuktāstasthurnabhasyeva munau na petuḥ
children.translated_text: Five arrows shot by another remained in the sky itself and did not fall upon the sage,
like the five senses of a discerning man afraid of <s>saṃsāra</s> when they turn toward sense objects.

children.text: jighāṃsayānyaḥ prasasāra ruṣṭo gadāṃ gṛhītvābhimukho maharṣeḥ
children.translated_text: Another, angry and intent on killing, advanced toward the Great Seer with mace in hand;
his desire unfulfilled, he fell helpless, like the world among faults that bring misfortune.

children.text: strī meghakālī tu kapālahastā kartuṃ maharṣeḥ kila cittamoham
children.translated_text: But the woman <s>Meghakālī</s>, skull in hand, seeking, it is said, to bewilder the Great Sage's mind,

children.text: babhrāma tatrāniyataṃ na tasthau calātmano buddhirivāgameṣu ||
children.translated_text: wandered there restlessly and did not stand still, like the intellect of an unsteady person among doctrines.
Someone fixed a blazing eye on him, wishing to burn him with the fire of his eye like a venomous serpent,

children.text: tatraiva nāsīnamṛṣiṃ dadarśa kāmātmakaḥ śreya ivopadiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: but right there he did not see the seated seer, like a sensual man failing to see the good even when it is taught.

children.text: gurvīṃ śilām udyamayaṃstathānyaḥ śaśrāma moghaṃ vihataprayatnaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise another, lifting a heavy rock, grew weary in vain, his effort thwarted,
like someone wishing to attain, through bodily hardship, the <s>dharma</s> of final good that is reached by knowledge and <s>samādhi</s>.
Others, taking the forms of hyenas and lions, roared aloud with great roars,

children.text: sattvāni yaiḥ saṃcukucuḥ samantādvajrāhatā dyauḥ phalatīti matvā ||
children.translated_text: at which creatures everywhere shrank back, thinking, 'The sky, struck by a thunderbolt, is splitting.'

children.text: mṛgā gajāścārtaravān sṛjanto vidudruvuścaiva nililyire ca
children.translated_text: Deer and elephants, uttering cries of distress, ran away and hid;

children.text: rātrau ca tasyāmahanīva digbhyaḥ khagā ruvantaḥ paripeturārtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and on that night, as if it were day, birds flew about from the quarters, crying in distress.

children.text: teṣāṃ praṇādaistu tathāvidhaistaiḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣvapi kampiteṣu
children.translated_text: But though all beings trembled at those roars of theirs, such as they were,

children.text: munirna tatrāsa na saṃcukoca ravairgarutmāniva vāyasānām ||
children.translated_text: the Sage was not frightened and did not shrink back, like <s>Garutmān</s> at the cries of crows.

children.text: bhayāvahebhyaḥ pariṣadgaṇebhyo yathā yathā naiva munirbibhāya
children.translated_text: In just the measure that the sage did not fear the terrifying hosts of assemblies,

children.text: tathā tathā dharmabhṛtāṃ sapatnaḥ śokācca roṣācca sasāda māraḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that same measure <s>Māra</s>, foe of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>, sank down from grief and anger.
Then a certain being, visible in form, a distinguished being, remaining in the sky,

children.text: dṛṣṭvarṣaye drugdham avairaruṣṭaṃ māraṃ babhāṣe mahatā svareṇa ||
children.translated_text: saw <s>Māra</s> hostile to the seer, and, without hostility or anger, addressed him in a great voice.

children.text: moghaṃ śramaṃ nārhasi māra kartuṃ hiṃsrātmatāmutsṛja gaccha śarma
children.translated_text: You should not undertake futile exertion, <s>Māra</s>; abandon your violent nature and go to peace.

children.text: naiṣa tvayā kampayituṃ hi śakyo mahāgirirmerurivānilena ||
children.translated_text: For he cannot be shaken by you, as the great mountain <s>Meru</s> cannot be shaken by the wind.

children.text: apyuṣṇabhāvaṃ jvalanaḥ prajahyādāpo dravatvaṃ pṛthivī sthiratvam
children.translated_text: Fire might even abandon its heat, waters their liquidity, and earth its steadiness,
but this man, whose meritorious deeds have been accumulated through many kalpas, would never abandon his resolve.

children.text: yo niścayo hyasya parākramaśca tejaśca yadyā ca dayā prajāsu
children.translated_text: For such is his determination, his valor, his brilliance, and his compassion for creatures,
that he will not rise without attaining reality, as the thousand-rayed sun does not rise without destroying darkness.

children.text: kāṣṭhaṃ hi mathnan labhate hutāśaṃ bhūmiṃ khananvindati cāpi toyam
children.translated_text: For one who rubs wood obtains fire, and one who digs the earth also finds water.

children.text: nirbandhinaḥ kiṃcana nāstyasādhyaṃ nyāyena yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ ca sarvam ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing unattainable for one who persists, when everything is joined with method and put into action.
Therefore, having compassion for the world that is afflicted and caught in diseases beginning with passion,
this great physician, laboring for the medicine of knowledge, does not deserve obstruction.

children.text: hṛte ca loke bahubhiḥ kumārgaiḥ sanmārgamanvicchati yaḥ śrameṇa
children.translated_text: And when the world has been carried off by many false paths, he seeks the true path with effort;

children.text: sa daiśikaḥ kṣobhayituṃ na yuktaṃ sudeśikaḥ sārtha iva pranaṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: that guide should not be disturbed, like a good guide when a caravan has lost its way.

children.text: sattveṣu naṣṭeṣu mahāndhakāre jñānapradīpaḥ kriyamāṇa eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: When beings are lost in great darkness, this lamp of knowledge is now being made,

children.text: āryasya nirvāpayituṃ na sādhu prajvālyamānastamasīva dīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and it is not right, noble one, to extinguish it, like a lamp being kindled in the dark.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsāramaye mahaughe magnaṃ jagatpāramavindamānam
children.translated_text: Seeing the world sunk in the great flood consisting of <s>saṃsāra</s>, unable to find the far shore,
he has set out to carry it across; what noble person would even think of doing him harm?
With patience as its rootlet, deeply rooted in firmness, with conduct as its flowers and mindfulness and intelligence as its branches,
this tree of knowledge, bestowing the fruit of <s>dharma</s>, does not deserve to be uprooted while it is growing.

children.text: baddhāṃ dṛḍhaiścetasi mohapāśairyasya prajāṃ mokṣayituṃ manīṣā
children.translated_text: His intention is to free creatures who are bound fast in mind by the nooses of delusion;

children.text: tasmin jighāṃsā tava nopapannā śrānte jagadbandhanamokṣahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: toward him, exhausted for the sake of releasing the world's bondage, your wish to kill is not fitting.

children.text: bodhāya karmāṇi hi yānyanena kṛtāni teṣāṃ niyato 'dya kālaḥ
children.translated_text: For the deeds that he has performed for awakening have their appointed time today.

children.text: sthāne tathāsminnupaviṣṭa eṣa yathaiva pūrve munayastathaiva ||
children.translated_text: He sits here in this place just as the former sages did.

children.text: eṣā hi nābhirvasudhātalasya kṛtsnena yuktā parameṇa dhāmnā
children.translated_text: For this is the navel of the surface of the earth, joined with supreme power in its entirety;

children.text: bhūmerato 'nyo 'sti hi na pradeśo vegaṃ samādherviṣaheta yo 'sya ||
children.translated_text: there is no other place on earth that could bear the force of his <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: tanmā kṛthāḥ śokamupehi śāntiṃ mā bhūnmahimnā tava māra mānaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore do not grieve; come to peace. Let there be no pride in your greatness, <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: viśrambhituṃ na kṣamam adhruvā śrīścale pade vismayamabhyupaiṣi ||
children.translated_text: Unstable splendor is not to be trusted; you are taking wonder in an unsteady position.

children.text: tataḥ sa saṃśrutya ca tasya tadvaco mahāmuneḥ prekṣya ca niṣprakampatām
children.translated_text: Then, having heard those words of his and seen the great sage's immovability,

children.text: jagāma māro vimano hatodyamaḥ śarairjagaccetasi yairvihanyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> went away dejected, his effort broken, with the arrows by which the world's mind is pierced.
Its delight gone, its labor made fruitless, its stones, thickets, and trees hurled away,

children.text: diśaḥ pradudrāva tato 'sya sā camūrhatāśrayeva dviṣatā dviṣaccamūḥ ||
children.translated_text: that army of his then fled in all directions, like a hostile army whose support has been struck down by enemies.

children.text: dravati saparipakṣe nirjite puṣpaketau jayati jitatamaske nīrajaske maharṣau
children.translated_text: As <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, together with his faction, fled defeated, and as the stainless great seer, who had conquered darkness, was victorious,

children.text: yuvatiriva sahāsā dyauścakāśe sacandrā surabhi ca jalagarbhaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ||
children.translated_text: the sky, moonlit, shone like a young woman with a smile, and a fragrant, water-laden shower of flowers fell.

children.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'śvaghoṣakṛte māravijayo nāma trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s> composed by <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>, the thirteenth canto, named 'The Defeat of <s>Māra</s>'.

children.text: tato mārabalaṃ jitvā dhairyeṇa ca śamena ca
children.translated_text: Then, after conquering <s>Māra</s>'s army by steadfastness and tranquillity,
he, skilled in <s>dhyāna</s> and wishing to know the highest truth, meditated.
Having attained the highest mastery over all the methods of <s>dhyāna</s>,
in the first watch of the night he remembered the succession of his former births.
'There I was named this; fallen from there, I came here';
in this way he remembered thousands of births, as if living through them again.

children.text: smṛtvā janma ca mṛtyuṃ ca tāsu tāsūpapattiṣu
children.translated_text: Remembering birth and death in each of those rebirths,
he, compassionate by nature, then directed compassion toward living beings.
Having abandoned one's own people here and then performing actions elsewhere,
this world, truly without refuge, goes round like a wheel.
As he, self-controlled, remembered in this way,
there arose in him the certainty that <s>saṃsāra</s> is without essence, like the core of a plantain tree.
But when the second watch arrived, he of unrivaled valor,

children.text: divyaṃ lebhe paraṃ cakṣuḥ sarvacakṣuṣmatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of all who possess sight, obtained the supreme divine eye.
Then with that divine, perfectly purified eye,
he saw the whole world as if in a spotless mirror.
As he saw beings whose actions were low or exalted,
their passing away and their rebirth, his compassionate nature grew stronger.
'These creatures, whose deeds are evil, go to a bad destiny;
these others, whose deeds are wholesome, take their place in <s>tripiṣṭapa</s> (heaven).'
'Born in a terrifying <s>naraka</s> (hell), exceedingly dreadful,
these wretched ones are tormented by sufferings of many kinds. Alas!'
Some are made to drink boiling molten iron, colored like fire;
others, crying out, are set upon a red-hot iron pillar.
Some, head downward, are cooked like meal in iron cauldrons.
Some are pitiably burned amid blazing heaps of coals.
Some are devoured by fierce dogs with sharp iron fangs,
and some by bold crows, iron-beaked as though made of iron.
Some, exhausted by burning and longing for cool shade,
enter this dark forest of sword-leaves as if they were bound.
Some, their arms bound, are split like wood with axes;
even in pain they do not die, their lives held fast by their actions.
The act that was done in the thought, 'May there be happiness,' for the removal of suffering,
has this as its fruit: helplessly, only suffering is experienced.
Having done evil for the sake of happiness, these beings are terribly afflicted;
what happiness, even the slightest, does the relish of that act bring them?
The defiled action that was done laughingly by people of defiled nature
is experienced by them, crying out, when its time has ripened.
If evildoers could see the fruit of actions in this way,
they would vomit hot blood, as if struck in their vital spots.
These others, miserable creatures, through various actions born from movements of the mind,
have arisen in the varied womb of animal birth.
There, for the sake of flesh, hide, hair, and teeth, whether from enmity or from pride,
they are pitifully killed even while their own kin look on.
Though powerless and unable to resist, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and weariness,
they become cattle and horses and are made to pull, their bodies wounded by goads.
They become elephants too and, though stronger, are driven by the weak;
their heads are tormented by hooks, and they are beaten with feet and heels.
There, although other sufferings exist as well, suffering is especially acute
because of mutual hostility and because of subjection to others.
Those in the sky are oppressed by sky-dwellers, and those in the water by water-roamers;
those on land are oppressed by land-dwellers, and, when they meet, by one another.
Likewise these beings, their minds overcome by miserliness,
have arisen in the lightless realm of the departed and pitiably consume their fruit.
With mouths like needle-holes and bellies like mountains,
these sharers in suffering are afflicted by pains born of hunger and thirst.
Overcome by longing and kept alive by their own actions,
they cannot obtain even cast-off, impure things to eat.
If a person knew such a fruit of miserliness,
he would by all means give, like <s>Śibi</s>, even the limbs of his own body.
These other creatures, in the impure pool called the womb, resembling hell,
are born among human beings and come to suffering.
